en: The 500-century windows of the miners.
The ancient Roman Arebrigium among the vineyards of the Enfer, with two medieval villages side by side, Arvier and Leverogne, and four castles.
The view of the Alps.

Block of rusty-coloured trachyte about 4 meters high, detached from Mount Castellazzu and shaped by the atmospheric agents in the form of a seated elephant, originally called "sa pedra pertunta" (the pertunta pedar). It houses two domus de janas excavated probably in the final Neolithic (3200-2800 BC); in the lower tomb are sculpted two bovine protomes. Since 2025 it is among the prenuragic necropolis Sardinian Heritage of Humanity.

Noble village of Vallagarina on the banks of the Adige, linked to the Counts Lodron: around Piazza Riolfatti the church of the Assunta, between the most beautiful Baroque monuments of Trentino, and the Free Palaces (Diocesan Museum), Guerrieri Gonzaga and Camelli; in the hamlets the flosser of Piazzo, the castle of Castellano and, higher up, the lake of Cei.

You enter from three gates: Porta Luce to the west, with the coat of arms and inscription that recalls the elevation to the city in 1793, Porta Nuova to the north, surmounted by the statue of St. Peter, and Porta Cappuccini to the east, restored in 1803. Inside, streets with original basolato, baroque palaces with portals and eighteenth-century balconies, churches and convents from the late fifteenth to the eighteenth century, the Seat of Via Vittorio Emanuele II with the oldest version of the city coat of arms, Palazzo Orsini today seat of the municipality and the lamp called "la pupa" (the pupa). Italia.it recommends the walk especially in the evening; in a pastry shop in the center was born the pastry.
The great Italian painting.

The main church of the village, destroyed by the artillery of Charles VIII in 1495 and rebuilt in the 16th century with a Latin cross on a design of the Bramantesque school; it has a bronze portal by Tommaso Gismondi and houses the wooden statue of the Madonna del Suffragio, about two meters high, of Flemish school, donated by Pope Urban VIII in 1632. On the same square Marconi stands the Town Hall with the council room.
Gothic church of 1399 in Piazza Città, born with the hospital: the oldest preserved church of Vipiteno, sober outside and frescoed inside by Giovanni da Brunico.
The city's most photographed secret. Nearby there are also the views of Via Oberdan and Via Malcontenti.

The castle and tower were erected around 860 by the Longobard king Rodoaldo near the bridge over the Liri, which dominated already in the IX century; the high walls that surrounded the village are visible for about 300 meters, with the Porta Santo Stefano in the homonymous district.
The short ride between sandstone steps and vineyards.
An excursion of about two and a half hours from Cadine through meadows, military remains of the First World War and panorama of the Adige valley.
Stone houses and alleys under the castle.
The Pelosa symbol.
The King's escape stage in 1943.
after the earthquake of 2016 the museums are partially usable (Let's Marche); card of the Park not updated (cita festa 2012-2014)

Piazzas, fountains and aristocratic buildings testify to the prosperity of the village between the Middle Ages and the modern era: the eighteenth-century Palomba and Doria palaces, the nineteenth-century Palazzo Labella and the Arch of the Piazza, medieval gate of the village; in the square dedicated to him the bronze monument to the lawyer Emanuele Gianturco. Historical districts have names such as Serritiello and Lavanga.
A density of nuraghi among the highest on the island.
The Roman theatre with views of the hills.
The history of wine and vermouth.
In the headquarters of the Confraternity of the Holy Trinity and of San Bernardino, ancient stop of pilgrims, works of John of Paul and Giuliano Traballesi and a reliquary of San Bernardino.

opening on request (tel. 0776 639327)
Pieve with origins in the 8th century, in the village of San Pancrazio.

Next to the abbey, with a large courtyard over a rustic portal and stone tower with arched windows; of the thirteenth century, it was home to the Knights of Calatrava, who came from Spain, and from 1563 residence of the Guevara feudataries.
The nineteenth-century garden.
Fortified mill moved by the waters of the Potenza river, with three millstones of which one original.
The industrial archaeology of Monteneve mines.

Founded in 1995 for public works of art and donations, it is located in a late-liberty palace of 1922-1923 on the promenade square and houses in two temporary exhibitions of modern and contemporary art; admission to free exhibitions.
The entrance door to the old town, dominated by the Rocca Albornoz of 1354; after Porta Fiorentina you enter the medieval Viterbo of Via Cavour.

Made to be built between 1330 and 1380 by the Valperga, higher than the round tower of rivals and a short distance from it: it is one of the towers of discord born from the struggles between the local lords. In 1469 he passed to the municipality, which used it as a watchtower and then placed the civic bell and the clock.

The route starts from Piazza della Repubblica, where the mother church of San Canio was demolished in 1883, and passes through the stone portals of Palazzo Rinaldi (today library) and Palazzo Zampaglione, the Arch of Zampaglione with its mask, Palazzo Berrilli with the clock stopped from 23 November 1980, the alley San Nicola, the narrowest of the village, and the loggettes of Via Alfonso del Re. From the steps of Via dell'Arco di Zampaglione you can see Mount Calvario with the church of Santa Lucia.

The centre of the Trompia Valley is linked to the arms museum in Villa Mutti Bernardelli; among the places of art are the basilica and the fifteenth-century convent of Santa Maria degli Angeli, Palazzo Chinelli-Rampinelli, the parish church of San Giorgio and the panoramic sanctuaries, and paths to Punta Almana and Santa Maria del Giogo.

Country of Valsesia with the large 18th century parish church of San Giacomo Maggiore, designed by Guarino Guarini, revised by Filippo Juvarra, the parish museum and the Art Path with fifteen chapels towards Cangello.

Park established in 1990 as a natural archaeological regional park of the rock churches of Materano: caves of the Paleolithic like the Grotto of the Bats, Neolithic villages of Murgecchia, Murgia Timone and Trasanello, masserie, jazzi and about 150 rock churches; symbol of the park is the hawk cricket.
The lake and the path along the Ledra canal in the Gemona plain, between the Tagliamento and the mountains Cuarnan and Cjampon.
The village on the hill of the Vallo di Diano.

The center brings together the Town Hall, designed after 1750 by the Rimini Gianfrancesco Buonamici, the Doge's Palace (already Malatestano, then Ginevri-Latoni) and numerous noble palaces, including Mattei-Baldini, Badalucchi, Guazzugli-Gabrielli, Caverni, Giannini (now Buschi), Ruffini and Cini. In August squares and streets host the reenactment of Medieval Pergola, with the palio among the districts.
Free outdoor course; some paid spaces
A break in the shade between museums.
residence reserved for the owners; the landing place by Carloforte or Portoscuso requires the permission of the condominium that manages the marina
The daily life of a noble family inside the castle.
The oldest church on the island.

It occupies part of the Dominican monastery built between 1394 and 1414 on the initiative of Sveva Sanseverino, inhabited by the Dominicans until 1809; the cloister contains medieval frescoes. It collects the civic archaeological collection expanded by the founder Raffaele Marrocco, the lapidary room and the Bibliotheca Scriptorum loci (since 1953), the exhibition on the Sanniti ...Gens fortissima Italiae ... (2014) and, on the first floor, an exhibition from the Risorgimento to the Second World War; it was reopened on 16 June 2013.
the MiC card indicates closed every day, with opening on the occasion of the patron celebrations: check with the Municipality
Roccaro with the eighteenth-century chapel of Our Lady Immaculate from the Baroque altar; Poggio developed around a tower along two perpendicular axes.
Dedicated to the Madonna delle Grazie, a place of pilgrimage with the Way of the Cross with pylons arranged in a triangle upstream, a small imitation of the Sacred Mount of Varallo.
Understand the delta before exploring it.
MiC card reports "Closed" every day of the week (card updated to 2020)
The ruins on the highest point of the village.
One of the Etruscan necropolis around Tuscania, from which come many finds of the archaeological museum.
The countryside of Lower Lodigiana by bicycle.

The old town, on a hill overlooking the Fortore valley and the Lake of Occhito, is made of narrow alleys, arches and steep stairs. Next to the castle stands the parish church of San Bartolomeo Apostolo, consecrated in 1696 by Cardinal Orsini, archbishop of Benevento; the church of San Nicola, of the 14th-XV century, is decorated with remarkable canvases.
The cathedral of the city, on the square of the same name, indicated by the Abruzzo Region among the main stages.
The lake reserve.

It rises on the ancient parish church of San Pietro d'Ico, around which the village grew since 1235, preserves the Romanesque structure with Gothic windows and internal basilica rebuilt in the eighteenth century; it preserves the icon of the Madonna delle Grazie, the Immaculate of Raffaellino del Colle and a San Carlo Borromeo by Giovan Francesco Guerrieri.

It dominates the village and shows construction phases of different eras, with a tower, a body added over time and a loggia; the Park signals the castled palace with Gothic arched door and saracinesca. Castelvecchio was a fief of the Counts of Celano between the 13th and 15th centuries, then from 1484 of the Piccolomini, then of the Colonna, of the Pietropaoli and from 1789 of the Barberini.
Sicilante and the sacred painting of the village.

The village of the witches of the high valley Argentina, Orange Flag, with the ethnographic museum and witchcraft linked to the process of 1587-1589, the Civic Museum of Palazzo Stella and the Collegiate Assumption.

Town of the valley of Vomano, on the edge of the Parco del Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga, gathered around Piazza Orsini with the Baroque collegiate church of San Rocco and the Palazzo marquisale Camponeschi-Carafa, and dominated on top of the hill by the Fort San Carlo of 1686.
The diocesan sanctuary dedicated to the Assumption, the heart of the devotional complex.

Rebuilt on a project by Paolo Falcone of Lugano, decided at the beginning of the seventeenth century, and reopened to worship in 1622; the façade was restored in 1890. Inside the Madonna del Rosario del Moncalvo (1620), the main altar of Giacomo Pellagatta (about 1760), the organ Serassi of 1852 in a baroque case of 1779 and the baptistery of 1964 by Luigi Visconti.
Discover the tradition of Friulian mosaicists.
In the Warehouse of the Sale Torre on the canal port, tools, documents and photos of the work of the saltworks; the Salina Camillone is its open-air section.

Outside the town, built according to tradition at the point where a Madonna-shaped rock found by miners became too heavy to carry. Feast on the first Sunday and Monday of September with cattle fair, sausage festival and Palio dei Berberi.
The artist who designed the face of the country.

Romanesque complex founded in the 11th century by Alberto da Prezzate (in Lombardy it dates to the 10th century) on the slopes of Monte Canto, with a wide view of the plain; it preserves frescoes, partly attributed to the Baschenis, and the sarcophagus of Teoperga. After the suppression the monastery was reborn in the twentieth century thanks to Father David Maria Turoldo. Guided tours by Lombardy Secret, by reservation.

On the small hill of Col di Zuca (cuel di Cjucie), west of the village, stood a place of early Christian worship used between the V and VII century AD; to the oldest phase belongs a basilica with a Mosaic presbyterial bench of Aquileian type, and remains visible part of the elegant mosaic floor with geometric and floral motifs.
Roman bridge built with stones of the nearby necropolis; you can reach it with a path along the river Biedano and a long passage flanked by graves.

Neoclassical municipal palace, formerly the prison palace, built in the second half of the nineteenth century with the contribution of the Turin architect Angelo Santoné; today it houses the Art Gallery of the Municipality.
Built for a vote at the Madonna di Oropa after the plague of 1399; next to the bell tower of Santo Stefano of the 11th century.
The complex is owned by the Valdese Church, designed in the sixties by architect Leonardo Ricci and considered one of the most original interventions of contemporary architecture in Sicily.
Baths and sunsets where three rivers meet the sea.
The dome closing the Grand Canal.
The castle above the city.
Monumental Palace on the Grand Canal which houses the 18th century Venetian Museum, among historical furnishings and 18th century works.
The Liberty in an Italian garden.

Started in 1572 and rebuilt between 1676 and 1689, with stuccoes by Paolo Frisoni and Michele Rigoli, the altarpiece of the Madonna del Carmine by Giovanni Masuti (1695) and works by Francesco Stringa and Carlo Cignani.

Opened in June 2008 in the canonical house of the church of San Giorgio Martire, it preserves the so-called Treasure of San Giorgio: sacred silvereries, wooden furnishings and liturgical vestments made largely by local craftsmen. Among the works there is a triptych by Bartolomeo Vivarini with the Madonna and Child between Saints George and Benedict and a wooden pulpit of the mid-sixteenth century. The environments were also a place for community assemblies, as 17th - century manuscripts attest. Without architectural barriers; information at 0984 411380.
The center of town life, to be seen even in the evening.
17th century building with travertine façade along the main street.
The main square with the Town Hall of the thirteenth century, whose thin tower is the symbol of the village, adorned with the coats of arms of the Podestà.
Monument of the end of the sixteenth century visible from Piazza Umberto I, between medieval palaces and Baroque churches of the center.

Inaugurated in 1965, the Sicilian ceramics from prehistory to the early twentieth century, from Greek and Roman artifacts to medieval, Baroque and nineteenth-century works; among the main pieces a crater of the fifth century BC with a workshop of ceramist and Athena Ergane.
Built between 1733 and 1754 with contributions from the municipality, the confraternities and the population.

The village of the zolfatari, called Altariva until the eighteenth century by Baron Pietro Altariva: the memory of the mines lives in the Zolfataro Monument, in the remains of the Trabia-Tallarita mines and in the Museum of the Solfare; then there are the prehistoric necropolis of the Caves and the Waldensian complex of Monte degli Ulivi by Leonardo Ricci.

The Superba, capital of the ancient maritime Republic: one of the largest historical centers in Europe, the New Roads and the Palaces of the Rolli UNESCO heritage, the Port Antico redesigned by Renzo Piano, the Lanterna and a vertical city of lifts, funiculars and strong up to the parks of Nervi and Pegli.
Luini and Gaudenzio Ferrari under the same roof.
Built in 1842 on the remains of the ancient Roman bridge of Arena.
The Greek tragedies where they were born.
By bike between vineyards and river.
The baptistery next to the bell tower of the cathedral, religious center of the city along with the cathedral.

Nestled in the rocks above the Gorges of Infernaccio, it is reached by a path in the beech woods. Benedictine Priory linked to Fonte Avellana from the 12th to the 15th century and then to the Camaldolese of Monte Corona, it was rebuilt by the foundations of the Capuchin Father Pietro Lavini.
Church decorated with frescoes by the painter Antonio Lanave.
Read the volcano Cimino in the rock.
The land of the barbatelle and its painters.

The white truffle (Tuber Magnatum Pico) grows on the hills of Palaia, which matures from September to December and to which the first card of identity has been dedicated here; in Forcoli, an ancient castle, every October for over thirty years the Exhibition of Truffle and Porcino is held. The Wine Route of the Pisan Hills starts from Palaia and crosses the Valdera between farms and historical estates with tastings and visits to the cellar.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 2 of the 5 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

The cemetery and the catacombs of the Capuchins, next to the church of Santa Maria della Pace and the convent: one of the most evocative and mysterious places in Sicily, with a deep historical and anthropological value.
A century of peasant life in sixty salt.
The church founded by the Dominicans in 1220 in the district of the Scotts, whose tombs it preserves, with many medieval elements and the decorated presbytery.
Black sand and clear water beach, with large free zones and a central part with sun loungers, umbrellas and bar; parking nearby.

The center, rebuilt after the invasion of 1509, rises on the Colle delle Capre within walls enlarged at the end of the fifteenth century and partly accessible with the Way of the Sentinel, with three doors: the monumental Porta Imperiale, Porta Oria and Porta Pusterla. Piazza Maggiore, reachable also by elevator, is dominated by the Castle of Alboino and surrounded by Lombard fountains, the church of Santi Rocco and Sebastiano, the Palazzo della Ragione and the Gazzi palaces, Bovio-Da Romagno and Guarnieri; many noble palaces have frescoed facades.

About 9 km of mainly sandy beaches in the stretch called "mare" of the seven colors. Campomarino, 2 km from the center, is a twentieth-century seaside resort with the largest marina on the Ionian-Salentine coast. Transparent and low water for several meters from the shore.
The story of a mountain pass in a 16th century palace.
The Gagini marble triptych.
Alpine lakes and border hills over 2,000 meters.
You can see it in a few minutes.
The historic villa of the center, today library, with park and frescoed ceilings.
A mountaineering museum to be reached on foot.
The track along the Bisenzio river, among the bike proposals of the Prato area.

Nordic Ski Stadium that hosted the World Cup Championships of 1991, 2003 and 2013 and World Cup races, with rings of different length, evening lighting in some days, biathlon area and outdoor skating rink; in summer walks and bikes along the valley floor and the Val di Fiemme bike path.
The square with the Bishop's Palace and the eighteenth century Palazzo Caracciolo.
The view from the Covetta Park.

Rufolo family residence with thirteenth-century nucleus around the Moorish courtyard with double gallery, extended until the end of the eighteenth century in Arabic, Siculo and Norman style; the main tower offers views of the Gulf of Salerno. The Scottish Francis Nevile Reid created in the nineteenth century the terraced garden, called "Giardino dell'Anima" (Garden of the Soul), which according to tradition inspired Wagner (visiting in May 1880) the garden of Klingsor del Parsifal; in the lower garden is held the Ravello Festival. Open every day 9-20 according to Italia.it.

Gothic-Romanesque cathedral with the pulpit of Nicola Pisano (1265-68), the young statues of Michelangelo on the Piccolomini altar and the San Giovanni Battista di Donatello; the marble tarsie floor is discovered only in some periods of the year.
the MiC card indicates "closed" every day without hours; summer guided tours reported by the MiC for the area: contact the Accademia degli Etruschi (tel. 348 5106404)

Village on a plateau of olive trees and orchards overlooking Lake Garda, formed by six small centres of medieval origin; above the lake dominates the Sanctuary of Montecastello, while at the port stands the lemon garden of Prà de la Fam.
The symbol of feudal power, with a view of the territory.
Walking in the Pinocchio TV sites.
It was founded in the 13th century as a monastery of the Humiliates, then an olive grove, with the sixteenth-century church of San Bortolo and the cloister.
A medieval oratory made of Roman stones.
A marble embroidery on the Arno.
The large white sandy beach, ideal for families.
The theatre of the opera of the capital, built by the impresario Domenico Costanzi in the area of Via Nazionale.
The high village above the promenade.
Inaugurated in 1974 at the Samoggia Palace next to Santa Croce in Jerusalem, with a large collection of musical instruments and a new inclusive itinerary.

Country of Alto Sannio at the foot of the hill Toppa Barrata, between Tammaro and Calore, with a castle plundered by Ruggero II in 1138 and rebuilt after the earthquake of 1456; it houses the seventeenth-century church of Santi Nicola and Rocco, the Museum of Arts and Popular Traditions and in October the International Balloon Gathering.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 3 of the 4 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

City founded by the Phoenicians at the end of the 8th century BC on nuragic traces, then Carthaginian, Roman from 238 BC and first capital of the Judicate of Arborea, abandoned in 1070. Between Capo San Marco and the San Giovanni hill: tofet by Su Murru Mannu, walls, temples (including the tetrastyle one with the columns still standing), spas, forum, aqueduct, necropolis and Spanish coastal towers. Visits every day 9-19 with reservation; managed by the Mont'e Prama Foundation.

In 1864 engineer Giovanni Eyquem discovered a rich zinc deposit and founded the company of Malfidano; between 1870 and 1890 the laverie arose and since 1866 more than one million tons of zinc and 200,000 of lead were extracted. On September 4, 1904, the miners' strike ended in the Buggerru massacre, with three workers killed. The visit crosses the miners' workplaces with a view of the sea and cliffs; the museum of local history is in a former workshop in front of the port.
Fishing and canoeing under the village.
The coats of arms painted by the Venetian Clusone.

Renaissance Palace of the late fifteenth century, built under the lordship of Del Balzo and passed to the Sangiovanni in 1643. The façade, unique in its kind, has a zigzag diamond-pointed bulwark; in the center the arched portal with phytomorphic motifs and two floors of arched windows, those of the noble floor framed by paraste. It is private property: it is admired from the outside.
The mother church and its altars.
The marsh valleys and the horses' boats.

Monferrato Astigiano village grew up around the abbey founded in the 10th century by the Marquis Aleramo, whose tomb is preserved in the former abbey church today parish; birthplace of the marshal Pietro Badoglio, remembered by the panoramic stele of 24 meters wanted by Battista Pininfarina and the historical museum Badogliano.
The house of the good Giant of boxing.
The granite cathedral.
The UNESCO landscape of the Coast.

Small museum of rural traditions was born when, at the end of the eighties, Francesco Balbiano transformed the family farm and decided to restore the objects of peasant life instead of eliminating them; it is set up in the old carriagehouse and was inaugurated in 1990. Visits by reservation.
Dolmen and peucetic village in a secluded gravina.

Municipality to the north-west of Teramo, gateway to the Laga Mountains, probably born between the IX and the X century as a fortified village; it preserves medieval churches in the hamlets, the ethnographic museum "Le genti della Laga" and the abandoned village of Valle Piola.

He rose to replace the pagan worship of the goddess Mefite with Christian worship: the first small church of the fourth century was destroyed with earthquakes of 1688 and 1694, was rebuilt at the end of the seventeenth century by the priest Giovanbattista Santoli and enriched over a century after a portal by the archpriest Vincenzo Maria Santoli. Rebuilt after World War I, it has been in its present form since 1928.

Ancient castle transformed in 1616 into a late Renaissance villa designed by Antonio Cantagallina, with loggia and Italian gardens; it houses the archaeological museum with the excavations of the villa in Tuscis of Plinio il Giovane.
The castle that tells the Ladin world.
The alabards engraved 4,500 years ago, always accessible.
The messapic supplies of the necropolis of Manduria.

The bell tower leaning against the Cathedral on Corso Marcelli, with the large ogival arch through which passes the road and four Roman togate statues; the current structure dates back to the restorations of 1456 of Bishop Giacomo Montaquila.
A masterpiece of the Renaissance in marble in a village church.

Recognized regional museum in 2010, it was born from the tools donated by Antonio De Rosa's private collection and is ordered in six sections: plowing, harvesting (bocker's tools, presses), agricultural tools, hemp and flax (tiles, combs, bunches), everyday objects and shoemakers', carpenters and blacksmith's trades.
The religious and civil heart of the country.
A hundred million years of Lazio told in a fortress.

The tour of the lakes of Cevedale touches Lake Lungo, Pian Palù delle Marmotte, Covel and Careser to Malga Mare, about 2,000 meters; the lake of Pian Palù and Lake Covel can be reached also with easy paths.

The seat of the diocese of Civitavecchia-Tarquinia, built in 1610, rebuilt in 1782 for Clement XIV on a project by Francesco Navone and cathedral since 1805; damaged in 1943 and restored in 1950 by Plinio Marconi. Baroque facade with double ionic order with statues of Faith and Justice by Pietro De Laurentiis; inside a Nativity attributed to the school of the Domenichino and the organ Pinchi restored in 2019.
open on request at times to be agreed with the Municipality
The church of the 13th century.
Wild sea in the rocks.
The light sundial of June 21st.

City of the Bergamo plain built between the 10th and 11th centuries around a castle; in the square the Basilica of San Martino with the Polyptych of Butinone and Zenale and a bell tower of 68 meters, not far from the Sanctuary of the Blessed Virgin of the Tears, linked to the miracle of 28 February 1522, and the civic museums.

Carzano, an ancient feud of the Martinengo family, preserves the Martinengo palace (private), the sixteenth-century Casa Novali and the Ziliani palace with stone portal of Sarnico; every five years it hosts the feast of Santa Croce, when the village and Novale are covered with thousands of paper flowers. Novale, a medieval village on a terrace above Carzano, in the mid-sixteenth century was the summer residence of the bishop of Brescia Marco Morosini (Casa Morosini).
The peasant and pastoral life of Pollino.
The popular museum of the village.

The church of "'o munacone" of the early seventeenth century designed by Fra Cuvolo, a Greek cross with majolica dome, which incorporates the catacombs of St. Gaudioso with frescoes and mosaics of the fifth and sixth centuries and the Madonna della Sanità, perhaps the oldest Marian image of Naples.
The symbol of Spoleto, to cross on foot.
An eighteenth-century villa with garden open to all.
The baroque lounge of the village.
Saturday morning market, one of the largest in Piedmont.
The bronze baroque in the center of the square.
Access door to the Maira Valley on foot.
Nineteenth-century church among the monuments not to be missed in the center.
The wood and crafts of the valley before the dam.
The village suspended.
The surviving bell tower of the village deleted from Etna.
The ruined towers on the lake's bike path.
One of the most spectacular panoramic points of Tuscia: the entire lake of Bolsena with the Martana and Bisentina islands and, on clear days, Mount Amiata and Tyrrhenian.
The Sacred Mile.
16th century façade and late-Gothic frescoes.

Next to the Civic Tower, the 13th-XIV century palace houses the Civic Museum with archaeological and paleontological finds of Montefeltro, in particular from the excavations of the ancient city of Pitinum Pisaurense; the paleontological section is set up in the civic tower.

Just over 2 km from the village, it occupies about 5,000 m2, of which at least 1,000 are a necropolis with 33 intact tombs, different in shape, covering, covering and orientation. The remains of a city walls and an inhabited area have also emerged; the furnishings indicate settlements since the Neolithic period. The site began to depopulate with the Roman conquest and was destroyed in the 5th century AD during the wars between Goths and Byzantines.
Remains of a villa of late Republican age outside the walls, with a residential part and a rustic with thermal facilities.

Three centuries of watches, from the end of the seventeenth century to today, in the village where watchmaking was for three centuries the main economic activity: eighteenth century pendulums, tower clocks, palette watches and recent production. For ongoing work at the moment it is not accessible to those with motor disabilities.

The church of the Name of Mary, to the west of the village, is the oldest and most remarkable building of the hamlet, with remains of frescoes in façade dated 1453; next, courtyards with loggia houses. To the south, on a rocky spur, the remains of the castle made of porphyry stone overlooking the valleys of Sesia, Sessera and Strona.

The green areas of the estate, reclaimed and arranged, are open to all: the eucalyptus forest, behind the main entrance, has a wellness path; to the east of the estate is the holm oak forest; the oak forest, in front of the entrance, where the Bourbon kings hunted, is today the picnic area dedicated to Don Peppe Diana. The picnic area opens on Sundays from 11 am to 4 pm, with tables on reservation; you can't light fires or barbecues and dogs are allowed on a leash and muzzle.

Museum of Modern and Religious Art born at the will of Daedalo Montali (Cagliari 1909 - Rodello 2001), painter, sculptor and poet, on the initiative of the widow Taja Satta Montali and the canon Mario Battaglino. Paintings and sculptures are ordained for periods and themes, from the pre-war to the end of the twentieth century, in two places: the halls of the church of the Immaculate Conception and the Residence. For visits: Municipality, tel. 0173 617107.
Climb by cable car over 3,200 meters above the entire basin.
Where the first Italian book was printed.

The village is located on the Lazio side of the park, at the foot of the Meta massif (2,242 meters), between beech, chestnut and oak woods; between the paths that of Ponte Lebranche and that towards the artificial lake of Grotta Campanaro, and in winter the ski resorts of Prati di Mezzo. The Morge del Corvo, walled in the woods on the Val Canneto and the Melfa river, are a climbing destination.
Pagani's shovel in the council room.
Seven centuries of sacred art is not an option.

The Romanesque-Gothic Duomo, from the 12th to the 14th century, with a richly decorated rose window and portal, a fourth nave on the right side and in counterfaced the Last Judgment of Ferraù Fenzoni.

The tower, commissioned by Alfonso d'Aragona and mentioned in 1542, was enlarged to four floors by the Bourbons and damaged in 1813; today it is private and used as a hotel. The cemetery has the nucleus of 1772 around the chapel of Santa Maria della Salvazione and the Sepulchre Tricoli (1837); the lighthouse is from 1858 and is still in operation.
The neighborhood of San Francesco.
Borgo del Casentino, among the most beautiful villages since 2015, with pedestrian streets and a tradition linked to chestnut.

The old town is located on two islands of the Livenza, with buildings mirroring in the water. Two castles on the left of the Cesano still surrounded by sturdy walls in shoes: Montalfoglio 393 meters and San Vito sul Cesano 353 meters, autonomous municipality until 1869. The I.A.T. Point includes Montalfoglio on the guided tour by reservation, while the San Vito Giovani Association organizes the San Vito Tour with the Pieve Vecchia.

The birthplace of Santa Caterina, in the area of Fontebranda, transformed over the centuries into a sanctuary; it is accessed by the Portico of the Municipalities of Italy (1939) and the heart is the Church of the Crucifix, with the wooden crucifix from which the Saint received the stigmata in 1375.

Piceno village from the historical center oval (about 180 for 90 meters) closed by the walls, with the oldest parts of the late thirteenth century: the Civic Museum of sacred art with the altarpiece of Vincenzo Pagani, the Town Hall with the San Giorgio, the Antiquarium \Pansoni Â with the finds of district Fiorano; around calanchi, wines and organic oil.

Terrace of 1.26 hectares on the Valle dei Calanchi, between Lake Bolsena and the Tiber, established in 2016 and managed by the Municipality, which helps to read the geomorphological processes of a lunar but luxuriant landscape. The point of view can be reached by car or by a 9-seater shuttle to be booked at least 7 days before with the Guides (tel. 328 5430394); reference is the Naturalistic Museum.

In the countryside around the fortified village, originally dedicated to St Simeon; according to the tradition reported by the source, King Ferdinand I of Bourbon gave her a painting of the Assumption.

Church of 16th century origin, remodelled in Baroque style in the 18th century and proclaimed Pontifical Basilica in 1998; the worship of the icon of the Mother of God generating Victories dates back to 1571, after the return of the Sanvitesi from Lepanto. Baroque façade with bronze portal, inside a Latin cross with three naves; preserves paintings by Paolo De Maio (Birth of the Virgin, Crucifixion, Last Supper), the Last Judgment of Barnaba Zizzi (1816), the silver reliquary of San Vito, an eighteenth-century organ case and 16 wooden sculptures of the Passion of the early nineteenth century.

City on the sea north of Bari, called dolmen: the ancient center with the Romanesque cathedral, the church of Sant'Adoeno of 1074 and the Swabian castle, the marina and in the countryside the Dolmen of Chianca of the Bronze Age.

Late medieval ass-back bridge with four stone arches on the Bormida of Millesimo, for centuries the only one that can be passed all year round; the chapel in the center of the main arch was originally a toll guard. In the 1994 flood, he lost parapets and chapels, but the arches resisted.

Commissioned in 1490 by Benedetto Fodri, with portal of 1493 by Alberto Maffiolo da Carrara, terracotta facade and courtyard with terracotta friezes.

Set up in the historic Villa Matarazzo, it exhibits a small collection of finds recovered in the backdrops in front of it, especially amphorae and anchors of Etruscan, Greek, Roman and Byzantine age. Closed in January and February.

Freshwater flooded forest of about 190 hectares, among the last of southern Europe, with a pedestrian ring of about 2 km and a birdwatching shed.

The parish church of San Michele Arcangelo was built between 1860 and 1870 in neoclassical style, designed by G.B. Carducci di Fermo, with a single nave and a peristyle of eight columns around presbytery and apse. In the center also Sant'Agostino, of the twelfth century, with ancient portal and arched windows, and Sant'Andrea, born with the first hospital authorized in 1421, with neoclassical structure and façade of the second half of the eighteenth century.

The large central avenue is flanked by elegant bourgeois palaces, shops and shops that arose with the development of the nineteenth century linked to sulphur (Palazzo Capone, D'Agostino, Salerno and Caruso); the town hall occupies the former Verginian Monastery, quadrangular building of the late sixteenth-early seventeenth century.

Excursion of about 7,8 km (2 hours and 30, 501 meters of climb) from the bridge of the village to Moso in the wild gorge of Passirio: the path follows the river with water with bridges and walkways on the walls, halfway up with views of the waterfall of Stulles and continues in the woods to the dam of Moso; you return with bus 240. At 1,333 meters south-east of Trento, on the edge of a vast plateau of pastures between Folgaria, Lavarone and Passo Vezzena; it is the last linguistic island in which the cimbrian, ancient Bavarian dialect, is spoken fluently by about 90% of the inhabitants.

In the Tower of Ligny, built in 1671 at the behest of Viceroy Claudio La Moraldo, Prince of Ligny: on the ground floor prehistoric and protohistoric finds of the province of Trapani, on the first floor over one hundred objects recovered in the Mediterranean sea bottom, between amphorae, anchors and objects of Greek, Roman and Punic use, with a bronze helmet of the IV-III century BC fished off Trapani. From the terrace the view ranges from Capo San Vito to Marsala and Mozia, with Trapani, Erice and the Egadi.

Bracket lagoon 22 km long and at most 3 km wide, a little more than 2 meters deep, which with that of Varano forms the largest brackish complex in southern Italy. A 7,65 km ring (about 5 and a half hours, high difficulty) from the church of Santa Maria a Castello a Punta Nasone (1,132 m), the highest peak of Somma, above the Valley of the Giant: the first stretch on the Via Traversa is equipped for the blind and disabled, then woods of robinia and chestnut, the cognoli of Trocchia and Sant'Anastasia with views of the gulf and the Gran Cono, and on top a chapel and a large cross linked to the Feast of the Mountain.

The site of the territorial museum "I volte dell'Ubagu" of the Arroscia Valley, tells about 10,000 years of local history, from prehistory to today: from the nearby caves, called pre-Roman Ligurian name "arma" are stone instruments, ceramics of the Iron Age and remains of fireplaces. A plastic exhibition where the caves are accessible, reachable by a signposted path; educational room and guided tours. Tel. 0183 382057.
Fortress with a starry plan on the right bank of the Po, rebuilt at the end of the seventeenth century against Venice; it can only be seen from the outside.

In the sixteenth century Villa Balestra, in a park at the edge of the village, the Museo diffuso del Risorgimento has two permanent exhibitions on Ippolito Nievo (1831-1861): Open during the hours of the municipal library or by appointment; accessible by elevator.

Path for experienced hikers (EE) of 4.7 km, about 2 hours and 50 minutes, 725 m of difference in altitude uphill: crosses the forest at the edge of a gravel, goes back to hairpin bends an ancient mule track on the east wall of the Fammera alternating rocks and stones, touches the Sella di Fammera di Spigno and with one last steep stretch reaches the summit. Views on the walls, on the eastern Aurunci and on the Ausente Valley to the sea; no water points, recommended season March-October.

It is located in the Capuchin monastery built since 1608 on a hill overlooking the village. It exhibits illuminated choir books, papal decrees from the sixteenth century, relics, wooden statues, paintings and liturgical furnishings from other Sardinian convents; an archaeological section with finds from the Neolithic to the early Christian and Byzantine ages; and the reconstruction of the daily life of the convent with the tools of the friars. The guided tour is included in the ticket. Open Saturday and Sunday 10-13 and 15:30-19 (from June to October 16-19:30).

Borgo on the north shore of Lake Iseo, with Piazza XIII Martiri on the port, the medieval village and its towers, the fifteenth-century Basilica of Santa Maria in Valvendra and the Galleria dell'Accademia Tadini, with works of Canova, in the neoclassical palace on the lakefront.

The center has a chessboard system closed by the bastions (Palestro, Montebello, Magenta, Solferino) and is crossed by Via Maestra, with about a kilometer of arcades, eighteenth-century houses such as Casa Castelli and Casa Daneo, the Palazzo dei Conti Czecho of Vaglierano and the liberty Casa Garola. In Piazza Libertà, the Palazzo Vagnone, in Umbertino style and connected to the Town Hall by a gallery, houses the Regional Enoteca delle Colline Alfieri; the Town Hall, historic residence of the Carlevaris, preserves in the atrium the funeral stele of Daniele Scarampi of 1445. Along Via Maestra also the church of Addolorata, known for its terracotta architecture.
A fifteenth-century church on the shores of Lake Bolsena, known for the ... "forgiveness" of St. Magnus, the plenary indulgence that is celebrated every year on 19 August.

A small white stone village in the Majella National Park, called the village crib, with views from the Gran Sasso to the sea; surroundings with the sanctuary of the Madonna dell'Elcina, the huts in tholos and the Paleolithic site of Valle Gimentina.

Founded in 1959 by the then mayor Pietro Fedele and re-arranged in 2001, it tells in 40 areas the prehistory of southern Lazio from about a million years ago. It preserves the cranial cap of the Man of Ceprano, called Argil, found by Italo Biddittu in 1994 and dated to over 800,000 years, among the oldest human fossils in Europe; hundreds of original finds (stone and bone instruments, bones and tusks of elephants) and life-size casts of Lucy, Homo habilis and Homo erectus, with many replicas to be touched even for the blind. Open Saturday and Sunday 15.30-18.30; guided tours, workshops and simulated excavations especially for schools.

A short distance from the parish church, the arch of San Cristoforo is inserted in a sixteenth-century house with a fresco of the saint; in Piazza San Rocco stands the church of the same name, whose origins date back to the end of the fifteenth century. From San Cristoforo start the step-by-step path and the mule track to the sanctuary of the Holy Trinity.

Built between 1901 and 1905 for Baron Carlo Maurizio Gamba on a project by Carlo Saroldi, it houses the regional collections of painting, sculpture and graphics collected since 1948; park with monumental trees.

A second section documents the rock necropolis of Viterbese.

Wide area of about 26,000 m2 south of the center, with bell-shaped grain pits dug into the ground, covered with stone or brick and closed with boards and earth; each pit is marked by a stone chip about 90 cm high with the initials of the owner and a number. Documented since 1225, in 1902 there were about 1,100: today 625 remain, about 200 still in use to store cereals, with average capacity of 500 quintals; the area is bound since 1982.

Established in 2007, it covers about 1,600 hectares: from the sea to the inland sandy and rocky coasts, humid areas retrodunal and marshland, woods, Mediterranean scrub, age-old olive groves and ravines, parallel karst canals dug by water. Built by Luca Spinola at the end of the fifteenth century on a 12th century complex, it stands on a tuff cliff above the Piota: irregular pentagonal plan, transition building between fortress and mansion, with double windows, slits under the windows, square tower towards the village, large Spinola coat of arms painted on the east side and fifteenth-century triangular courtyard with arches and stone columns. Inside paintings, antique furniture and a gallery of coats of arms; it is still owned by Spinola. A legend wants three gold roses hidden in the courtyard left in 1565 by Isabella Corvalan.

The walls preserve fortifications of the 14th and 15th centuries and suggestive military walks covered; from the village the look ranges from the Adriatic to the Sibillini Mountains. Locality of the Brescian shore of Garda linked to Gabriele d'Annunzio, who created the Vittoriale degli Italiani between 1921 and 1938; with the Botanical Garden André Heller, the lakefront and the Liberty villas and déco immersed in Mediterranean parks.

Here were laid the foundations of the Congregation of Monte Corona and in the 16th century there found refuge two minor friars who founded the Order of the Capuchins; the caves also served as a hiding place for the friars persecuted by the Inquisition. The cellars can only be visited in a group.

A circular tower probably in the mid-15th century, restored in the nineties, which houses the museum of the old parish church of Santa Maria Assunta destroyed by the earthquake of 1915: furnishings of the church, sculptures and sacred vestments of over three centuries.

Lecci, olive trees and carobs, caves, streams, waterfalls and ponds, orchids also endemic, cedars of Lebanon and the Himalayas and a great magnolia.

According to tradition, the Virgin appeared here to Blessed Mario Omodei on 29 September 1504; the sanctuary, designed by Tommaso Rodari with a Latin cross with three naves, transept and dome, was begun in 1505, had the bell tower in 1576 and the dome in 1580, and in 1927 was raised to a minor basilica by Pius XI. Inside the golden statues of the Apparition by Giovan Angelo Del Majno (1519), five great Marian paintings by Giovan Battista Recchi (1634-1637), the main altar in black marble of Varenna (1748) and especially the organ of Giuseppe Bulgarini (1608-1617), with about 2,200 reeds, whose carved case is the most admired work. In the municipal palace, it tells the social and artistic history of the territory from prehistory to today: the Archaeological Museum "Valerio Cianfarani" (Valerio Cianfarani), the Civic Museum "Raffaele Campelli" (Raffaele Campelli), the Historical Museum of the territory (home weaving with 15th century canvases, brick kilns, history of the Varnelli distillery), the xylographies of Maria Ciccotti and the collection Gino Marotta in the council hall, with the fortepiano of composer Filippo Marchetti.

Around the villa there is a large romantic park that can be visited by itself. Open from Tuesday to Sunday, closed on Mondays.
The glacier under the Matterhorn.
Casentino centre with the Torre dei Tarlati, churches with Robbian ceramics and an archaeological museum.

In the neoclassical house that Spontini bought and rebuilt with his wife Celeste Erard for his return to Maiolati. Tools in stone, remains of hunted animals and finds that tell the continuous home of the territory from prehistory; a small museum known for the educational setup.

Hand stitching still alive.

Avifaunistic oasis of municipal property in the hills of Fagagna, born with a project to re-introduction of white stork, today visible throughout the country. In 2025 69 storks and 52 ibis hermits were born there, a species of which the oasis hosts about a quarter of the 800 specimens in the world; it also hosts ducks protected as elevator, dairy and tobacconist bites, and hosts about 10,000 visitors a year.

In the middle of the 13th century, with façade in Romanesque-Gothic tuff (gate and rosette with twelve columns), side sixteenth century with stone portal and dome with steps of Byzantine model; bell tower and interior were rebuilt in the eighteenth century. Church and convent today seat of the Town Hall, known for its beautiful 18th century cloister.

Small village about 1,000 m on the slopes of Terminillo, overlooking the Velino Gorges 112 km from Rome: along the Salaria, next to the river, stands the Benedictine abbey of Saints Quirico and Julitta, documented since 984; in the village the church of San Lorenzo Martire and the Civic Museum of the Arts and Popular Traditions.

The city of ceramics is overlooking the sea of the province of Messina at the foot of the Nebrodi: rebuilt further south after the earthquake of 1682, it is the historic center of Sicilian ceramics and Matrangela, with streets full of shops and the Civic Museum of ceramics in Palazzo Trabia.

Funeral monument of Augustan age or of the first century A.D., so called for the cusp shape similar to a basket to collect; the municipality considers it almost the symbol of the Roman architecture of Quarto.

He guards a Madonna with Child donated in 1875 by the German painter Franz Johann Heinrich Nadorp; tradition links the church to the miracle of Sister Claudia De Angelis, after whose stop the spiritual father found bouquets of roses on the altar.

The village is entirely made of white limestone, without real walls: a continuous ring of houses with a few small windows was a dwelling and a defence. Straight and winding streets go up to the tower, through arcades, arched portals, stone windows, mullioned windows and Medici balconies; the House of the Captain is of the fifteenth century. The southeast gate keeps the Medici coat of arms.

Church on two levels: the upper one of the 15th century, retouched at the end of the 18th century in Baroque forms; the lower one, more ancient, dedicated to Santa Maria delle Grazie, is a suggestive succorpore that houses a small alabaster statue of the Madonna of Trapani (late 16th century).
Built at the end of the fifteenth century at the highest point of the old town, it has a tripartite Gothic façade with a rosette decorated; the interior is baroque and preserves valuable art works.
To live Siena like the Sienese.

Val di Tures village in the valleys of the Natural Park Vedrette di Ries-Aurina, Orange Flag of Touring, dominated by Castel Tures, one of the best preserved castles of South Tyrol; around the late-Gothic parish and, in Caminata, the Riva waterfalls.
Cities at the gates of Turin in the Parco del Po Piemontese: the Freidano ecomuseum in the New Mill and the medieval tower of the historic centre.
A series of small waterfalls and jumps along the Water Path.

T-shirts, objects and photographs of Italian and foreign champions such as Binda, Girardengo, Guerra, Bartali, Coppi, Gimondi, Merckx and Maspes, with yellow tour jerseys and pink tour jerseys and all Toni Pessot jerseys donated by his daughter to the municipality; also on display are three pairs of boxing gloves, one belonging to Primo Carnera. Visits only by reservation, every day.

On the rocks above the village, it is the ancient parish dedicated to the holy healer after the vow made by the inhabitants during a serious epidemic, according to tradition in 1878; every year in May there is held the sacred representation of the martyrdom of the saint.
Fossils, minerals and a Nile crocodile in seminary.
Taranto traditions in a noble palace.
The square is surrounded by Baroque palaces, a UNESCO World Heritage Site; at the end the Baroque church of Saint Lucia alla Badia, dedicated to the patron saint.

Nuraghe of 1500-900 BC, about 700 meters away, with two massive towers joined by a thick wall curtain. Nearby eight domus de Janas, a dolmen, three tombs of Giants and three Nuragheddu villages (Nurageddu, the fortress of Seroni and the megalithic village of Seddorrulu, of the third millennium BC).

Roman town hall on a ridge at 526 meters overlooking the Umbra valley, a few hundred meters from Collemancio: plant of the second century BC, maximum development between the end of the first century BC and beginning II AD, decline in the fifth century. The walls remain sections, the urban layout along the road to Mevania and Vettona, a temple of the II century BC on podium of 23.80 x 17.80 meters, a cistern and a spa complex of over 400 square meters; with Roman materials was built the early Christian basilica of Santa Maria de Orbinum.
A rare Byzantine dome building.

The capital of the Natisone Valleys for the population, where in the SMO museum the cultural landscape of the Slovenian provinces of Udine, Gorizia and Trieste is told in a multimedia way; in the hamlet of Biarzo a cavity along the river has returned the oldest human traces of the area, of the upper Paleolithic and of the Neolithic; in the municipal territory there are the latedogotic churches of San Quirino, San Bartolomeo and Sant'Antonio Abate and the castellieri of Roba and Barda.

Founded in 1801 on the bequest of the abbot Marcantonio Maldotti, since 1857 Garibaldi was in the process where the Jesuit church of San Luigi (1741) stood: about 100,000 volumes, about twenty incunabula, paintings, prints, coins, medals and herbari, with a sixteenth-century puteal in the atrium. Fortified village of the Garfagnana, already Roman castrum, closed by the walls and towers built by Lucca in 1371: a rare almost intact walled village.
Also known as Hermitage of the Saints, it was founded by the Benedictines in the 12th century and passed to the canons in the 14th century; the external part dates back to the 19th century.

The territory has 40 Nuragic settlements: the main is the complex of Is Meurras with village and tomb of Giganti, which with the nearby imposing Nuraghe Carroccia controlled the territory; the nuraghe Tratalias, with central tower and three perimeter towers joined by curtains, is the best preserved complex, the nuraghe Cuccu the best preserved monotorre.

In an ancient manor house, twelve thematic rooms with panels on the researches at the nuraghe Arrubiu, conducted from 1981 to 1996 and resumed in 2012, and on the protohistory of Sardinia and the Mediterranean. Access for a fee, guided tours only in the afternoon.
In the middle of the vineyards, overlooking the hills, the Alps and the Apennines.
The Sila Piccola woods are just a few kilometres from the village.
The Orient of Merchants.
The main theatre of Fano, named after the ancient Fanum Fortunae: it hosts opera, prose and dance; renovated and reopened in 2002.

Late-Gothic monastic church founded in 1452 by Antonio Sanseverino and consecrated in 1485, with ogival portal in yellow stone and wooden ceiling in ship hull, unique in Calabria. Inside there is a fifteenth-century wooden crucifix, the 1611 pulpit, the choir carved in 1538 and the 15th-century cloister.
Paintings by Osvaldo Licini and works by Lucio Fontana, Hans Hartung and Roberto Sebastian Matta.

Country of the Sicani Mountains, on a plateau among fields and vineyards, dominated by the Mother Church of San Giovanni Battista; home of the director Frank Capra, preserves the Museum of the clock in the shop of the Scibetta watchmakers and, on Monte Triona, the seventeenth-century Sanctuary of the Madonna del Balzo.
Trecentesque frescoes in a country oratory.

Medieval village of white houses on a spur overlooking the sea of the Ulysses Riviera, with Torre Truglia and the gates of the Caetani; at the foot of the promontory the Villa di Tiberio with the cave and the National Archaeological Museum of the Odyssey sculptural groups, and about 10 km of golden beaches.
The center of Christendom.
On the trail of the Garibaldi.

Area of the Majella National Park activated in August 2003 to make known the wolf, at 750 meters: it hosts a couple of wolves and can accommodate injured or problematic specimens not liberable. The best hours to watch them are the winter afternoon and the summer evening; the guided tour starts from the Environmental Education Center      • The Big Beech (via Fontepalombo 36).

In the historic centre, it exhibits the tradition of carpets, blankets and embroidery of the village: Longobucco is one of the few places in Calabria where weaves again on handlooms, with the design woven into the weft and not embroidered; its fabrics were exhibited in Rome between 1921 and 1925 and awarded with the silver medal in Barcelona (1929) and Milan (1930).

In Acquarica del Capo, a centre adjacent to Presicce, medieval origins are testified by the remains of the castle, hidden among the old houses.

Stone village at 428 meters, mentioned since 1211 and remained almost intact, between the most beautiful villages in Italy and Orange Flag; since the post-war period it has attracted artists from all over Europe. Outside the village, the statue of the Villa del Monte reminds us of the ancient autonomous administration; in August there is the rustic Middle Ages, in winter the Christmas markets.
The capital of Barbera in Monferrato UNESCO, with the  "Campanon" symbol of the city and the museums of wine and taste.

The city of Brianza is linked to the family of the ... Giussano, from which tradition leads Alberto, legendary captain of the Company of Death at the battle of Legnano in 1176. To see Villa Sartirana with its park, Casa Mazerta designed by Pellegrino Tibaldi and the windows of Aligi Sassu in the Council Hall.

Frazione 550 meters, about five km from the center: from the square you can see the Pettoruto, the plain of Sibari and, on clear days, two stretches of the Ionian. The Palace, which dates back to 1126, is the oldest building, in Renaissance-baroque style, with the chapel of the Immaculate Church in front of it; the church of San Nicola di Bari, with a single nave with wooden pulpit and bell of 1791, preserves the Madonna della Pietà of supposed Neapolitan school, disputed in 1881 with San Marco Argentano.
Summer resort at 625 meters, in a panoramic position in the upper valley of Ceno and along the Via Francigena, with flowery meadows, streams and panoramic walks.

Borgo dei Monti Sibillini founded around 1300 as Castrum Sancti Angeli, a triangular plan with tower, walls and doors, near the springs of the Black and the foot of Mount Prata; it preserves fourteenth-century churches like San Martino and Santo Stefano and houses the center of the Park dedicated to the deer. The village was hit by the 2016 earthquake.

City between the rivers Maira and Mellea, between Five and Six hundred candidate in the capital of the duchy of Sabaudo: the medieval Piazza Santa Rosa with the Civic Tower and the triumphal arch, the Palaces Taffini d'Acceglio and Muratori Cravetta, the Civic Museum with the Gipsoteca Calandra and the Piemontese Railway Museum.

Neoclassical church dedicated to the patron saint, inspired by the Roman basilica of St. John Lateran: started in 1808, open to worship in 1818, completed in 1865 and parish since 1869, in 1967 received the title of Minor Papal Basilica.

Murialdo is one of the two Ligurian localities with a sword in the rock: it is located not far from the Castle Del Carretto, along a path that the regional portal defines very beautiful and suitable for families.

Mausoleum of Augustian age on the Appian Way in Acervara, attributed by tradition to Marco Tullio Cicero, killed in Formia on December 7th 43 BC by the assassins of Marco Antonio, but without inscriptions that confirm it: tower about 24 meters high with square base and circular drum, two burial chambers superimposed and fenced in cross-linked work around the funeral garden. Managed by Sinus Formianus.

Villa of the early twentieth century in Empire style with garden in English, has been the donation of the painter of chierista Vittorio Viviani (ten paintings and more than fifty drawings); restored in 1998 and again until the reopening of 2024, it houses the civic artistic collection. The Arts of the Fire section brings together contemporary painting and sculpture on porcelain, ceramics, terracotta, glass and glazes, awarded at the National Competition "Arti del fuoco" (Fire Arts), the painting section also includes the works of the Vittorio Viviani Prize, the ...Bice Bugatti-Giovanni Segantini Prize and the Engraving Review (1996-2014).

The village is enclosed by a medieval wall of elliptical shape with square towers and the gateway called Aretina, connected to the fortress. Inside the Palazzo Pretorio of the fourteenth century and, in Piazza Lazzeri, a medieval cistern.
The small frescoed church can be reached on foot.

A circular plan baptistery of the sixth century, built on a Roman building of the II-III century and mentioned already in 841: a dome on fifteen arches supported by pairs of columns covers the octagonal baptismal bath, according to the Municipality the second of the genus in Italy after that of San Giovanni in Laterano. Today it is about four meters below the road plan.

Romanesque parish church probably of the 11th century, with Renaissance additions and an octagonal baptismal font believed to be prior to the 1st century. At Christmas, the village becomes the village of the nativity scenes, with nativity scenes illuminated in the courtyards.

The old town is a combination of stairs, alleys and arches, from which the city takes its name; characteristic the 'Suppourti', covered stretches of the streets born for defensive needs. Scalea was an important maritime port of call from the Norman era and in the Angevin-Aragonese period it exceeded the 5000 inhabitants; bombed in the Second World War, from the 60s the center was progressively abandoned in favor of the coast.

Country of the Orco Valley in the Gran Paradiso National Park, at the foot of the Noaschetta waterfall, about 32 meters high. In the town hall there is the visitor center of the Park dedicated to the shapes of the landscape; above the village the ring of the high hamlets leads to the waterfall of the Roc, and in about 3 hours on foot you go up to the royal hunting house of the Gran Piano.
The panorama of the plain up to Monte Rosa.

Civic Museum founded in 2010 at the foot of Monte Marrone, near the places where the Italian Liberation Corps was formed: over 900 square meters in ten rooms with uniforms, accessories and original weapons, a room with more than 200 types of weapons deactivated and external hangars with large military means and artillery, as well as library and rare war periodicals. Seasonal hours from Tuesday to Sunday, 10-13 and 16-20 in summer, 16-19 in winter.
A Walser village as it was.

The castle on the main square houses the Town Hall and is always open.It houses the reproduction of the Warrior of Capestrano, a limestone statue of Italian warrior over two meters high of the 6th century BC, found in 1934 and preserved at the National Archaeological Museum of Abruzzo in Chieti. From the view of the courtyard you can see Rocca Calascio.

In the middle of the sixteenth century, in a cave not far from the village, a Byzantine Madonna icon was found among the bushes; in 1577 Mgr. Cesare Bovio had the present single nave church built with three altars, and in the seventeenth century the icon was set on the central altar.

Documented from the early Middle Ages, the parish already in 1443; the façade bears the date 1651 and the inscription "P.F. 1685 , year of restoration financed by the Archconfraternity of the SS. Sacramento, with three-order bell tower and statues of Saints Peter and Paul. Three naves with barrel vaults; inside the Holy Family of the polycastrese painter Francesco Giordano, a San Sebastiano near the ways of Mattia Preti on the altar in polychrome marble, a Renaissance limestone waterworks, a Pietà in stone with traces of color and a nineteenth century choir of 24 stables.
A walled village with the house of Nino Manfredi.

The convent was founded in 1216 in the wake of the preaching of St. Francis; on the ground floor of the western side it houses the demoethanological Museum of Terracotta, dedicated to the craftsmanship of terracotta for which Fratte Rosa is known.

The ruins of the ancient Tusculum just outside the city, with the Roman theatre of 75 BC; a short distance from the Tuscolo Cross (677 m), with a view of the Castles and, on clear days, the Tyrrhenian Sea.

At the entrance of the cave, it traces the history of the cavity from the Neolithic, when the first visitors reached the most accessible part of it, at the nineteenth century of the birth of scientific and sports caving and of the first researches on the underground Timavo. Accessible and free; just outside the cave, in a short gorge, a small botanical garden with plants typical of the entrances of the karst chasms.
A white labyrinth overlooking the valley of Ofanto.
The art of the twentieth century in the city.

From Monte Celeste the village dominates the high valley of Sacco and preserves pre-Roman polygonal walls and the castle tower of the 13th century. In July, the re-enactment "Dies in Castro Olibani" celebrates the patron saint with medieval crafts and shows.
The medieval network of underground galleries that brought water to the city's sources, signalled by Terre di Siena among the places to visit.

Opened in 1991 on the second floor of Palazzo Forte: about 250 local ceramics from the 12th to the 21st century, to enhance the ancient folk majolica of Ariano, and finds from the 9th to the 15th century from the excavations along the ancient walls.

Lecci, roverelle, cork and chestnuts surround the village; the ancient paths of transhumance lead to the slopes of Mount Mungianeddu, to the valley of Bau 'e Fonne and to the woods of Sa Costa 'e Sili and Orovole. In the valley the rivers Tino and Torrei flow into Lake Taloro.
Frazione in the Sibillini National Park; its symbol is the church of Saints Peter and Paul, at the top of the village, with two naves with a Pietà painted in 1543.
Three towers of different eras and the view of the Ulysses Riviera.
The traces of Dertona in the urban fabric.

Five rooms in a historic building tell the Second World War from the point of view of civilians, crushed between Germans and allies during the battles of Cassino, with video testimonies, objects donated by families, documents, war finds and aerial photos of the RAF on the area of Mount Cairo granted by the National Aerophototheque. According to the MiC card is open Friday 15-18, Saturday 10-18 and Sunday 10-13, with reservation for schools and groups; the same card indicates both a ticket of 2 euros (free for residents) and a free offer of 10-13, while VisitLazio gives it to visit only by reservation.
The square of the Palio di Ferrara.
19th century architecture in the main square.
The most complete fossil shark of its kind and the prehistory of Lessinia.
Six hundred meters of pedestrian walk between cafes and shops, with the triangular square at the arrowpoint of the Lombard League.

The belt, almost four kilometers long, contained 107 hectares, a second extension only to that of Ugento. The excavations of 1986-1992 identified three concentric walls, the first before 300 BC; the best preserved stretch is the north-eastern one, about 840 meters long, with the north gate. Open-air archaeological area accessible to all.

Built between 1644 and 1665 for Giovanni Battista Giussani on a project attributed to Pellegrino Tibaldi, he then passed to the Mazenta, extinct in 1875, and finally to the Maggioni. Abandoned in the twentieth century, it has been recovered since 1988 and opened in 1998: it preserves the square courtyard system and the large internal porch with six groups of binated columns in pink granite and the staircase with marble balustrade. Today it is a civic hall for events, conferences and exhibitions.
Walking in the Ladin village between Puzzone and markets.
Sixteenth-century altar and rituals of Holy Week.
A neoclassical parish church frescoed in the heart of the country.

Karst resurgence at the foot of Mount Uddè, the most important Sardinian spring and natural monument since 1998: the water flows from a vertical rift with an average flow rate of about 500 liters per second, in shades from emerald green to blue; in 2010 it was explored up to 135 meters. It is observed from the terrace of the little church of Our Lady of the Pietà; around a forest of eucalyptuses.

Inaugurated in 2013 in front of the Paleolithic site of Valle Gimentina, among the most important in Abruzzo for the lower and middle Paleolithic (Radmilli excavations 1954-55, new research since 2012); six shelters in stone rebuilt tell the Neanderthals, the transhumant pastoral care, flora and fauna, with an outdoor workshop of splintering of the flint.
A walled village in concentric circles.

Also called San Francesco Vecchio, it was built in the fifteenth century and restored in the eighteenth century, with stuccoes and decorations.
The reserves of the Farma stream and the Upper Merse, suitable for outdoor activities and swimming in the streams.

Inaugurated in 1989 in the seventeenth-century Palazzo Volpi, one of the four locations of the Civic Museums: the pictorial and sculptural heritage of the city up to the twentieth century, futurism, rationalism and design.

Built between 1688 and 1698 and Basilica minor since 1961, monumental single nave with eight altars and entrance staircase: the main altar is Andrea Fantoni, the altarpiece of the Assumption of Sebastiano Ricci, other paintings by Carpinoni, Vicentino and Querena. The Basilica Museum has three oratories and eight rooms.

The village rises on an isolated hill below Mount Velino, with a wide view of the Palentine Fields; the writer Edward Lear described it. In the route between the churches of the capital, from the church of Saint Lucia, you will find the small church of Our Lady of Loreto, of the fourteenth century, with Marian frescoes, the convent and the church of Saint Dominic, of the fifteenth century, and the shrine of the fallen inaugurated in 1932.

Ancient cathedral built in the 12th century on pre-Roman structures, next to Palazzo Caetani, with façade "a vela" (sailing), in 1378 the antipope Clement VII was elected. Inside a Cosmatesque episcopal throne and, in the chapel of the Count, the Mausoleum Caetani supported by three female figures, a Majesty of Antoniazzo Romano and an Annunciation of Christopher Scacco with Saint Honored who holds the model of the castle of the late fifteenth century.
One of the oldest squares in the city, once a place of markets, on which the former Franciscan monastery of the thirteenth century faces, today a cultural space.

Villa Gambarini-Cagnola-Giavazzi, built as a family residence by Carlo Maria Gambarini in the French period (1797-1815). It passed by inheritance to Rosa Gambarini and her husband, the Milanese nobleman and deputy Giovanni Battista Cagnola, and in 1902 to Giovanni Javazzi and his sons; occupied by the Germans in the Second World War and then abandoned, it was bought by the Municipality in 1972 and since 1980, after the restoration, it is the seat of the Town Hall. Free access to public opening hours.

The 16th-century castle, the heart of the village, houses the museum that tells the Bourbon del Monte family and its marquisate, imperial fief from 1250 to 1815, and the connection with the city and territory of the Tiber Valley. Recently the route has been enriched with an archaeological section with the findings of the territory.
One of the main squares, between shops and bars, where stands and markets are often held; in the center a fountain with three balls that recall the three patrons Alfio, Cirino and Filadelfo.

Building on three arches designed by Jesuit Leonardo Ximenes under Pietro Leopoldo of Lorraine for the reclamation of the Maremma, regulated the outflow of the swamp waters. It houses the Museum of the Diaccia Botrona Reserve, with documentaries, local models and a virtual hut to learn how to recognize birds in flight; from here start birdwatching and boat visits to the swamp.

Established in 2003 in the restored premises of a former 15th century prison, with the original grates: the geological section (2004) tells in an interactive way the history of the Madonie, from coral reefs to about 3000 years ago, with the Rock Library and Sala Salgemma; the archaeological section (2008) exhibits the Collisani Collection, with a room dedicated to the Grotto of the Vecchiuzzo, prehistoric site discovered by Antonio Collisani.

In the lower floors of the Baronial Palace of the Caetani, seat of the Municipality, is dedicated to the humanist and publisher Aldo Manuzio (1449-1515), born in Bassiano: three rooms with typographical machines follow the path "Fiume delle Scripture" on the evolution of writing, integrated with the historical traces of the halls and the prison, with space to the marginal writings local like those of the shepherds.

She teaches in black and white, the colors of the city, laid for Valentine's Day 2022 by the artist sorano Guido Gabriele: a couple who kisses, with the arm of the man who draws the course of the Liri and seven red points for the seven bridges of Sora.
Meadows and views over the Friuli hills.

View of the village and the valley.

The beach is linked to the life of fishermen, with cliffs overlooking the sea, coves and hills with paths among the pine forests.
The mosaic on the rationalist facade.
The palace started in 1548 by Cardinal Girolamo Capodiferro, with the painting and the famous perspective of Borromini.

Borgo della Tuscia on the heights above Lake Bolsena, dominated by Rocca Farnese, where Cardinal Alessandro Farnese was born in 1520; after the destruction of Castro (1649) became the capital of the Farnesian Duchy. In the Rocca the Prehistory Museum of Tuscia, in a collegiate village, churches and Renaissance doors.
The oldest Roman mill in Liguria.
The life of the fields in a rebuilt peasant house.

Built in 1330 on a Longobard castle donated in 1039 to the Abbey of Farfa, it is the Romanesque-Gothic monument in the most important terracotta of Offida, on a steep cliff. The three-nave crypt contains fourteenth-century frescoes by the Master of Offida with the stories of Saint Catherine of Alexandria and Saint Lucia; in the apse of the upper church prophets, musical angels and virgins of Ugolino di Vanne, and a Madonna with Child attributed to Vincenzo Pagani. Open Saturday and Sunday.
A network of tunnels develops under the village and is accessible from the basement of the castle.

Built in 1938 in the Botteghelle district, behind a small church documented in 1725 and now disappeared, where Salvatore Quasimodo was baptized by Francesco Maria di Francia; he preserves an ancient statue of the Madonna del Carmelo, a Saint Joseph and a canvas of the Madonna with the souls of Purgatory. On July 16th the procession, and the following Sunday the statue goes by boat on the sea of Roccalumera and Nice.
The most beautiful view of Vicenza.

Unspoilt nature valley that opens between the castles of Montelagello and Migliano.
The prehistoric plateau next to the caves.

Built from 1738 to 1742 at the behest of Carlo di Borbone as a summer residence, attracted by the excavations of Ercolano, on a project by Giovanni Antonio Medrano and Antonio Canevari, with interventions by Vanvitelli and Fuga; the main staircase was frescoed between 1743 and 1746. Sold in 1871 to the Province of Naples, since 1872 it hosts the Scuola Superiore di Agricoltura, today the Department of Agriculture of Federico II.

Didactic Museum on the Battle of Trasimeno of 217 BC, in which the Roman army was defeated by the Carthaginian troops of Hannibal: interactive stations, multimedia and a 4D cinema room with an eight-minute video reconstruction in 3D graphics and multisensory effects.
A church inside a Roman temple.

Founded in 1999 for the company's 50th anniversary by President Claudio Luti, in 2000 he won the Guggenheim Enterprise & Culture Prize as the best business museum. It is based in the Kartell factory, headquarters since 1967, designed by Anna Castelli Ferrieri and Ignazio Gardella and considered one of the most interesting examples of industrial architecture in Lombardy. The collections count over 8,000 objects, 5,000 drawings and 15,000 photographs; the permanent exhibition, on more than 2,000 square meters with Ferruccio Laviani's set-up and the care of Elisa Storace, goes from 1949 to the present, between car accessories, housewives, lamps and furnishings become icons of Italian design.
The sanctuary of the apparition of 1722.

The Duke of Milan Galeazzo Sforza had him built in 1476 on a previous Visconti fortress, entrusting the works to Ambrogio Ferrari and Danesio Mainerio, as hunting residence of the Milanese court, continued use with Ludovico il Moro. Rectangular plant of 80 x 108 meters, walls about 3,5 meters thick and 7.5 meters high up to the blackbirds, moat fed by the Codimonte Roggia, four corner towers connected by underground passages and two entrances with drawbridge and poster it still visible. In the sleeve and in the south-west tower there is the municipal library, with over 10,000 rare pieces between incunaboli and five hundred.

Small center of Sannio, called the village of the palaces, with a walled nucleus around the baronial palace, noble palaces houses including the birthplace of the Enlightenment Giuseppe Maria Galanti, the churches of Santa Croce and Santa Maria Assunta, and the passage of the Royal Tratturo Pescasseroli-Candela.
The sixteenth-century castle symbol of the Oltrepò.

The churches rebuilt after 1627: the Baroque sanctuary of the Madonna del Soccorso, the Romanesque façade of San Severino, the wooden choir and the four statues of Ambrogio Piazza in San Nicola, the marbles and gildings of the church of Pietà, and San Lorenzo delle Benedettine, stages of the guided tours in the city.

Founded at the beginning of the 12th century and rebuilt in the 18th century, it is among the best examples of Baroque Baroque of the Land of Bari: monumental façade, paintings by Palma il Giovane and Francesco De Mura and the Byzantine icon of Our Lady of the Madia (about 1280), which legend wants to come from the sea on beams then used for the roof. Open every day 8-12 and 16-20.30.

Fortress of the twelfth century on a rocky spur, with a polygonal plan with two cylindrical towers on opposite sides; it was protected by a double circle of walls, of which visible traces remain.

He tells in thematic rooms the culture, traditions and history of Mamoiada using the traditional clothes as a guiding thread: the life of men and women until the mid-Twentieth century, the social role, the moments of celebration and mourning. The main hall is dedicated to the crafts of the country. cumulative ticket with the Museum of Masks €6, reduced €4.
Mausolei tower of ancient age along the Via Tiburtina Valeria, a few steps from the Basilica Valvense di San Pelino.
A curiosity of rural architecture.

The house of Maria Tarditi, an elementary teacher who began writing at the age of seventy and is remembered as the last writer of the Langhe, is today a museum open to the public thanks to the publisher Araba Fenice; many of his novels are set in Monesiglio, where it also takes place in part "I Sansôssi" by Augusto Monti.
A country shrine of Byzantine rite worship, surrounded by about fifty cumbessias, the houses of pilgrims.
Climbing in the sun even in winter.
The ancient nucleus on the highest point of the town, at more than 800 meters, with the most significant testimonies of the past of the city and panoramic views.

It rises where until the thirteenth century there was the original nucleus of the town, today inside the cemetery of Palazzolo; according to tradition on this hill San Zeno, bishop of Verona in the fourth century, celebrated Mass for the population. Built probably around the Mille in Romanesque style, with Moorish fishbone stones, and damaged by the earthquake of 1117, it has only one nave and two apses, one of which housed the ancient baptismal font; inside frescoes partly dated around the Mille. Reopened after more than two years of restoration.
One of the oldest churches in the Upper Lario.

Cultural center of 5,600 square meters in a former chemical factory: it houses the Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Aurelio De Felice, the Archaeological Museum (17 rooms between pre-Roman and Roman age) and the Sergio Secci Theatre.
