Street of high and narrow houses overlooking the main palaces: Palazzo Miano-Pizzolo (XVII century) with balcony on sandstone shelves, Palazzo Garufi-Schipilliti renovated in 1771; in the surroundings Palazzo Mauro with arched porch, Palazzo Bondì with domed balcony and elliptical windows, the eighteenth-century houses of Via Roma and Casa Crisafulli-Gussio in Piazza Duomo, and the alley of the prisons with grate cells and underground shelters.

The Council Hall dedicated to Aligi Sassu preserves windows made by the artist with the master glassmaker Tito Toneguzzo of Monza. In one, the mathematician Gabrio Piola (1794-1850) is portrayed among moving numbers that break into colorful forms: Sassu recovers his futurist youthful passion.
It rises where the ancient gate of the castle was; its bell, known since 1487, is called "the bell of reason."

Portici along Via Umberto I and Piazza Palazzo Civico, the Palazzo del Comune restored, three fourteenth-century palaces of the Princes of Acaja, the eighteenth-century Palazzo Sillano, Palazzo Baudi di Selve and the building of Via Umberto I, administrative seat of the assets of the Acaja in the fourteenth century and modified by the seventeenth century; in the former hospital, now a retirement home, a loggia of the fourteenth century.

Built in 1580, in the middle of the Counter-Reformation, about 600 m of altitude between woods and cultivated fields; according to the tradition in August, in mature wheat, it snowed and the Madonna appeared where the sanctuary stands today. The bell tower, very rare in Langa, has the shape of the papal triregno with three concentric crowns.
Baroque church of 1733 next to the Commenda, with the dome frescoed by Matthäus Günther.

Villa Curti, in the historic nucleus, was Bissari since the end of the fifteenth century and Curti since 1870; Villa Marzotto-Schiavo in San Daniele is a building of the seventeenth century with a side portico of the nineteenth century; Villa Civena in Contrà Garibaldo brings the date 1592 and has a dove with spiral staircase.
The Forest of Violins and Deer.
The mountains of Valsesia.
One of the last stretches of Adriatic coast without construction.

Former military village of the early twentieth century on the west side of Caprera, today the only inhabited center of the island and seat of the environmental education center of the park; the mineralogical-naturalistic museum exposes the rocks of the archipelago, the sands of the beaches of Caprera, fossils and fragments of meteorites.

Residence of the Torelli and then of the Gonzaga, which hosted Torquato Tasso and Guercino: rebuilt by Francesco Capriani called the Volterra and Tommaso Filippi, with decorations by Bernardino Campi, was completed around 1570. It houses the City Museum with the Maldotti Quadreria, about fifty works including Luca Ferrari, Marcantonio Franceschini, Giuseppe Bazzani, a watercolor of Hayez and an oil of De Nittis, and temporary exhibitions. Borgo on a hill of tuff overlooking Lake Bolsena, dominated by the sixteenth-century Palazzo Farnese di Antonio da Sangallo il Giovane, which houses the Museum of Farnesian Costume; in the historic center the Collegiate Church of Santa Maria Maddalena with its museum of sacred art. Land of Aleatico and Grechetto DOC wines and of the "Lunch of Purgatory" on Ash Wednesday.

In the hamlet Trisungo remains a testimony of the ancient via Salaria, with a milestone of the first century BC. The last weekend of October hosts the festival "Marrone che passione" .

Six domus de janas of the final Neolithic (about 3200-2800 BC) excavated in a single granite outcrop between philirea and cork oaks. The tomb I, the most articulated, has anticell, central chamber and two secondary environments; the IV keeps a counter and traces of two semi-colons. Outside a false door carved on a rock and on top a block that was probably an altar.
Long sandy beaches with the pine forest behind them.
A walk through monumental trees in the center.

Four thematic itineraries: the Trail of the Acciugai, on the routes of the typical trade of Celle; the Trail of the Alpine Construction, between the villages with the "casseforti" , sailing buildings rich in carved stones; the Trail of the Faith, dotted with votive pylons; the Trail of the Giants, in a wood of secular larch in the hamlet Ramei. The territory is also crossed by the Great Crossing of the Alps and the Occitani Routes, with a path beyond the pastures of Mount Tibert towards Castelmagno.

The collection is housed in the Gonzaghesque Civic Tower, a rare example of a tower with three masonry sides and one open, with an eighteenth-century annex and an exhibition hall. Born at the end of the seventies on the initiative of fans linked to the Pro Loco and donated to the Municipality in 1995, it brings together paintings, prints, graphics and sculptures mainly of Mantua artists from the early twentieth century to today, including Alessandro Dal Prato, Arturo Cavicchini, Giuseppe Lucchini and Mimì Buzzacchi Quilici, and hosts temporary exhibitions. Open Monday, Wednesday and Thursday 15-18.30, Friday 9-12.30 and 15-18.30, Sunday 9-12.30 and 15-19 (Sunday by reservation, except the first of the month); free entry and guided tours, accessible route.
The partisan story of the Ossola told by who lived it.

Inaugurated in 2023 in the castle: on the ground floor the history of the territory with the findings of the preventive excavations (including those for high speed), in the former stables the accessories of Acerrae from the fourth century BC to the Roman age, a room on prehistory and one on Suessula, flourishing from the IX century BC and abandoned after the Middle Ages.

Borgo on the eastern shore of Lake Como, already inhabited in pre-Roman and imperial times, with the churches of Santa Tecla and San Giovanni, the sixteenth-century Villa Pliniana anchored to the rock and, on the mountains, the avelli dug in erratic boulders and the Pietra Pendula of Montepiatto along the Strada Regia.

Last village of the Val d'Asta, 1053 meters at the foot of Mount Cusna: in winter skiing facilities, in summer base for hiking, mountain biking and horse riding; the chairlift Febbio 2000 works in both seasons.
In the building of the ancient factory of Corso Cento Cannoni, tells the story of the hat manufacture founded in 1857 and the culture of the Italian hat.

Fraction with the sanctuary of the Madonna della Neve, the late Baroque parish, a sixteenth-century oratory and numerous chapels surrounded by greenery; in the historic center passes one of the paths of the museum "Strade di pietra" .

Country of the lower Brescia on the river Churches, with two civic museums flanked in Via Cappellazzi: the archaeological, set up in the former frescoed church of the Disciplines, and the Museum of Churches and peasant civilization.

Baths, mud and inhalations on medical prescription, also in agreement with the Health Service; wellness treatments on reservation. Casa-torre of the 13th century of the Cappello family, the Capulet of the legend: the hall covered with love cards, the courtyard with balcony and statue of Juliet by Nereo Costantini, the interior with furnishings and costumes of the film by Zeffirelli.

More than 1,400 hectares of forest in the Regional Park of the Roman Castles, frequented by hikers, mountain bikers and knights; in the woods there are the Via Sacra and a necropolis with cave tombs of the Bronze Age.
In the Church of Mercy, he exhibits the casts of the hand and face of the emperor and tells his interests for books and theater.

Italian garden designed by Diomede Leoni in the sixteenth century, on two levels along the ancient bastions, with the statue of Cosimo III de' Medici (1688) and a rose garden; in summer it hosts the sculpture exhibition "Forms in the Green."
Giulio Romano also in the cathedral.
Two historic cafés in the square: the legendary Caffè degli Specchi and the Tommaseo, the Trieste restaurant which has been open continuously for more time.

Borgo in the woods, mentioned already in 1350 and recently restored, dominated by the castle with the tower of the early thirteenth century and surrounded by medieval walls. In the square the church of Santa Maria Maddalena, rebuilt between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and the statue of the Archangel Michele carved in 1937 by Michele Perla.
A pedestrian path of 2 km along the Via Sacra with 14 chapels to the sanctuary, UNESCO heritage.

To the north-west of Apricena, on the edge of the Murge, the monastery was founded in 1050 by Petronio, Count of Lesina; passed from the Benedictines to the Celestines in the early 1280s, in 1294 Celestine V united Holy Spirit of Sulmona. Abandoned after the transfer of the Celestines to San Severo, it was the destination of pilgrimages to the Madonna della Rocca until the twentieth century. Of the Latin cross church with apse aisle remain fragments of frescoes and the remains of wells, fish ponds and walls of the belt.

Country of the Astigian hills, in whose territory rises the canonical of Santa Maria di Vezzolano, considered the most important Romanesque monument of Piedmont; from the Belvedere Motta, the highest point of the village, the view ranges to 360 degrees on the hills, and towards Berzano there is the Romanesque San Pietro di Fenestrella.

The church of Santa Maria Assunta was probably built in 1201 on a previous Lombard church; the castle remains a gateway and some defensive structures, including the fortress on top of the hill, and the old town hall has the coat of arms of Bridge on the portal.

12th century village on a strategic hill, known for its cylindrical tower, in the DOC Colli di Luni wine area.
A coastal town between the mouths of Tronto and Salinello, the first Abruzzo beach, which grew around the sixteenth-century Torre di Carlo V which today houses the Antiquarium of Castrum Truentinum.

Built several times in the 19th century in the center, it has neoclassical façade facing the west. The interior with a single nave has five side altars in marble, wooden sculptures (Holy Family, St. Joseph with Child, Sacred Heart of Jesus), paintings by the Scridian painter Giuseppe Barchitta (1874-1959), including the Madonna of the Lost, two frescoes by Giuseppe Barone on the vault and a large wooden Crucifix in the apse. On March 19, the feast of the saint opens with the parade of barred horses.
Low sea for families and pine forest.

It was quoted in a document dated 1096, named after the Pignatelli; little remains of its original appearance, because the families that possessed it adapted it to the defense. The current appearance derives from the restorations after the earthquake of 1456 and from the Carafa, feudal for over three hundred years: the arch of access to the courtyard is from 1505, the ramparts of the eighteenth century, and preserves walls and a cylindrical tower. It houses the multimedia museum with vintage photographs and testimonies of local culture; visit by reservation.
The Simone Martini of Calabria.

It tells the story of Satrianum from the Bronze Age to the destruction in 1420, with finds from the V-III century B.C. from a shrine and necropolis (ex-vote, weapons, imported ceramics and locals) and medieval majolica ceramics; open on request.
the MiC card "Antiquarium comunale di Agropoli" has the same address (via Carlo Pisacane) but has not been opened: identity with the new archaeological museum to be confirmed
See the only coin of King Ariperto I known in Italy.

Baroque Lombard style building: the façade has an entrance portal, a balcony with wrought iron balustrade and, on the second floor, two windows decorated with shell motifs.

Go up 330 steps from the station to the basilica through Porta Marina, with fifteen newsstands designed by Amerigo Staffolani in 1942 and bronze panels of the Rosary Mysteries merged in 1895 by Guarino Roscioli; on top, under the balcony of Piazzale Giovanni Paolo II, a wooden crucifix with a view to the sea.

A mountain village in Valnerina with four medieval gates and three walls, the Clock Tower and the San Francesco complex, under which is displayed the copy of the Etruscan Biga of the 6th century BC found in 1902 at the Colle del Capitano and today at the Metropolitan Museum in New York.
The relics of the miracle of 1273.
A unique museum on the trot.
The park along the rivers Tordino and Vezzola, indicated by the Abruzzo Region for outdoor walks.

A small town on the Lombard shore of Lake Maggiore, with a lakefront of about 2 km shaded by plane trees, the old port and a historic center of shops and palaces; to see the church of Carmine of the fifteenth century, the great international station nineteenth century and, on Wednesday, the historic market.
A symbol of the troubled city. The donkey (1109-1119) is 97.20 m high; the Garisenda, lower and inclined, is not visited inside.
Built in the seventeenth century near the castle, it preserves on the main altar a wooden ancone of Gaspare Serra dated 1738.
The ruins in the heart of the old town.
Borgo at the gates of Saluzzo dominated by the castle of Saluzzo della Manta, well FAI with one of the most extraordinary profane pictorial cycles in Europe.
Nizzoli's liberty in town hall.

A 17 km walk along the track of the mine railway, which runs from 1872 to 1928, connecting Casino di Terra with the station of Villetta, where lignite was loaded. From the municipal territory you can also walk to the village of Miemo with the route   ... between the giants of the wind and the giants of the woods, that crosses the Wind Park.

The ancient Hasta Pompeia, the city of the hundred towers on the Via Francigena, the Palio and the sparkling wine: the Troyan Tower, the Collegiate Church of San Secondo, the cathedral in terracotta and the birthplace of Vittorio Alfieri.

The Morrutto (broken wall) is the oldest part of the country, a maze of homes of the year Mille built with poor materials and strong defensive asymmetries, some above underground caves; the walls with three doors and the abbey palace with the coat of arms of Cardinal Vincenzo Maria Orsini, then Pope Benedict XIII.

One of the two oldest gardens and the four main parks of Catania, green lung at the bottom of Via Etnea with driveways, busts of illustrious men and floral compositions; the people called it "Laberinto."

Country of the plain under Cividale, feud of the chapter of the Duomo already in 1192: villa de Claricini Dornpacher with the collections of the family, the Italian garden and the park, the Palladian villa de Puppi and the fourteenth-century church of San Giovanni Battista.

Working mill in the area of Pezol, of the Rizzi family (Salin) from the nineteenth century: two millstones for barley, an oil mill, a pestle with vertical motion and a windmill. Restored by Giuseppe Longo and opened in 1983, it was the first section on the territory of the Ladin Museum.
From the tower you can see the lakes of Chiusi and Montepulciano.
Waterfalls and porches in the beech forest of Nero.
The statue of the patron of Pietro Bernini.

The heart of the city in front of the Duomo, with the statue of the Neptune called the Giant, left unfinished by Baccio Bandinelli and mounted in 1563 by Alberico I in a fountain with two dolphins; on the corner with Via Finelli a plaque recalls the stays of Michelangelo came to choose the marble.

One of the most important Etruscan cities, Romanized at the end of the III century BC and abandoned in the Middle Ages: large stretches of walls, the Roman city, a small amphitheatre and the thermal baths.
A fortress camouflaged in granite, with views up to Corsica.

Built at the beginning of the nineteenth century by the Marquis Boyl on the site of a noble house of the fourteenth century, it is a neoclassical building with Pompeian red facade and entrance gallery; Carlo Felice, Carlo Alberto, Grazia Deledda, D'Annunzio and Balzac stayed there (1838). It houses a cultural center with a small art gallery and the museum of costume and Sardinian jewelry: fabrics, clothes and jewels that show the evolution of the costume in the last two centuries.
The village enclosed in its walls, intact.
