The valley between Italy and France with the cromlech of the Salassi, which at the summer solstice lights up with games of light, the Roman remains of the mansio, the via delle Gallie, a small temple and a column at Jupiter, united by the easy Path of Memory.
The green of Celius.

Medieval village on the slopes of Monte Croce di Serra, with a castle and a double wall of the 12th century; in the territory the large Umbrian-Etruscan necropolis of the Vallone di San Lorenzo, whose finds are at the Antiquarium of Palazzo Ancajani in Tenaglie, and the castle of Melezzole.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione del Monferrato casalese, between the castle with hanging gardens, the infernot and the industrial memory of lime and cement.

Walk in the ancient village: the pear of about 300 years of Piazza Suspize, the sundials with Latin mottos of the houses Allemand and Ambrois, the chapel of the Madonna delle Grazie (1712), the chapel of San Rocco of the vote after the plague of 1630 and Casa Pellerin with the gate of 1555.
Just outside the city, the church with a small temple in polychrome marble of Sansovino.

Images, tools and testimonials of the granite stonemasons Sanfedelino, which takes its name from the first open quarry next to the Sanctuary of San Fedele and paved streets and squares of Milan, Como, Pavia and Bologna: in the five years before the Great War, more than 82,000 tons of stone left the station of Novate, and between the twenties and thirty the quarries were twenty; today one remains active. Open a few days a week; guided tours by reservation.

The collections of Baron Enrico Pirajno of Mandralisca: art gallery, archaeology, coins, one of the richest collections of shells in Europe and the Portrait of Man by Antonello da Messina (1460-1470).
The country's defenses.
An ancient village of cave houses, houses dug into the typical rock of the Mediterranean, which probably date back to the Neolithic age, if not to the upper Paleolithic.
Val Tidone on foot or by bike.
Village walled on the hill of Cerruglio, among the vineyards of the Wine Route of the Lucca Hills and Montecarlo.

Established in 1996 between Roccastrada and Monticiano, on the border between the provinces of Siena and Grosseto: in the valley bottom beech, maples, birch and badgers, on the slopes north chestnuts and cork; live marten, skunk, wild cat and two species of bats. Along the Ferriere path you will find the Ferriera Mill, in the middle of the thirteenth century and well preserved.
The other Peschiera, the Austrian barracks.

The hilly village of Aurorno and Roman origins on the border with Campania, above the sea hamlets of Scauri and Marina di Minturno; on the Garigliano you can visit the Roman colony of Minturnae, crossed by the Appia and part of the UNESCO site Via Appia. Regina Viarum and Ponte Real Ferdinando, the first iron chain bridge in Italy (1832).

The village of the upper Trompia Valley is about 1000 meters away, crossed by the Bavorgo stream, with the seventeenth-century town hall and the 18th-century parish church of the Saints Nazarius and Celsus; it is known for the iron mine of Sant'Aloisio, today's museum and adventure park, the Romanesque church of San Rocco and the Maniva Pass area.
A late 18th century villa with a large English park in the center.
Medieval plant centre with Palazzo Vannicelli, now seat of the Municipality, and the Bishop's Palace of 1593; the main monuments have information panels with QR code.
The Gothic of the village.

15th-century residence built for Maytinus Roncalli, ancestor of the pope, who chose it as summer residence until shortly before the election; on the façade a sundial with the motto "Errantes revocotat" and inside fifteenth-century frescoes with the coat of arms of the Maytini, then became papal coat of arms. Today it is a museum with relics: part of the library, gifts, the typewriter and the world map of the papal study, the bed in which he died and the altar of the private chapel, works of Manzù, Scorzelli, Bodini, Manfredi and German Nani and an Opel Kapitan of 1956. Open on Saturday and Sunday, 9-12 and 14-18.
A small museum of primitive Tuscans.
Stone and crystal greenhouse in the Garzoni garden with over a thousand species of butterflies from all over the world.
The Friuli that left for the world, told by whom he left.
In Salino, on the road to Paularo, the waterfall is just past the village, behind a curve.
The remains of the Swabian fortress over the country.
Museum dedicated to engines and cars, which renews the exhibition every six months, in spring and autumn, with always different themes related to the car.
The fortress extended on a rock spur, rebuilt in 1570 with the Museum of Montanara Civilization and the Museum of Mechanical Musical Instruments.
The regional park with the peak of 1945 meters, the ski resort and the ridge lake.
Dora herons.
The panoramic ascent above the Catholic.

Museum dedicated to the Marshal Pietro Badoglio, born in Grazzano, managed by the Cultural Centre Pietro Badoglio (a voluntary association established in 1991), who expanded its collections and rearranged it in 2001. Since December 2000 the Centre has also set up, in a hall of the former kindergarten, the permanent exhibition "L'Italia dei governamenti di guerra" (Italy of war governments).
It preserves a wooden Christ of the fifteenth century.
The village turns on foot in no time.
A signed Venetian gold fund.
It preserves the majestic Decollation of the Baptist of Anton Maria Maragliano and the Baptism of Jesus.
A stone village under the Little Horn.

The castle of Jugo is documented since 1191; in 1503, Cesare Borgia had its defenses dismantled and the sixteenth-century palace, initiated by the Farnese, was completed by Mattei, who bought it in 1597 and became dukes by the will of Urban VIII. It has five floors, corner towers, 365 windows and a helical ramp that can be crossed by carriages going up to a loggia on the Tiber Valley; the halls have mythological ceilings attributed to the schools of Domenichino, Veronese and Orazio Alfani.
Founded in 1997 and renovated in 2007 in the City Hall, it exhibits works by MAACK artists and donations, a collection of 114 works including paintings, installations and sculptures.
An ancient village under the cliff.
The view of the Gulf of Naples.

In the house next to the church of the Madonna degli Angeli, it offers a path of memory with the faithful reconstruction of domestic environments of the past: a house from the beginning of the twentieth century. Open on Sundays from 3 pm to 5 pm or on reservation (tel. +39 0174 391101).
A palace to discover during the exhibitions.
The Gothic church in the historic centre, overlooking Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, with a polychrome terracotta Pietà from the 15th century in the chapel on the left.

The second island of Calabria by extension, in the Regional Marine Park of the Cedars: limestone outcrop covered with Mediterranean scrub, with caves, coves and cliffs, seabeds with Posidonia oceanica and Pinna nobilis. At the top of the remains of the sighting tower, dated to the ninth century. You can catch up by boat.
Two hundred ancient instruments.

Country of the Colline Novaresi about 24 km north of Novara, among horse pastures and vineyards of the Colline Novaresi DOC. To see the ancient Pieve di San Genesio, documented since 1132, the center with the eighteenth-century parish and the nineteenth-century castle, the astronomical observatory Galileo Galilei and the Ring of the Horses.

Protected wetland, already Lake Perotto, managed by Legambiente and WWF: it hosts rare and threatened species such as the butterfly Lycaena dispar and birds like heron ash, folaga, water chicken, pig, swamp falcon (nidifying) and tarabusino; in early autumn there are large numbers of swallows before migration.
The country that reads the hour on the walls.
Throat, rock and memory of the plague.
The Rodari Portal and the White Dance Macabra.
The large iron bridge over the Po, symbol of the meeting between Ticino and Po.
the source indicates closed access paths for jobs and remains largely unvisitable in safety
Liberty on the cliff.

The Gothic Cathedral from the bell tower considered one of the most beautiful in the region, seat of the diocese of Bolzano-Bressanone since 1964, with the pulpit in sandstone, the frescoes of the Chapel of the Graces and the decorated roof restored in 2009.
Our Lady venerated next to Porta Garibaldi.

A village at 470 metres in the Sibillini Mountains National Park, feud of Camerino in the Middle Ages; in the capital the Pieve di Santa Maria Assunta with the art gallery and the former convent of Sant'Agostino with the Museo della Nostra Terra, while the Water Trail leads to the waterfalls of Sant'Angelo and the mill of Rijeka.

In Caleno, Pignataro Maggiore houses a small civic museum dedicated to tools and tools of peasant and artisan life and, in Piazza Umberto I, the church of Santa Maria della Misericordia, decorated with stucco; on the hill towards San Pasquale remain the ruins of Castellone dei Ranallo.

A former Franciscan convent that the tradition ties to the passage of St. Francis in 1220; after the suppression of the convents decreed by Giuseppe Bonaparte in 1807 it became a national boarding house, attended from 1821 to 1827 by Luigi Settembrini, who later named it at Giordano Bruno. Portale in piperno of 1758; in the living room the ceiling houses the largest canvas in the world (700 sq m), painted in 1756 by Giovanni Funaro and workshop with the Immaculate Conception, St. Francis and St. Anthony within architectural squares. In the adjacent church of Sant'Antonio da Padova, on the sides of the marble altar, two angels, head of the altar by Giuseppe Sammartino (1761).
Mon closed · Mar-ven 10-16 · sab-dom-festive 10-18
At about 10 km, ancient medieval fortress of which the walls remain, a tower used as a bell tower and the parish built in place of the castle.
360° view of Mugello and the Apennines.
Walk through the palaces of the medieval village.

17th century villa with frescoed rooms, today municipal. The formal Italian garden of Silva, known from the engravings of Marc'Antonio Dal Re (1726), was transformed at the end of the eighteenth century by Ercole Silva into one of the first landscape parks in English in Italy; Silva theorized its model in the treatise        • Of the art of English gardens • (1801). The park, about 5,44 hectares open to the public and almost intact, preserves obelisk, neoclassical exedra dedicated to Health, Scottish lodges, Swiss chalet of the 19th century and a sarcophagus cover with the inscription "Et in Arcadia ego"; in the courtyard of honor there is a monumental magnolia with sinuous trunks.

Church of late-Gothic forms whose façade is decorated by the twentieth-century graffiti by Costantino Nivola. In the village also the seventeenth-century St. John the Baptist, with a wooden pulpit carved with a Franciscan symbol, and the church of the Rosary, with frescoes.
The Romanesque Cluniac in the woods.
The neighborhood is outside the walls.
The seabed of the marine area up close.
The Renaissance on the lake.
The first century AD, with the axis greater than 65 meters and more than 10,000 places, of which some parts remain.

Ancient village on a spur of the Serra, which is accessed by a medieval town gate; next to a viewpoint on the Biellese stands the church of Santa Maria Assunta, with the wooden pulpit of 1712, and the village houses the Museo Laboratorio dell'Oro and the Pietra dell'Ecomuseo del Biellese.
An architecture of Sangallo in a small village.
Nineteenth-century farmhouse built on a private Roman thermal bath, with Roman and late antique materials including the statue of Togato and a tub in Chio's breach.

Small lake born from an ancient clay quarry, immersed in the vegetation of the Groane Park and the Briantea Brughiera; in summer the water lilies bloom, many species of birds are observed and you can fish. From the lake start paths between oaks, pine forests and moors.
Car access to the Auronzo Refuge only with reservation (dreizinnen.com)

In the former convent of the Capuchins of the seventeenth century, with the adjoining church of San Francesco used as auditorium, eleven rooms tell Morgantina from the Bronze Age to the Roman-Republican era: ceramics of the Morgets, the Serra Orlando room with busts of Persephone and ex-vote, the silvers of Morgantina and the acrolites of Demeter and Kore. The symbol piece is the goddess of Morgantina (425-400 BC, 2,24 m high, face and arms in Paro marble), passed by J. P. Getty Museum of Malibu and returned; also exposed the head of Hades ...Barbablu's terracotta polychrome.

Permanent exposure of locomobili and tractors Landini with hot head, motorbikes of the thirties, forty and fifty and four-stroke mopeds, restored according to the original tradition; stands out the series of Slanzi engines. Visits on request (tel. 0522 669858).
In the hamlet of Pieve, the ruins of the Roman city of Septempeda.
The oldest church, with late-medieval frescoes.

From 2005 the church of Santa Maria degli Angeli houses the Parish Museum of Sacred Furniture, with sacred paintings from the fifteenth century to the beginning of the seventeenth century: five small tables of the late fourteenth century with stories of the Virgin, a Flemish triptych of the sixteenth century and the Madonna dell'Accomandata by Antonello Freri (1510).
MiC card (updated to February 2021) is closed every day

Borgo grew up around the castle that the Ferretti family built from the fourteenth century; near the manor, in the area of the cemetery, the church of Santa Maria della Misericordia preserves frescoes from the fifteenth century.

Country of the lower valley of Coghinas, in Anglona, a few minutes from the Gulf of Asinara: the Archaeological Museum with about 80 Roman funerary stele, the sanctuary and necropolis of San Leonardo, the park of Monte San Giovanni and the summit of San Gavino.
Medieval village, on the Tiber Valley, Orange Flag since 2025, along the ancient Amerina street.
Rationalist building of 1935 at the mouth of the river Albula, on the promenade.
Remains of the Roman amphitheatre in the eastern part of the city, of which the ancient town hall, which had this title in '89 BC, also preserves the hole under the square and sections of the walls.
Medieval village born on the Roman road of the Gallie, among the terraced vineyards of the first DOC wine of the Valle d'Aosta.
€5, reduced €3 (13-18 years)

Housed in the noble Palazzo Torrusio of the eighteenth century, it is described as the first and most articulated ethnographic museum of the interior Cilento: over a thousand objects from the seventeenth to the twentieth century, born also from the work of the local elementary schools, in domestic, historical, arts and crafts, textiles, weights and measurements, olive growing, wine, cereals and religion (the latter in the nearby church of San Bartolomeo). The main piece is the base of a sandstone wine press with symbolic engravings, found in Pellare in 1978. Part of the Municipal Museum Pole founded in 2016, open from Tuesday to Sunday 9-18, closed on Monday; recommended reservation, mandatory for groups.

Small church with the characteristics of a castle chapel inside the medieval village, probably of the XIII-XIV centuries, with the curious entrance wall curved to the apse: the legend wants Giulia Farnese to do so to reach it directly from the castle. It was the seat of the Confraternity of the Disciplined; a unique hall with wooden trusses and an eighteenth-century canvas of the Martyrdom of Saint Lucia. Restored in 2006.
The Longobard village on the hill.
The school of sculptors of Viggiu in the twentieth century.
Comfortable Riva for a stop.
The town along the sea.
Civic museum housed in the medieval castle of Via Lo Pizzo, with free entrance. Open from Monday to Friday, 8-14 and 15.30-18.30, with times that vary according to the season.

Born from the excavations of preventive archaeology for the high-speed line Turin-Milan (2001-2003), which brought to light the Roman necropolis of Livorno Ferraris (I-IV century A.D.). In a corridor and four halls exhibits local funeral equipment and materials from Balocco, from the necropolis of Crescentino and Motta de' Conti; it is the result of the collaboration between Superintendence, Municipality and Royal Museums of Turin. Open Wednesday and Saturday 9.30-11.30, other days by reservation; cumulative with the Ferraris Museum €5.
Abella's graves.

The parish church was among the richest in art in the diocese of Treviso when the air trumpet of July 24, 1930 destroyed it; the new church, large and sober, was designed by architect F. Shield to welcome the recovered works. It preserves the dossal of the main altar of Giorgio Massari, coming from the demolished Certosa del Montello, and six large canvases with stories of Moses by Giannantonio and Francesco Guardi and Francesco Fontebasso, restored by the Cassamarca Foundation.
Artificial lakes with sandy beach, Mediterranean maquis and marina.

The ancient Nomentum, then castle of the Crescenzi, the Orsini and the Borghese, linked to the battle of 3 November 1867 between the Garibaldi and the papal and French troops: the Garibaldi museum, the Park of the Remembrance with the altar-bone, the MuCaM archaeological museum and the medieval village with the Borghese Palace and Palazzo Crescenzi.
€6, reduced €3 (guided tour)
The altar attributed to Juvarra in a neoclassical parish.

Marino DOP wine was already known to the Roman patricians of Colli Albani; the donuts with must, with local must, extra virgin olive oil and raisins, follow a recipe of the seventeenth century and have their feast on the third Sunday of October. Other specialties: honey and chocolate mustaccioli and bride cookies, for sale in the shops of the historic center.
A village of probably Etruscan origins on the Via Francigena, in the heart of the UNESCO Valley, with the thermal hamlet of Bagno Vignoni.

The belt rebuilt after 1541 by order of Pedro de Toledo with five pentagonal bulwarks (Don Pedro, Toledo, Marquis, Villafranca, Pedro Nigro) and two rivets, the Bastione del Fosso with date 1550 and the Bunny of 1595.
Our Lady returned from slavery.

Alpine lake in the shape of a heart at the foot of Monte Coglians, reached by the Tolazzi Refuge (hill fraction) with dirt road and CAI 144 path: almost two hours and about 600 meters of altitude difference. On the opposite shores, two refuges, the Austrian Pichlhütte and the Italian Lambertenghi-Romanin, reminiscent of two lieutenants of the Great War.

The first settlement was founded by Giorgio Santacroce in 1560 according to a planned plant; the Altieri took control of the village in the seventeenth century. The ancient Via Clodia is a wide avenue with commercial activities.

karst coast overlooking the Adriatic between Trieste and Monfalcone: the castle of the princes of the Tower and Tasso where Rilke wrote the Dunean Elegies, the white cliffs, the bay of Sistiana and the Risorgive of Timavo with the mitreum and the Roman villa.
Getting lost in the alleys of the medieval Gaeta.

Piazza XX Settembre is the large stone space at the entrance of the center, where the elderly find themselves in the shade; Corso Vittorio Emanuele, called "U'ring" or "Ringo" is the main road and the best way to enter the centre, because the main attractions of the Baroque noble palaces overlook it.

Fortified dam, the long bridge, built from 1393 to 1395 for Gian Galeazzo Visconti: 650 meters long and 25 meters wide, connected to the Scaliger Castle by two high crenellated curtains, formed with it the Serraglio, the defensive system of the Scaligero on the Mincio.

Built in the 13th century by the counts of Appiano as a residential castle, today it is a restored ruin; the mast can be climbed and offers views of the Oltradige, to Bolzano and the Adige valley. There is a tavern of the castle; you reach it on foot, last stretch on steep asphalt road.

The palace designed by Buontalenti, residence of Medici, Lorraine and Savoy, with furnishings, paintings, armor and tapestries from the Six to the Nineteenth Century; from the Galileo tower looked at the sky.
The treasures of the hypogei dauni.
The church of the pilgrims at the foot of the wall of the Sas dla Crusc.

Liberty villa with medieval-inspired decorations, once home to noble Genoese families and now home to the Town Hall, surrounded by a large park where the Mediterranean flora joins exotic plants, cedars of Lebanon and centuries-old trees; along the avenues iron greenhouses in Art Nouveau style, and peacocks live free all year round.
The ancient village above the sea town.
The baroque cathedral of the city.
The Certosa on Mount Pisano, a stage recommended by Visit Tuscany in the Terre di Pisa.

In the 14th century Cassero, a tower on three levels of the walls wanted by the Florentines in 1328, the municipal museum of Italian sculpture of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries collects from donations more than 2,500 works among bronze, marble, plasters, terracotta and drawings, with artists such as Temo Bortolotti, Arturo Stagliano, Valmore Gemignani and the local Ernesto Galeffi.
Lake, wind and water sports.

Founded in 1008 with a donation from Bishop Landolfo II, it became parish in 1299; rebuilt between 1734 and 1739 and consecrated in 1743, it has frescoes by Angelo Trainini in 1919 and a cloister restored in 2001.
A walk through the nativity painted on the walls.
The collections of Cardinal Giulio Alberoni with the Ecce Homo by Antonello da Messina, the diptych by Jan Provost and the tapestries.
Romanesque building with circular plan of the 11th century, with works by Romanino, Moretto and Cossali.
The frescoed halls of the ancient capital.

XV century cathedral with two bell towers identical to the sides of the façade, center of devotion to Saint Venus; in the floor of the transept runs a marble sundial with twelve zodiac signs, work of the Danish astronomer Peters.

Church wanted in the early seventeenth century by Prince Branciforte and his wife Joan of Austria, nephew of Charles V, next to the Benedictine monastery, indicated as the third for importance of Sicily; has sumptuous altars in polychrome marble and there is buried Francesco Branciforte.
Stone and frescoes.
An evening at theater downtown.
The peasant life of the valley between ovens and oil tools.

The large brick building of the former Augustinian convent (1338-1441), houses the relics of the Eucharistic miracle of Lanciano in 1273, arrived at Offida in 1280; part of the host is preserved in a fourteenth-century gold-plated silver cross of a Venetian goldsmith. The relics are exhibited on May 3rd; open Saturday and Sunday.
The black and white heart of Catania.
A short stop for a 17th century fresco.
The churches and palaces of the village born from the ashes of Norba.

The highest part of Talla, a medieval village with a small church and a row of narrow and leaning houses; here the small fortress from which the Ubertini ruled the area until 1384, when Arezzo finally submitted to Florence.
cave temporarily closed for extraordinary maintenance (Regional direction Musei Lazio)
A curious symbol of the local memory.
Sanctuary entrusted to the Franciscan friars, in the upper part of the village.

Late-Gothic, designed by Filippo delle Vacche with first stone laid on October 7, 1453 on the site of a pagan temple and the parish church of Santa Maria. It preserves the polyptych of Paolo Veneziano, two paintings by Romanino, works by Moretto, Zenone Veronese, Palma il Giovane, Andrea Celesti and Angelo Landi, the chapel of the Most Holy decorated by Malosso and an ancient wooden crucifix by Giovanni Teutonico. In July, the concerts of the Summer Musicale are held on the churchyard.
A church that the Municipality defines as a museum of itself.
A sculpture that frames the village and the mountain.
Woods and hills just a step from the Riviera del Conero.

The municipality is 40 metres above sea level in the Salento area of Tarantino, overlooking the Gulf of Taranto with about 8 km of coast between cliffs and sandy coves, from Luogovivo to Lido Silvana. In the historic center the Castle de Falconibus, enlarged in 1435, and the church of Santa Maria La Nova; in the necropolis territory and remains of villages of the fourteenth century BC, unique traces of the Bronze Age so far discovered in the Gulf of Taranto.
In the church of Santa Maria del Gesù, sacred art (Coppo di Marcovaldo, Ambrogio Lorenzetti), Etruscan finds and a section of contemporary art.

In the Runcal area of the Stelvio National Park, along the road that climbs from Peio Fonti to Peio Paese, you can observe deer and roe deer in their environment; the deer house is a teaching center with panels on the fauna of the park designed for children and young people.
The source where the village was born.

Opened by the Municipality in 1982: finds of the Roman quarries of Fantiscritti and Gioia, a marble library of 310 samples from all over the world, machinery and tools of quarry from Roman times to today, plaster casts and works of contemporary sculpture.
Walk like pilgrims.

Gorge excavated in pure white marble from the Racines river, which falls into several waterfalls (according to italia.it 15 meters high), from Stanghe to Ponte Giovo; protected natural monument, you walk on walkways, wooden bridges and stairs made in 1896, fallen between the two wars and restored in the early Sixties. About an hour a journey, 1.5 hours round trip; starting from Ponte Giovo you save 175 m of ascent, and you should avoid 10-12:30.
Fortress of the 12th century rebuilt in 1560-64, today open air theatre with views of the village.
Walk through the heaps of a gold mine from 2,000 years ago.
The house-museum of Sorrento with the view on the gulf.

Tower on a rock spur overlooking the plain of Dervio; more exactly a mastic, whose fortification consisted of the walls of the surrounding buildings. The municipality indicates it with access for a fee, without amount or times.

Land towers formed over thousands of years by landslides and rains, where large boulders protect the ground below from erosion; in Tyrol they are located in the Mutbach gorge near Castel Tyrol and in the Fine Valley towards Caines. You can see from the top with the Hochmuth cable car, Herrschaftsweg trail or the route of about 5 km from Tyrol Castle to Farmerkreuz.

Borgo dei Monti Dauni on the hill overlooking the valley of Cervaro, the ancient Roman Vibinum, Orange Flag and among the most beautiful villages in Italy: about 800 stone portals, seven churches that are worth the name of  "Urbino del Sud" (Urbino del Sud), the ducal castle with the diocesan museum and the cathedral of 1231.
The fake Dome of Well.
The lighthouse on the rock and the coves of the west coast.
The Gallura of the bandits, without mythizing them.
Neoclassical theatre designed by Pietro Ghinelli and inaugurated in 1827.
The main road that crosses the whole Upper City, indicated by VisitBergamo among the routes to be done on foot.
The arts in the neoclassical palace.

The walls of 1554 draw the six-pointed star plant with angular wedge bulwarks and are interrupted only by Porta Vittoria (the oldest, marble and brick) and Porta Imperiale (1579, rebuilt in the nineteenth century). Around the village run for about 18 km the surrounding embankments against the flood of Po and Oglio.
Baroque on the main square.
The herbs of the pilgrims of Francigena.

Benedictine Abbey of Longobard foundation, about five kilometers from Ferentillo along the Black, considered the most significant testimony of the Duchy of Spoleto: founded by Duke Faroldo II on the church initiated by the hermits John and Lazarus, then mausoleum. It preserves a votive stele, Roman fragments, several sarcophagi, a Longobard altar, remains of frescoes and a two-level cloister of the 12th century. Church and cloister are visited by contacting the parish; other parts house a hotel in a private historical residence. From Ferentillo a trail of 7.8 km to Gabbio, Lorino and Forca.

Permanent exhibition of contemporary art made with the piles of wood, scattered among alleys, androns, squares, balconies and courtyards, which is enriched every year with new works with sculptors from all over the world: a face crying, the shuttle of the frame, a giant panicle, landscapes of woods as inlays. On the APT website you can download the route map and a brochure.
The popes museum.

Various coasts: sand in Paolina, Procchio and Spartaia, sand and rock in Sant'Andrea, rocks in Punta Nera and Chiessi, gravel and rock in Pomonte and Patresi; from Chiessi a challenging path with views of Capraia and Corsica.
Built in 1866 about 3 km from the village, on the side of the promontory called         Â"Fourth Warm Â": a house with a tower of 18 meters.
The oldest church in the village, with frescoes stratified over the centuries.
The eighteenth-century collections of the Institute of Sciences: anatomical and obstetric waxes, nautical charts, physics and the museum of Ulisse Aldrovandi, among frescoes by Pellegrino Tibaldi.
The medieval village on a hill between citrus fruits and vineyards.
Glass and steel balcony at the point where, in 1337, Francesco I Ventimiglia threw himself on horseback in the precipice, chased by the troops of Pietro II of Aragon.
The Natisone Valleys and the Slovenian culture of Friuli are told in an interactive way.

What remains of the plants and sulphur mines Trabia-Tallarita can be visited in the surroundings of the village, in the direction of Sommatino; the complex is documented in the Museo delle Solfare and it is a stop of the "Via delle Zolfare e dei Castelli" in Sicily of Mezzo.
The frescoes of the fourteenth century in the mountains.

The municipality of the upper Staffora Valley, in the Oltrepò Pavese Apennines, with a Roman furnace among the best preserved in Lombardy in Massinigo, the Salumiere Museum dedicated to the Salame of Varzi and the Brignati Trail between secular chestnuts and mills; it is part of the Ecomuseum "The wheat in grass" .
Stuff and gold from the 19th century theatre.
€1, free under 12 and over 65
The city market.
Between the two churches of the village, it was paved in 1975 with the local porphyry and is a permanent exhibition of the machining of the porphyry of the Val di Cembra.
The sightseeing of the Alps of the Valley of Susa.

Founded by the Carthaginians at the end of the 6th century BC on a nuragic settlement, it was razed to the ground for resisting in Rome and then became a early Christian episcopal center. The Punic phase remains walls and burials; on Columbaris hill, facing the sea, three basilica buildings, a small baptistery, stone sarcophagi still in situ, cappuccina tombs and canteens for the coolerium. It can be reached from the SS 292 to about 25 km, following the signs . Cornus-Columbaris.
The sea of Rome.
From the Etruscans to the Middle Ages.

Municipality of Val Colvera, at the foot of Mount Raut and inside the Natural Park of the Friulian Dolomites: the hamlet of Poffabro, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, with stone houses and wooden balconies and the church of San Nicolò; in Frisanco the Piazzatta Pognici and the exhibition "Da li mans di Carlin" .

Built at the end of the republican age and at the most splendor under Augustus, it remained hidden for centuries under the medieval city and re-emerged after the bombings of 1943; inaugurated on November 11, 2023, with the cavea re-composed with the original limestone steps and traces of the orchestra floor in colored marble. The last excavations have returned a portrait of Julius Caesar. Tickets through the Tourist Office.
See the Great River from the water.
The monumental heart of the village.
The house where Leonardo was born on 15 April 1452, about 3 km from Vinci, with a 3D multimedia story.
Liberty downtown.
Patronal church of the village, built in the fourteenth century and enlarged between 1885 and 1898, with a dome of 23 meters and in the apse a fresco by Gerardo Doctors of 1949.
The crenellated tower symbol of the village, panoramic view over the hills of Barbaresco.
The view extends to the sea.
The cloistered life told by objects.

Museum of the family-run historical wool mill that produces wool fabrics and quality yarns for fashion and does research and experimentation; open to the public, offers a path immersive in the processing of wool and in the garments that are born.
Palace of 1698 that preserves better than others the external appearance and the original plant.
A tribute to the scientist who named the country.
City of the plain of the Regi Lagni with the baronial castle of Lombard origin, built on the remains of the Roman theatre, which houses the museum of history and archeology of Acerra and Suessula.
The baroque church of the Walser colony.
Toys and vintage automatons in a 18th century villa.
A Romanesque church on the temple of Hercules.
Historic houses.
Municipality of the Polcevera valley with the seventeenth-century Palazzo Balbi, home of the museum of puppets of Angelo Cenderelli, and in its territory the lakes of the Gorezente.
Roman stones in the walls of a church.
A stone centre symbolizing the rebirth of the Sibillini.
Water and tuff in the wild Tuscia.

Free beach on the lake, always open, with lawn, pier, kiosk bar open from May to September and toilets. It is one of the points touched by the Blue Ring, the tour of Lake Orta on foot and by mountain bike.
One of Sicily's most elegant castles, linked to the legend of Queen Bianca of Navarre: the coat of arms room, the mirror room, the music room and the billiards, in a park of almost 8 hectares.

A relief of 602 meters at the northern edge of the bell plain, called the holm oak, where according to Silio Italico, Hannibal camped around 216 BC. On a minor summit, about 526 meters, remain the foundations of the temple of Jupiter Tifatino oriented towards Capua, located in 1996; on top there are ancient walls and a chapel linked to the hermit Saint Offa, and on the side towards Capua remains of villas, aqueducts and Roman sepulchres. From the ridge the view reaches the sea and Caiazzo.
Walking in Magna Grecia.

Designed by the architect Frontoni in 1722 and completed in 1751, with a round arch, it is the last still intact of the four gates of the historic center; it takes its name from the conquest of the city by Garibaldi on October 26, 1867.
Ancient castle transformed by Michelozzo from 1443 for Cosimo il Vecchio, loved by Lorenzo il Magnifico.

Fortified village about 650 meters on the western side of Majella, between the rivers Orta and Orfento, known for the sulphurous thermal baths active from the early twentieth century, the medieval churches and the reserve of the Orfento Valley.

Church of the XVI century dedicated to the patron saint of Terranova; restored, it preserves the original door made of pine (pine of Heldreich) and a 16th century painting by the Lucan painter Attilio De Laurentis with the Madonna of Grace and the Saints Carlo Borromeo and Francesco d'Assisi.
A sandwich with lampredotto where the Florentines eat it.
Lake Torre del Lago, with guided tours of the marshy flora and birdwatching huts, migratory stop for many birds; on the shores the Gran Teatro al fresco of the Puccini Festival in summer.
The second square of the city, which preserves in white marble the perimeter of the demolished church of Santa Giustina, with the monument to Garibaldi of Ettore Ferrari of 1896.

A fishing village between the Adda and the Lecco mountains, which in July is animated with the \'batei \' regatta; here you can admire the Â"Lucia Â" , an ancient wooden boat dedicated to the heroine of the Promisi Sposi.
The residence of the Fieschi overlooking the square.

Roman colony founded in 181 BC, among the major cities of the Empire and Mediterranean gate, destroyed by Attila in 452: UNESCO heritage with the patriarchal Basilica and the largest early Christian mosaic of the West, the river port and national museums.

Norman fortress of about 1054, on megalithic walls of the VI-IV century BC, trapezoidal plan with a tower per corner: the Norman Master Tower about 25 meters high, the cylindrical tower of Giulio Antonio Acquaviva today symbol of the city and the polygonal tower for the artillery; from the XV century residence of the Acquaviva.

The long promenade accompanies the main beach; the beach behind the pier is among the best known and is frequented by surfers, that of the Stone has a low and sandy seabed suitable for children, that of Vallesanta is of mixed pebbles, interrupted by the rock of Bernardone that hides a small creek.

It is reached in about twenty minutes on foot following the old ring of the Serremarchetto cross-country track of the seventies and eighties, a quiet walk among shady beech woods suitable for everyone. From the bench the view spans the lower Val Chisone and the plain of Pinerol and, on clear days, the Alpine arch from the Marittime to the Monviso.

On the second floor of the Palazzo della Magnifica Comunità, founded in 1880 and set up in 1984: pre-Roman and Roman finds of the sanctuary of Lagole, dedicated to the deity Trumusiate then identified with Apollo, the necropolis of Domegge and the crest of Valle di Cadore. In the atrium a black and white geometric mosaic from the end of the first century A.D. from a Roman domus.
On the trail of Nino Manfredi in his country.

At Campus Quagliariello the museums of the University Museum System, including the Museum of Zoology Lidia Liaci, the Museum of Earth Sciences and the Collection of the instruments of the epoch of Physics; guided tours by reservation.
18th century building in Baroque style.

The village perched on Mount Xibet in front of Enna, with medieval Norman plant: the Church Mother Royal Palatine Chapel on the ruins of the castle Marco, the church and the tower of San Pietro, the caves of Via Carcere, the Jewish quarter and, in the countryside, the necropolis of Realmese and the Byzantine village of Canalotto.
Two canvases by Teofilo Patini.

Small and romantic mountain lake at the end of the Valdurna valley, in the Sarentine Alps, a naturalistic protection area; a destination for fishermen and ring excursions. From the beginning of winter natural ice allows you to skate.
The trident of the Roman streets.
The narrow passage on the north side of Piazza delle Erbe, between the Case Mazzanti, where according to the story Tebaldo killed Mercutio: a plaque recalls the episode.
The ruins of Marturanum above the necropolis.
Art, archaeology and terrace on the sea.
A memorial of the Great War became city hall.
A Renaissance portico with different columns.
The Roman Asti.

Opposite the abbey, founded in 1224 by Cardinal Guala Bicchieri as the nucleus of the ancient Hospital for the pilgrims of the Via Francigena: arcade with arches and frescoed hall, open for exhibitions and events.
The place of St. Catherine.

Two glacial lakes about 1,935-1,940 meters in the Adamello group, between Corno Alto, La Cingla and La Costaccia, reachable only on foot from Diaga or Pozza delle Vacche (paths 230 and 221) in 1 hour and half-2 hours. On the shore is the nineteenth-century church of San Giuliano in stone and wood and the San Giuliano refuge of the 1930s; around the alpine pastures Campo and Germenega. Recommended period from late June to early October.
The villa of the exile of Giulia, on the promontory.
The fortress of the medieval center.

Panoramic path of medium difficulty, with steep stretches, starting from Via Monsignor Pullano and connecting the lagoon of Marinello to the sanctuary, with views of about 180° from the Gulf of Patti to the Aeolian Islands and Capo Milazzo.
Area indicated by the Park as temporarily closed for restoration or maintenance (the Museum of Greek Shipwrecks inside is open)

Chapel built in 1954 in Colle dei Frati, just outside Bettola, where according to tradition in 1496 the Virgin appeared to a shepherd among the branches of an oak; after the apparition there arose a church and a Franciscan monastery. Inside a mosaic by Luciano Ricchetti with the scene of the apparition; from April 2026 next door there are a reception center for pilgrims, a screening room and the reconstruction of the house of the pastorella.
An ancient Roman house for rent on the slopes of the Capitol, at the base of the stairway of Aracoeli.
Church of the XIII century in Madonna delle Grazie square; after the earthquake of 2009 it houses the statue of San Domenico di Sora and the celebrations of the patronal feast of May 1.

Porta della Valcellina at the foot of the Friulian Dolomites: the former Malnisio hydroelectric power station with original turbines and generators, the archaeological museum in Palazzo Toffoli, the necropolis of the Iron Age of Dominu in Grizzo and the Forra del Cellina, the largest canyon in the region.
Alpine village at 1047 meters between rascards and strong stone houses, dear to Carducci who wrote to you "The hostess of Gaby" .

Built in 1756 by the noble family of the same name, it is one of the best examples of 18th century architecture: living stone exterior, rooms with ceilings, stuccoes and trompe-l'oeil decorations by Gaspare Fumagalli and his father-in-law Pietro Martorana.

Center enclosed by the walls, with medieval squares and alleys, the Palazzo del Sedile and two doors: Porta Manfredi and Porta Taranto, called Porta degli Hebrei, which gives access to the Jewish community district established in the IX century. In August the historical procession of Frederick II and the Tournament of the Rioni.

Ruins on a relief that dominates the entrance of the valley between Pirchiriano and Caprasio, near the Dora Riparia: the first defensive traces would date back to the clash between Charlemagne and Desire alle Chiuse (771-774), while the castle of Caprie is mentioned from the thirteenth century as the center of an abbey castle, seat of court and prison. There remain perimeter walls, a tower, a seventeenth-century chapel of the Assumption and a large erratic boulder with an inscription on the passage of Charlemagne. Parking a few meters and short walk up.

Inaugurated in 1978, designed by Vittorio Viale and curated by Silvino Borla, it collects artifacts and photographic documentation of archaeological research in Trino; in the structure there is an audioguide. Open on the first and third Saturdays of the month from 15 to 18, or by appointment; free entry.

Ancient stronghold at the highest point of Larciano, the last refuge of the population in wartime, with irregular plan following the hill; inside the walls a church, a palace with tower, the mast, an ancient cistern and the foundations of the Captain's house. The 36-metre tower-cassero offers a wide view and since 1975 hosts the Civic Museum: kitchen ceramics, metals, polychrome majolica, brickwork, burials and everyday objects, with a didactic section and reconstruction of a tomb to the cappuccino of the Roman age. The sources date the castle between the XI-XII and the XIV century.

Founded in the 13th century, it is a pilgrimage destination linked to numerous miracles; in the first weekend of September it hosts the celebrations of the Mother of Good Council with the traditional fair.
temporarily closed for restoration (Common, September-October 2026 hours)
On the eastern side, it hosts at the end of May the feast of the saint with a fair-show of cattle.
The shrine to which the most heartfelt feast of the country is linked.
Sacred art in the heart of the village.
Church in high position in the rebuilt village, with severe and majolica interiors by Pietro Cascella on facade, altar, baptismal font, via crucis, paliotti, aquasantiere and chandeliers.

Romanesque monument of great importance built at the end of the 12th century on the hill of Montalino, where there is also the homonymous fortress (today private residence not visitable, with sixteenth-century loggia closed by a veranda).
Hans Clemer's masterpiece in the mountains.

On the highest hill, where the fortress stood, the Collegiata was built between 1422 and 1425 by the Solari brothers for Cardinal Branda: in the apse stories of the Virgin and Saints Stefano and Lorenzo of Masolino da Panicale (volta), Vecchietta and Paolo Schiavo, and the tomb of the cardinal. The Baptistery, obtained from a tower of the castle, has the cycle of the Life of the Baptist of Masolino (1435) with the Banquet of Herod; in the ancient Canonica the museum exhibits the Crucifixion of Blacks of Bicci, the Annunciation of Apollonius of John, goldsmiths and Ambrosian codes. Closed on Mondays; seasonal hours (from April to September Tuesday to Sunday 10-13 and 15-18).
A palace to see when hosting exhibitions.
Civil architecture of the village.

He tells with anthropological cut the Maremma brigandage and the figure of Domenico Tiburzi, born in the hamlet of Pianiano, from the second half of the nineteenth century to today. On the ground floor sources and historical reasons in a setting that evokes the forest (the tradition) and the train (modernity disappointed), among sounds, drawers to open, newspapers and films; on the second floor multimedia installations on the myth of Tiburzi; finally the 'taverna of the brigante's on the contemporary uses of his image. It is part of the Bolsena Lake Museum System; open on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, free for residents.
The omerica house of the early twentieth century, as it was.
The church of the Holy Nail with the portal of the fifteenth century.

With roots in the 16th century, when it had watchtowers and defensive structures, it was renovated in 1720 by the Lubelli family, which eliminated most of the towers: one remains visible. A stone portal between two columns leads into an open square atrium; a three-arched loggia preserves traces of painted decorations. Owned by the municipality since 1982, it is the seat of the Town Hall and has a congress hall.
Leo Leoni's bronze in front of the cathedral.
The sanctuary of the patron along the Via Amerina.

Borgo on the slopes of Monte Consolino, home of the philosopher Tommaso Campanella and in the X century main Byzantine center of southern Calabria. Its symbol is the Catholic, five-dome Byzantine church; in the stone village the 14th century Cathedral, the churches of St. Francis and St. John Theresti and, at the top, the remains of the Norman castle.
The civic museum illustrates the history and geomorphology of the Arzachena archaeological park area.
The Basilica of the Seven Churches that preserves the relics of the Cross brought to Rome by Saint Helena.
The history of the village in five rooms.
An Apuan alpine pasture out of time.
The Resistance of the Taro, Ceno and Mozzola valleys.
An underground cathedral of bones.
Nativity scenes from all over the world in the village of the crib.
Shadow and walk in the city.
Here the radio was born.
Alleys, talismanic symbols and terrace on the gorges.
Fortified village about ten kilometers from Pienza, with the castle of the mid-Twentieth century and the church of Santi Leonardo and Cristoforo from the Gothic portal.
Town of villages scattered on the hill east of Aosta, with the castle of the lords of Quart, the Neolithic necropolis of Vollein and the walks along the rus.
The four tower castle.
The defensive city largely intact with the towers of the ancient curtain, which makes the center one of the fortified villages of Val Conca.
The oldest church in the village and the Neapolitan paintings of the eighteenth century.
The former church of Purgatory, probably at the end of the 17th century, now auditorium Guido Calogero.

The main centre of Val Seriana, just over 30 km from Bergamo, with a historic centre on several levels: in Piazza dell'Orologio the planetary clock of Pietro Fanzago (1583), in front of the Basilica dell'Assunta the Oratory of the Disciplines with the Triumph and the Dance of Death (1485), and the MAT in Palazzo Marinoni Barca.

Benedictine Basilica dedicated to Saint Michael, rebuilt in 1072 for the abbot Desire on the temple of Diana Tifatina with materials of the ancient sanctuary; the interior is entirely frescoed by the Campania-Byzantine school with stories of the Old and New Testaments and the universal Judgment, the largest medieval pictorial cycle of southern Italy.
Founded in 1212, it dominates the village from the top of a staircase built in 1911; it has three aisles, it preserves two paintings by William Borremans (1728) and a sixteenth-century altarpiece.
On the trail of Don Camillo.
Space without symmetry and frontal alignments, one of the most interesting medieval urbanistic achievements of the region.
The 18th-century parish of the country.
Small Italian theatre of the second half of the nineteenth century, with a porticoed façade with brick columns and richly decorated interior; still used for shows and concerts.

Borgo perched on the southern buttress of Monte Soratte, limestone massif isolated in the Tiber valley 58 km from Rome: inside the walls with three gates there are the sixteenth-century Palazzo Caccia-Canali, attributed to the Vignola and seat of the Naturalistic Museum, and the church of San Lorenzo; on the mountain the Hermitage of San Silvestro and the galleries of the Bunker Soratte.

Romanesque church built around the thousand with Roman materials of the place, among the oldest in the Val d'Adige; in 1796 it was largely damaged by Napoleonic soldiers, but the perimeter walls, the entrance and the 18-metre-high square bell tower remain intact, and the frescoes of the apse arch have been recently restored.
Four temples in the middle of traffic.
The flowers of the hill.
The twentieth century in a villa with park.
Four geological ages.

Wanted by Pietro II d'Aragona on the ruins of the castle Marco, completed in 1340 and named Royal Palatine Chapel in 1342; with three naves, it is among the main expressions of Catalan art in the province, with column bases with winged felines and griffons. From the floor you can see the excavations of the castle and, under a glass, a early Christian rock church.
From the Dauni Mountains to the Tremiti.

Started at the end of the sixteenth century and almost completely rebuilt between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, originally  "Church of Purgatory" is from 1638 the seat of the Archconfraternity of the Dead. Curved façade with portal in the breach and stone statues of St. Francis and St. Anthony; inside Neapolitan canvases of the seventeenth century, the Purgatory of Nunzio De Nunzi (1707), a Venetian Deposition of the sixteenth century, a sixteenth-century organ and paintings of the Christmas Vault Penati (1938).

Small village entirely included in the Regional Park Campo dei Fiori, which houses the headquarters of the agency; there are the Museum of Rural Culture Prealpina, Lake Brinzio with the nearby Cascata del Pesegh and the departure of several paths of the park.

Commissioned in 1517 by Cardinal Alessandro Farnese, future Pope Paul III, to Antonio da Sangallo the Younger, rises at the highest point of the country on the remains of an ancient castle and was the summer residence of the Farnese. After the fall of Castro (1649) became a convent of the Filippini Fathers; purchased by the Municipality in 1911, it is municipal seat since 1919 and was restored in 1986 and 1997, with the recovery of many frescoes. The rooms have frescoes, terracotta floors and wooden coffered ceilings.
The town museum that tells Ferrara from the Risorgimento to the Resistance, along Corso Ercole I d'Este.

Renaissance square dedicated to Prince Doria with the Doria Palace and the oratory erected around 1580 after a pestilence, with frescoed façade by Giovan Battista Carlone; four horse castans from 1853 in the center.
The monastery of the thirteenth century with the cloister, now the venue of concerts; the Cisterna Square was the cloister of the monastery founded in 1286.

Church completed in 1270, with a single nave with oval vaults, portal to pointed sixth and rose window; the convent dates back to the first decades of the thirteenth century and the cloister, the only surviving earthquake of 1915, has frescoed lunettes with the life of St. Francis taken from the major legend of St. Bonaventure.

Medieval village of Beneventano with doors of the fourteenth century, the circular Torre dei Provenzali and Piazza Risorgimento; in the historic center is the Museum of tower clocks, with fifty machines restored by the master watchmaker Salvatore Ricci, and along Via Roma the shops of the crunchy torrone.

Romanesque building probably of the 11th century, restored and enlarged in Renaissance age, when the bell tower was erected; the sacristy is of the late 16th century. It was the parish church of Induno until the construction of St. John the Baptist. The hut façade preserves in part the original plaster frescoed with the Virgin, Child and saints; the portal with bezel is made of Viggiu stone and inside remain precious frescoes, marked by time. Open for Fall 2020 and Spring 2022 FAI Days.
The sheltered area of 274 hectares around the caves, with dense vegetation, rare fauna and outings of chalk, part of the UNESCO site of the Gessi dell'Emilia-Romagna.
Trekking among the most ancient spas and fumaroles.
The long narrow street of shopping, ancient Roman cardoon, with liberty windows, a 17th century jewelry and the Antico Caffè di Simo frequented by Puccini.

The municipality of the Groane Park is known for its delightful villas: Villa San Carlo Borromeo, where Cardinal Federico Borromeo welcomed seminarians and theologians during the plague of 1630, Villa Corbella-Martinelli-Sioli, former summer residence of the archbishops of Milan, and Villa Verzolo-Monzini with its English park.
The residence of the Hats, lords of the village.

Country of the high plain 13 km from Modena, documented since 1025 and for almost four centuries feud of the Rangoni, known for the processing of pigmeat: the Torrione della Rocca, the monument to the pig, the museum of the salumery and, in Montale, the archaeological park of Terramara and the tomb of Luciano Pavarotti.
Garden among the city parks reported by PromoTurismoFVG.
The majolica bell tower on the sea and its Master.
Church of the 16th century.

Medieval village of the Alta Maremma on Poggio Ballone, once lordship of the Pannocchieschi and then mining center of the pyrite between Otto and Novecento: today the Natural Mining Park with the museum in the gallery, the Theatre of the Rocks, the Pozzo Roma and the Ravi-Marchi area. In the territory of Castel di Pietra, linked to Pia di Dante, the parish church of San Giuliano, San Biagio a Caldana and the Etruscan necropolis of San Germano.

Cistercian Abbey started in 1143 by the monks who arrived in 1142, built with stones of the Roman Urbs Salvia: three-nave church with pointed vaults, brick cloister, capitular hall, refectory and cellars that house the Wine Museum and the Museum of Rural Civilization.
The village collapsed with views of the Roman city.
Frescoed cloister and panoramic view from Mount Santa Trinità.
Giotteschi frescoes in a medieval monastery, which can be visited only on special occasions.
Land of oil DOP and Vulci, one of the most powerful city-states of Etruria: walls, temples, domus and necropolis with the Tomb François, the Castle of Badia and the Devil's Bridge on the Flower.
The heart of the ancient village with its fifteenth-century bell tower.
A museum of the nineteenth century intact.
Monument erected in 1892, for the four hundred years of the discovery of America, in the main square of the village of San Giovanni, to remember the bond of the village with the family of Colombo.

Roman colony from 194 BC, port and bishop's seat, abandoned after the burial of the port and earthquakes of 1223 and 1255. It preserves the early Christian basilica of the 4th century with mosaic floors, on which since 2016 stands the installation in metal mesh of Edoardo Tresoldi .Where art reconstructs the time, 14 meters high; next, the Romanesque basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore (end XI-beginning XII century), a cubic plan with dome, crypt and portal with columns on lions. Open from Wednesday to Sunday 10.30-19.30.
The Renaissance in the country.
Hosted in the abbey complex since 2009.

Built between 1468 and 1587 to guard the Holy House, according to tradition the house of Nazareth of the Virgin came to Loreto in the night between 9 and 10 December 1294. Giuliano da Maiano brought it to the drum and Giuliano da Sangallo turned the dome, repainted by Cesare Maccari between 1895 and 1907; Istria stone façade completed in 1587 and bell tower by Luigi Vanvitelli (1750-1755). Inside the Chapel of the Annunciation frescoed by Federico Zuccari, the Sacristy of St. Mark of Melozzo da Forlì, that of St. John of Luca Signorelli and the Treasury Hall with the turn of the Pomarancio (1605-1610).
The walls of ex-vote.
Consecrated in 1762, it preserves an eighteenth-century tabernacle carved and gilded by a Valsesian artist and furnishings of the 16th-XVIII centuries.

Village of Vallagarina on the left bank of the Adige, in a sunny amphitheatre of vineyards and orchards, dominated by Castel Beseno, the largest fortified complex in Trentino, which since the twelfth century has been guarding the road towards the highlands of Folgaria and Lavarone.
Flag Orange and the most beautiful village in Italy, it holds one of the best preserved medieval recipes: about 200 stone houses among walls, towers and cobbled rue.
The Guja gold mine, which can be visited.

Also known as Santa Maria della Lode, the ancient cathedral of the diocese of Forum Novum and then of Sabina until 1733: a single nave with raised presbytery and semi-anular crypt of the 11th century, cycle of frescoes of the 2rd-Three hundred with stories of the Old and New Testaments and, in counterfaced, a great universal judgment of the school of Pietro Cavallini, rediscovered under the skilful in 1930; five-order bell tower of double and triple windows. Open every day 8-20 according to the MiC card.
An architecture on the river.
The minerals of Gallura in a small museum.

The parish church, on the highest hill of the village and reached by a stone staircase, was built in 1600, rebuilt in 1805 after a earthquake and redesigned in 1937; the vault is frescoed by Mario De Tollis with the Ascent of the Virgin. Next to it, the Church of the Sorrowful preserves a wooden Madonna of the sixteenth century, two paintings by Carmine Muliere and the "Deposition" frescoed in 1924 by Arnaldo De Lisio.
A walk inside the walls of a castle of Farfense.

Established in 1986 in the basement of the eighteenth century College of Santa Croce, unicum in Italy: over 20,000 objects produced by Casalmaggiore factories between the late nineteenth and seventies, with tools, machines, photos and catalogs of the industrial gold century of the city, plus a didactic workshop of fusion and gilding. Open Tuesday-Saturday 10-12 and 15-18, Sunday and holidays 15-19; free on the first Sunday of the month.
A Malaspinian village along the Francigena.
The façade of about 8,500 diamond-pointed marble bugs creates unique light games; inside the great art exhibitions.
This is where the visit to the engravings begins.
The ancient gate of the city next to Castel Capuano, commissioned by King Ferrante d'Aragona to the architect Giuliano da Maiano in the renovation project of Naples.
Big red bench in Capecchiara, inaugurated on November 25, 2022 as a symbol against violence against women and recovery after the earthquake of 2016, with a wide view.
A castle furnished in the city center.

Narrow streets with historic buildings, portals and fountains, the parish church of St. Joseph, the church of St. George and the birthplace of Cipriano Valorsa,     Â Â the Raffaello della Valtellina Â Â Â the first Sunday of Lent will take off Carneval Vecc.
The history of industrial design and Olivetti technology, with educational workshops.
One of the densest concentrations of dolmen in Italy, among the olive trees.
visits only by reservation (tel. 095 7832962)

Villa on the hills that descend from Civitella, near Oliveto, with the current appearance due above all to a nineteenth century intervention: mills and cellars, noble floor and service floor, surrounded by a park of large trees and olive groves terraces. During the Second World War it was a concentration camp and today it hosts the Center of documentation on the concentration camp.
Panoramas and trails above the lake.
Painting from the Renaissance to the Baroque.
The tombs of the Roman city.

Village of the Amalfi Coast about 600 meters, among terraces of olive trees, vineyards and lemons, known for the Fiordo with its fishing village and for the more than one hundred ' artist walls that make it a painted village.
The ex-vote tells the country life of three centuries.
The village on top of the hill, with the panoramic balcony.
civic hall open for events and exhibitions; visiting hours not indicated by the source
The gate of the first century BC, also known as Sant'Andrea, with the arch in sandstone blocks from which came those who arrived from Via Aretina.
The castle of Frederick II on Messapia.
Six hundred items from East Africa.
In Marina di Grosseto, dunes and ancient pine forest between the sea and the Riserva della Diaccia Botrona.
Neoclassical in miniature.
Usually open from mid-June to mid-September

It gathers the works of the artists of the national competition of painting "Premio Città di Civitella" ("Premio Città di Civitella Award"), founded in 1964 by Pro Loco for the cultural rebirth of the country after 1944, alternated in the seventies with the sculpture exhibition "S"Objectively. About 200 paintings (one hundred exhibited in the gallery, in a renovated former school) and almost 70 sculptures, of which 28 large permanently installed in the village; the oldest work is a black and white painting of 1971 by the American Ellisse Pogafsky Hakrs.
The church of the hamlet Veravo, which dominates the valley.
The Romanesque parish church of the Bardi's manor.
Opened at the end of the nineteenth century in the form of a temple, the largest opera house in Italy and the third in Europe, with the symbolic Wheel painted by Luigi di Giovanni and guided tours.

Borgo della Lomellina dominated by the Litta-Beccaria Castle, documented by the 11th century and transformed into a noble villa by Agostino Litta in 1573, which in the Long Channel hosts the Lomellino Archaeological Museum; not far from the Romanesque parish church of Sant'Eusebio, renovated in Baroque age.

Founded in 1466 to accommodate 173 codes donated by the humanist Guarniero d'Artegna, it is the oldest public library in Friuli: more than 600 manuscripts, including a Byzantine Bible of the late 12th century and a Divine Comedy of the late 14th century, about 80 incunabula and 12,000 ancient volumes. The ancient section is visited by reservation and is closed in August.
The lake, the Maestro Canal of Chiana and the surrounding fields: together with the lake of Chiusi is what remains of the marshes of the valley, one of the most important wetlands in central Italy.
The traces of the Lucans over Orthodox.
The Risorgimento seen from the top of the tower.
The heart of the city of San Benedetto.

Site of the Upper Paleolithic in the locality Nuppolara, discovered in 1961: outside the 1.20 meters long graffito of two bovids (Bos primigenius), among the oldest evidence of prehistoric art in Italy, and burials of about 10,500 years ago (three double burials, including the young hunter The findings cover about 23,000-10,000 years ago; in the Neolithic layer much obsidian suggests a base for trade between Tyrrhenian and Ionian. The site has catwalks, lighting, multilingual audio guides and an antiquarium with some artifacts; the reproduction of the graffito is at the National Museum of Reggio Calabria.
In Palazzo Marinozzi, a permanent national exhibition on cinema advertising graphics.

Promontory just over 700 meters south of the village which, with Mount Ciolino, barred the valley: in the Great War it was not a battlefield but an observation point for Italians and Austrians. Open all year round with free entry, with marked trails and a panoramic terrace over Borgo and the valley.
The coast seen from above.
Medieval church built in 1428 on the remains of the castle tower, next to Palazzo Gervasoni; its clock bell tower, rebuilt in the mid-nineteenth century, can be seen coming from the lake.
The Sicilian baroque in Giarre.

18th century residence with ancient rural village in three courts along the east-west axis, entrance garden, main garden and park; passed to Marietti in 1811, then to Tosi and Ricotti. In the garden a neo-Moresca Coffee House with pebble mosaics and, next to the Italian garden, the eighteenth-century lemon house with high wooden ceilings.
An outdoor museum of funeral sculptures.
One of the most beautiful seafronts in Italy, overlooking the Adriatic and the most beautiful buildings of the city, pleasant to walk through locals and typical restaurants.

The smallest municipality of Basilicata, founded around 1534 by Albanian refugees in the Sarmento valley in the Pollino National Park; the Arbëreshe community preserves language and Byzantine rite, told in the Museum of Arbëreshe culture.
