Borgo canavesano among woods and countryside, Orange Flag, told by Guido Gozzano and dominated by the Ducal Castle of the Savoy.
18th-century Palace of Norimbergese merchants Sichardt, since 2019 a participatory and interactive museum on the history of the oaks.
Sanctuary on a hill near Castello di Sambuca, around which from 1722 the homonymous convent arose.
Fortified village of Chianti, one of the most beautiful villages in Italy, with the Romanesque parish church and Palazzo Malaspina, seat of the tourist office.

Ancient buildings and narrow streets with small shops and terraces to discover on foot around the Patriarch's Camp; the promenade is the recommended point for sunset. Typical dish of boreto, fish with vinegar sauce.

Considered one of the most beautiful civil works of the Sicilian Middle Ages, it crosses the Simeto in the district of "Salto del Pecoraio." Probably of Roman origin, along one of the roads of the wheat towards the Ionic ports, was rebuilt in Arabic era with sharp sixth arches and alternation of light and dark stones; in Norman age it connected Troina to Catania. Damaged by the earthquake of 1693 and the flood of 1948, it preserves the main central arch in Gothic style. From 2000 it falls on the site of community interest  "Forre lavache del Simeto" with gorges 5 to 15 meters high excavated in basalt; in the nearby Mendolito district the walls and the South Gate of a Sicilian city of the IX-V century BC have been identified.
The village where Michelangelo Buonarroti was born on March 6, 1475, when his father was a podestà.
Equipped beach on Lake Caldonazzo, with sandy areas and lawn, next to the small church of San Cristoforo.
museum open only on the first Saturday of the month from 10 am to 12 pm (schools on reservation); private castle not accessible; museum not accessible to people with disabilities

Dedicated to the Etruscan border, it exhibits the findings of the Villanovian and Etruscan-Campan center, especially the collections of over 10,000 graves dug in the necropolis in about fifty years. The chronological route goes from the Eneolithic to the Roman age, with sections on cities, necropolis, sanctuaries and crafts and a section on the Orientalizing aristocracies (VIII-VII century BC) with tombs \'principesche Â Â; in the collection also contemporary works by Pietro Lista and Perino&Vele. Closed on Monday.
The traces of Flaminia in the valley of Topino.
The frescoes of Guido da Ranzo.
A palace rising from the sea.
The Marzemino in his house, under frescoes of the eighteenth century.
Historical villa with park, inserted by the municipality among the gardens, villas and parks of the city.
The parish church of the Cusani, a stone's throw from the castle.
The most famous balcony in the world.
The daunie stems in a castle on the sea.
The neo-Gothic castle of Castiglioncello.
In Piazza San Domenico the church has a Baroque façade dating back to 1742; next to it stands the Sedile di San Luigi, the only surviving noble seat of the city.

The Rice Fair, founded in 1967, hosts between September and October the Festa del risotto italiano, with the prize for the best risotto among restaurants, trattorias and private; you cook the Vialone Nano, IGP rice of the low Veronese, also in the typical risotto at the taste.
Municipality of villages on the hill above Chambave, with ancient medieval russ, the frescoes of Giacomino d'Ivrea and the reserve of the pond of Loson.
The cyclopean walls surrounding the village.
Russian domes on the Riviera.
With a tower 20 meters high, separated from the central body and leaning against a wall of tuff.
Elegant 19th century theatre in the lower part of Corso Umberto I, starting point of the visit to the village.
It rises where there was a dried-up pond: it is the largest open space in the city, called the "Big Zardin" with a fountain with water games, parties and fairs.
A Donatellian Madonna in the mountains.
In a former convent, dedicated to agricultural life, with the reconstruction of a typical farmhouse.
Ancient hermitage transformed into a church by the Jesuits in 1736; the Stations of the Way of the Cross are partly carved into the rock.
hours of the source referring to the season 2024 (Friday-Sunday and holidays), out of season visits only by reservation

The Museum opened with the Cathedral, the Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul (XVI-XVII century), with white stone façade of Syracuse and high bell tower, the eighteenth-century Municipal Palace and Palazzo Modò, which housed the Eldorado Theatre; the concentric ring flooring of 2009 is by Scaccianoce, Messina and Paolo Portoghesi.

The old town is reached by two ancient gates, Porta San Nicolò and Porta Nova; there are the crenellated tower and the Castle or Baronial Palace, built in the fifteenth century, whose remains with the Mother Church tell the history of the village.

The lake basin, which takes its name from the nearby village of Barrea, includes Villetta Barrea and Civitella Alfedena; paths and bike paths run along it and there is a small beach, La Gravara. Some excursions are only for experienced hikers; dogs on a leash.
One of the masterpieces of the Romanesque Abruzzo, overlooking the Gran Sasso.

About 25 km of coast between Principina a Mare and Talamone, with the Uccellina Mountains, cliffs, pine forests, marshes, the mouth of the Ombrone and wild beaches where they graze horses and Maremma cows.
From the village to the panorama of the sea and Corsica.
High-altitude lake between marmots and war memories.

In the ancient bishop's palace in Piazza Duomo, Roman mosaics, medieval sculptures and paintings of Lotto, Moroni, Baschenis and Manzù, with the Picta Hall restored; the same ticket opens the Baptistery and the former Oratory of San Lupo.

Small village of the Prenestini Mountains, 63 km from Rome, gathered around the Fortress Colonna that houses the Geopaleontological Museum "Ardito Desio" and an astronomical observatory; in the surroundings the fossil clay cliff, natural monument, and the planetary with the reconstruction of the dinosaur "Tito" .
About €6 whole (data 2026 of the Ministry); free with BW Card and before Sunday of the month
A Byzantine church of the tenth century.
The seventeenth-century palace designed by the architect stage designer Ferdinando Galli Bibiena for the Costa Counts.
Romanesque with Baroque façade, in the cemetery: 13th century apse and 15th century frescoes.
The Gothic porch in the square.
The view of the harbor.

Small pilgrimage church dedicated to Our Lady of Loreto, built in 1652 (date on the entrance) and once equipped with hermitage, the most frequented pilgrimage of the Pusteria media. It is climbed along the Way of the Cross; inside the Black Madonna with the Child between the Saints Anna and Joachim, the Annunciation on the tympanum of the altar and the Saints Joseph and Silvestro above the doors.
A late Liberty theater reborn.
The civic bell tower that cuts the city in two.
From €12 single tour, €20 full tour with the Arab wing reopened in 2026 (source of news); the Metropolitan City indicates €10
Seven thousand years of Upper Mantua and the room of Napoleon III.

Church documented since 1362, immersed in olive trees with palm trees on the churchyard; legend has it that in the nearby olive grove the janares were gathered. Several times reported to the Places of the FAI Heart.

The monument to the scientist, born in the village then called Livorno Vercellese, rises in the square dedicated to him next to the museum, in front of the church of San Giovanni Decollato. Ferraris founded the first school of electrical engineering in Italy in 1889 and in 1896 the Italian Electrical Association; he died that year at 49 years of age.
A treasure of sacred art in a mountain country.

Centre of the Arezzo Valley gathered around Piazza Varchi, with the Collegiate Church of San Lorenzo and its Museum of sacred art with the temple of Andrea della Robbia, the Palaeontological Museum of the Accademia Valdarnese del Poggio and the Cassero for sculpture.
From Mattia Preti to De Chirico.
The natural rock pools.

Small village of Maceratese that preserves the remains of the walls with perimeter towers and an ogival door before 1200; among its churches the SS. Annunziata with the Nativity of Giovanni Andrea De Magistris (1560) and the Church of the Loggia with a Renaissance fresco; in summer it hosts the Artistrada Buskers Festival.

Series of almost circular cavities, joined by narrow passages, born from the erosion of the waters flowing under the ancient Toce glacier. The Southern Horrid, the most spectacular, is about 200 meters long and 20-30 deep; the North-East Horrid, near the oratory of Saint Lucia, is a gorge of about 150 meters crossed in whole; the West Horrid is the least important. Iron ladders and walkways make sure the path is marked, but with wet or frozen bottom the risk can be very high.
One of the masterpieces of the Umbrian Renaissance.
By boat or canoe in the submerged valleys.
€9 whole (church and museum)

Castello degli Aldobrandeschi mentioned in 1140 (until 1188 Rocca di Fabiano), then Sienese and from 1555 Medici, seat of Podestria under Medici and Lorraine. The center is spread on a terrace of Riolithic rock towards the ancient "carceri" with a stretch of east wall; the only door left, very restored, is the Madonnino Gate, between Vicolo Basso and Piazzetta dell'Incroccia. At the entrance from Piazza Gramsci a trachite sculpture by Renaux François.

Mountain village on a rocky spur at 1,250 meters, overlooking the valley of Sangro in the National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise, with alleys portraited also by Escher, the church of Santa Maria Assunta and the Museum of Chamois; under the village the Val Fondillo, the greenest valley of the Park, in whose reserve area there is the largest of the old beech woods of the Park recognized World Heritage.
Hosted in the former Franciscan convent and in the neo-Gothic Torre del Palagi, it exhibits crystals, fossils and minerals from all over the world.

Borgo della Val Casotto in the Monregalese Valleys, with 23 fountains named after women: in the upper part the eighteenth-century castle of the Marquis Cordero, now Town Hall, the parish church of San Biagio and the Baroque oratory of Sant'Antonio; among the chestnuts the chapel of San Bernardo with frescoes from 1482, in Serra the Museum of the Uses of Mountain People and in Valcasotto a stone mill of the Napoleonic era.

Seaside town of the Riviera di Ponente, imperial fief of the Dorias, with a historic center among the best preserved of Liguria: Palazzo Doria (seat of the Municipality, with a mosaic of the third century), the Castle of the Dorias, the Convent of Monte Carmelo, the Pentagonal Tower and the Decagonal Cathedral of San Giovanni Battista; long sandy beaches Blue Flag and one of the largest ports of the Ponente.
A 7.20 m wide section of a smaller wall in the Roman city, in basoli on a bottom of bricks, amphorae and tiles.
The silvers and furnishings of the Duomo and the memory of the first seminar.

Permanent institute based at Palazzo Castellano, which, with the participation of the inhabitants, studies and enhances the natural and cultural heritage of the valley, considering the entire territory as a museum diffused in the landscape and traditions.
The table with the picture of the castle.
It is also part of the castle complex, with an ancient Franciscan monastery.

The capital of Val Graveglia, in the Aveto Regional Natural Park, a valley of great geological and mineralogical interest; there is the manganese mine of Gambatesa, now a museum, and in Reppia a mineralogical museum.
An eighteenth-century shrine built on an earlier newsstand, in the place of an ancient lazzaretto; a popular fair is held on the churchyard in September.

The street collects the most typical elements of the medieval village and is an example of an ancient mercantile village: the shops looked out onto the arcades, born at a later moment as canopies to repair the goods on display, and the traffic passed inside the village. At the entrance stood the main door, called "Piè del Borgo" (Piè del Borgo), almost all the street is flanked by arcades and in some stretches remains the original pavement. The building at number 11, with wooden ceiling, is the oldest in the village.

Two rooms of about 90 m2 on two levels dedicated to Maria Carta, singer, musicologist, poetess and actress born in Siligo in 1934 and died in Rome in 1994: sections on biography, music and research on the folk traditions Sardinian, poetry (with "Song of ritual" , 1975, unpublished manuscripts and a film in which she plays), theatre and cinema and commitment as city councilwoman in Rome; photos, stage costumes, prizes, press reviews and relics. Monday-Friday 10-13 and 16-19, Saturday and Sunday on request.
The tools of the peasant world.

The Fontana Maggiore, among the greatest examples of medieval Italian sculpture, was built between 1278 and 1280 by Nicola and Giovanni Pisano to celebrate the new aqueduct, on a project by Fra Bevignate and with the hydraulic part of Boninsegna from Venice.
Three churches superimposed.
A very powerful Last Supper, almost always without a tail.

On the plateau at the most advanced point of the Lepini Mountains remain the remains of an ancient city, especially hydraulic works to collect and distribute water, with polygonal walls dated to the sixth century BC, terraces and fortifications; guided paths, panels and a tour center. Here is also the Big Bench 434.

The museum tells the Resistance lived by the people of the valley: facts, people and places become symbol, up to the Liberation and beyond, with today's reading and suggestions for visitors; in the valley it is flanked by other places of memory such as the Ossario and the Common Fossa. In the same building the Ecomuseum Alta Val Sangone has a ground teaching workshop (LABSOL), a weaving workshop, temporary exhibition rooms and the tourist office. Free admission; open during the tourist office hours, which vary with the season.
Magnificent eighteenth-century villa surrounded by greenery, at the beginning of the Kilometer of Knowledge.

In the public park in front of Porta Serio, east of the historic centre, there are raised bald cypresses (Taxodium distichum) almost 30 meters tall, indicated as the most fascinating monumental trees of Cremasco; in Piazzale delle Rimembranze two symmetrical ginkgo bilobas on the sides of the fountain accompany towards the center, and between the cobbled streets a cedar of Lebanon pops up for almost two centuries beyond the wall of Palazzo Premoli.
Romanesque church erected in 1074, one of the oldest in Puglia, behind the castle tower.
On the hill above the Po, the Savoy castle where Vittorio Emanuele II signed in 1849 the Proclamation of Moncalieri.
To be combined with the Collegio del Cambio.
A 19th-century village theatre.
The panoramic summit above the Abetone.
The oldest nucleus of the city and ancient ghetto, with low porticos, the fifteenth-century synagogue and the church of San Sebastiano.

The center, today pedestrian, has calli and campielli reminiscent of Venice and colorful houses around the fishing port; the Rio Terrà is one of the most frequented outdoor living rooms of Veneto, even out of season. In Calle Lunga the Palazzòn has an original fifteenth-century body and owes its name to the many families living there; in Rio Terrà Romiati a facade brings a frescoed sundial of marine inspiration. The centre of the city is Piazza Vescovado, recently renovated, with the Duomo and next to the palace.
In the surroundings of the village there are hundreds of cellars dug into the tuff, used in the past to preserve wine.

Born as a fortress on a hill overlooking the city, it was rebuilt in 1678 by the Durazzo family as a summer residence on the model of the Genoese villas of the seventeenth century; since 1973 it is of the Municipality. Inside there are statues, frescoes, majolica floors and Genoese granite, Murano chandeliers, antique furniture, a painting gallery of Genoese painters from the 17th and 18th centuries (Piola, Borzone, Paggi, De Ferrari) and the reconstruction of the study by writer Vittorio G. Rossi; in front of the entrance a square in white and black stones. The park, of about three hectares overlooking the Gulf, brings together Agrumeto, Giardino all'italiana, romantic English wood (voluted in 1919 by Alfredo Chierichetti) and Secret Garden of the Princes Centurione, and since 2006 is part of the Great Italian Gardens; the entrance to the park is free. Ticket €3 from 6 to 12 years, €4 for groups of 15 people and members FAI and Touring (MiC card updated to 2020). Tel. 0185 293135.
The full tour of the municipality among woods and views.
A nineteenth century sanctuary with a Renaissance altarpiece.
Snooping through the desks downtown.
A 15th century Sienese hydraulic work.
Medieval doors and views of the countryside from the viewpoint.
By cable car on the balcony of Vipiteno.
The volcanic landscape of the Postman.
The monumental ship-shaped sculpture of 1987.

Two sections, in the Bishop's Palace and in the northern matron of the cathedral: the chalice of St. Donnino (Renish goldsmith's church of the XII-XIII century), the Eucharistic dove in bronze, the Madonna in throne with the Child attributed to Benedetto Antelami and the Treasury Hall with works from the XI to the XVI century, gifts of pilgrims. Open Saturday and Sunday, in the weekdays only groups by reservation.
The palace and the bell of the free municipality.

The island of the protected marine area, in front of Capo Carbonara, which owes its name to the abundance of wild cabbages; in its backdrops the submerged statue of the Madonna del Naufrago (Virgin of the Sea) of Pinuccio Sciola, half every third Sunday of July of a procession of decorated boats.

The medieval fortified nucleus of Cupra Marittima, with traces from the IX-X century and free commune from the XI century with a fortified port and trade up to Venice, Ragusa and Durazzo; it is still surrounded by walls with square and polygonal towers wanted in the XV century by Francesco Sforza. You enter the Porta Maggiore or Marina; in the village the Palazzo Brancadoro, built by the Sforza, the remains of the fortress and the panorama of the sea.

Built in 1970 on the tip of the telegraph of Capo Palinuro, on the bases of an ancient watchtower of which traces remain; about 70 meters high, it is second in Italy for luminous flow, visible up to Sicily. The interior cannot be visited because the military area; you can reach it on foot or by car.
Church in the park with a altarpiece attributed to Hannibal Carracci; recognized by UNESCO as a "monument messenger of culture of peace."
A nuragic village inside the village.
Stone streets and Roman inscriptions on a panoramic promontory.
Lose yourself in the alleys of the city of Primitivo.
Ancient houses in traditional Campidano architecture; the Rio Mannu divides the village into the  "grande" and "small" districts, connected by three bridges.
Built between 1522 and 1528 after a pestilence, it preserves numerous frescoes dedicated to the saint owner.

Medieval village of Sabina above the valley of Farfa, divided for centuries between the Orsini, in the lower part, and the Colonna, in the upper part: Porta Maggiore with the fifteenth-century palaces, Palazzo Orsini seat of the Municipality, Santa Maria Nova on the site of the Colonna fortress, the church of San Lorenzo outside the walls and the museum of Maria Petrucci.
The Gothic church of Santa Maddalena, reached on foot.

On a panoramic hill, commissioned by Vincenzo Giustiniani in the seventeenth century as a family mausoleum: monumental façade between two bell towers with the large bust of the Redentore, inside a Latin cross with dome, decorated only with stuccoes; the monastery, after the war, was donated by Prince Odescalchi to the Silvestrini Benedictines. It preserves the first Christ Portacroce by Michelangelo, abandoned in 1514 for a dark vein on the cheek, purchased by Giustiniani in 1607 and completed by another sculptor (perhaps Bernini), brought here in 1644 by his nephew Andrea; the restoration of the Superintendence of 2001 confirmed the attribution. In 2025 he was exposed to the Osaka Expo.
In the surroundings of the capital, the castle is distinguished by the high square tower, from which you can enjoy a wide panorama between Umbria and Tuscany.
The facade of city power.
The great museum of cycling in the city of Girardengo and Coppi.
Walk in the places of the Resistance to Paraloup.
Highlights accessible without barriers
The highest view of the municipality, comfortable even with children.

Carnia municipality that rises from the plain of Tagliamento to the top of Monte Verzegnis, with fractions at different altitudes around an artificial lake; at Villa di Verzegnis the collector Egidio Marzona created the Art Park, open-air museum with works by Merz, LeWitt, Long and Penone.
The mine told by those who worked on it.
Attached to the cathedral, begun in 1355 with a Greek cross and transformed into a Baroque style, with the large wooden canopy by Carlo Riccione from the late 17th century.

Alleys and squares with bars and restaurants; the Palazzo Imperiali-Pilotico rises on the remains of a Norman castle, and among the churches there are St. Anthony with the convent, St. Mary of Constantinople, St. Lucia, the Madonna of Carmine and St. Francis of Assisi.

Rock village of about 3,000 square meters formed by dozens of units partly dug into the rock and partly built, used as houses, shelters for animals, for the production of wine and lime and as granaries; the oldest traces seem to date back to the VIII-XII centuries. The hypothesis about origin are two: a colony of oriental populations or a productive outpost or deposit of the nearby Kastron of Mesiano. Guided tours by reservation (info@grottezungri.it, 377 441 9886); not recommended to those who have difficulty in getting rid of steps and uneven and steep terrain.
The prehistory to touch with your hand.
A creative tradition still alive.

At 1,120 meters in the Nebrodi Park, Troina was in 1060 the seat of Count Ruggero and the first Norman capital of Sicily, with the first Norman cathedral of the island; today you can visit the Torre Capitania with the portrait of Paolo III of Tiziano, the museum of war photos of Robert Capa, the medieval quarter Scalforio, the ruins of the Basilian monasteries of San Michele, Monte Muganà and Lake Sartori.

The port of Claudio was started in 42 AD north of the mouth of the Tiber to bring to the sea the river traffic of Rome, today under the airport; Trajan enlarged it in 106 AD with a large hexagonal basin more internal and secure, digging the channel that created the Sacred Island.
In front of Palazzo Vagnone in Piazza Libertà, it has a baroque interior and a polychrome ceramic cover; next to it stands the Clock Tower.
One of the most beautiful bell towers in Lazio.
In the castle of Da Varano, collection of tools of the local peasant and artisan civilization that tells the rural traditions of the village.
The Roman gate dug into the cliff.
The climb that gives the view of Odle and Sassolungo.

Among the most ancient monuments of Sorrento, in the historic center; restored in the 15th century and restored in the early 20th century. In addition to religious use, it served the city administration: the councils were gathered there and the seal for municipal acts was kept there. Today it also hosts outdoor weddings.
The oldest market in the city, heir of the Arab souk, between counters, "abandoned" sellers and street food.

Civic Museum of Religious Art established on September 7, 2002 in the fourteenth-century church of Sant'Emidio and named after Nicola Filotesio, called Cola dell'Amatrice: more than 80 works from the churches of Amatrice and the hamlets, including the Madonna with Child and San Giovannino di Cola (1527), the fifteenth-century processional crosses of Pietro Vannini (from Pinaco and Preta) and a Madonna with Child from the second half of the thirteenth century by Cossito.
the MiC card (updated to 2021) indicates Mar-dom 10-18 times but the ticket office is closed every day; contact the museum (tel. 039 21927037)
The simplicity of Cistercian brick in the Milanese countryside.

The stream has dug the granite forming two waterfalls in succession, with a larger pool and other smaller pools of crystal clear water between granite walls; they can be reached on foot through the spot with age-old junipers and asphodles, passing next to a dam and a hydroelectric power plant of the Flumendosa high system.
The baths of the Roman city.
A medieval baptistery on the square.

Started in 1577 on a project by Bartolomeo Scapitta and consecrated in 1627, it is three naves with vaults and eight pillars in local stone; the main Baroque altar is inlaid black bardiglio marble. It preserves an ancon signed by Scapitta and dated 1619, a canvas of Moncalvesca area with St. Francis who establishes the Tertiaries, late sixteenth century frescoes in the left aisle, the body of St. Justin martyr and a nineteenth-century organ. Visitable during functions.

A noble residence of the fourteenth century called Casa Gillino, probably home of the first lords of Ormea: in the façade sculpted panels in black stone, a bifora with storied glass and a black marble frieze above the door. You can see it from the outside.
One of the best preserved Cistercian cloisters in Veneto.
The sea of Ionic Salento.

On the Pradis plateau, more than 500 meters in the heart of the Carnic Alps, hundreds of karst cavities; the visit includes the Cave of the Madonna, the Orrido with waterfalls, natural arches and caves, and a ring walk over the gorge. Free for children under 6 years old, people with disabilities and residents; guided tours for groups by reservation (€10-12).
The oldest inscription of the village.
A large ceramic plastic that reconstructs the city as it was around 1300, with all its towers; the entrance is free, with free offer.
The island's symbol faraglioni.
Beech trees and high-altitude meadows an hour from Rome.

On the site of Gibellina, a few kilometers from the new city, Alberto Burri covered the ruins with white concrete and lime castings that reproduce the cracks left by the earthquake: it is considered one of the greatest land art works in the world and a monument to the earthquake of 1968. Next to the opera there was only one wall of the house; since the eighties the Cretto also acts as a stage for theatre performances.
18th century cathedral designed by Francesco Gallo, next to the bishop's palace.
A labyrinth of alleyways between the Ausoni Mountains.

Ancient village of narrow streets, high and centenarian palaces and ancient cellars, gathered around squares described as sobriety monumental. In the sixteenth century the Strada Priula connected Morbegno to Bergamo, making it a point of passage between the Republic of Venice and the north.

Baronial castle on a high rock formation on top of the village, from which dominates the valley; in 1898 it was indicated as baronial castle of Sele. The complex remains a few walls, damaged by the earthquake of 23 November 1980.

At about 3 km north-west of the city, at the foot of the mountains of the Badessa, a sanctuary of the seventeenth century with a frescoed Basilian crypt, where according to tradition the saint hid in 68 to escape the persecutions of Nero, and a source attributed to him. Not far away, surrounded by greenery, the rock sanctuary of San Biagio, carved into the rock with Byzantine frescoes from the 12th century. Visits on request.
One hundred thousand shells from the seas of the world.

State since 2001, it is the most important monumental testimony of the Celtic culture of Golasecca (XII-V century BC) in north-western Italy, identified in the nineteenth century and excavated from the end of the century. Three circular funeral enclosures and two rectangular 8th-VII century BC are visible, delimited by large stones (the cromlech), with tombs grouped in small groups probably familiar; the cinerary urns with ceramic, bronze and iron sets are at the Civic Museum of Sesto Calende and at the Castello Sforzesco in Milan. For the visit the Park of Ticino refers to its authorized naturalistic guides.
The waterfall hidden in the heart of Linas.
The Quaternary caves.
A unique clay landscape.

The square houses the Fontanone, the Roman cistern of the III-I century BC, which within the walls guaranteed water even during a siege, and the Convent of St. Francis of 1630 with cloister, church and portico with four arches, historical residence restored in 1984.
The mother abbey of Valnerina and Precian surgery.
Two nineteenth-century palaces in the country.

In the hamlet of Piazze, it is the eighteenth-century reconstruction of a fifteenth-century building, with granite portal and a single nave interior of two bays with side chapels, decorated with white stuccoes and gold, frescoes in the medallions of the vaults and some canvases.

Sa Trebina Longa (812 m) is the highest peak of Mount Arci, a neck, that is a fossil volcanic duct. The pine forest of Is Benas can be reached on foot or by mountain bike from Morgongiori, along a path with springs, waterfalls, caves, walls for clean climbing and wild horses. The park houses the largest obsidian deposit in Sardinia; the entrance is free.

The capital of the Val di Sole, rebuilt after the fire of 1892: around the square with the decanal church of Santa Maria Assunta are the Museo della Civiltà Solandra in the former palazzo pretorile, the Venetian Segheria of the eighteenth century and, in Pondasio, the Fucina Marinelli, one of the few hydraulic forges still operating in the Alps.
A house of the fifteenth century.
The view that gives the name to the village.
18th century church with its imposing façade; next to a panoramic terrace with views of the territory up to the Alpine chain.

Small museum of sacred art in the premises next to the basilica, with paintings, sculptures, furnishings and vestments from the late fourteenth to the eighteenth century coming from churches and convents of the territory. The masterpiece is the Annunciation of Blessed Angelico (1432-1440); there are works of Scheggia, brother of Masaccio, already in San Lorenzo, Mariotto di Cristofano, Jacopo del Sellaio, Domenico di Michelino, Giovanni da San Giovanni and the triptych of the Trinity between Saints of Mariotto of Nardo from the Pieve.
The temple from acoustic concert.

The square is the heart of the village and is dominated by the Collegiate Church of Santa Lucia, of ancient origins and rebuilt in neoclassical style; around the eighteenth-century buildings Egidi, Farsinelli, De Scrilli, Rossi, Ciarrocchi and Simonetti.
Hills of vineyards and olive trees as far as the eye can see.
A bronze statue about 3 meters high by the sculptor Hermann Mejer, on the seafront next to the Lama Monachile, dedicated to the songwriter of ... In blue painted by blue ("Volare") born in Polignano.
visits only by reservation (Visit Bergamo)
Visit Cuneese indicates it is temporarily closed and invites you to contact the museum before visiting
The most elegant building in Scanno.

Dedicated to the Roman ship sunk near Spargi around 120 BC with hundreds of wine amphorae and canteen pottery: the central piece is the life-size reconstruction of a section of the hull with 202 amphorae stoked; it also exhibits on-board objects and anchors in lead.
Savoca's peasant life.
temporarily closed for renovation work, date of reopening not known (Sardinia Cultura)

The main palaces date back to the Cinque-Seventh century: the Bishop's Palace next to the Cathedral, with the chapel of San Basilio; Palazzo Nugent, built on the medieval castle and enclosing Porta Maggiore or Sant'Eufemia, residence of the Riario Sforza in the eighteenth century; Palazzo D'Amato Cantorio (XV century) and Palazzo Janora, home of the historian Michele Janora, both bugnati in via Roma; Palazzo Arsia in via Sant'Angelo, with the motto Palazzo Rizzi in Via Antica Tribuna.

At the end of the course Carlo Alberto the Clock Gate, or Porta Castello, introduces to Terravecchia, interweaving of alleys, narrow passages and arches of Arab-Norman origin. The old town, built inside the medieval and Renaissance walls, preserves palaces with courtyard and stairway, houses with profferlo staircase, churches and chapels, some private palaces are abandoned.
In an old mill, objects of agricultural work and craftsman and some horned masks of the Carnival.

About 12 hectares in the north-western part of the terrace of Pian delle Vigne, where the archaeological remains blend with greenery and a centuries-old olive grove; excavations from the nineteenth century and then in 1912-1914 to Piano delle Vigne and on the hill of Nolio Carozzo. The route touches the remains of a large public building, classical houses with wells and furnaces and the sacred building of Calderazzo, excavated between 2014 and 2018 near the place of discovery of Orsi.

At the foot of the village, two 19th century watermills, rare examples of hydraulic factories in the province, restored: the upstream mill houses an ancient art museum with didactic function, the downstream one is a recreational space. From the storage tanks, the pool is obtained .Mulini, with panoramic view.
The garden of agricultural tools.

Outside the medieval walls, the basilica with its shapes that intertwine influences and styles, with cosmatesque floors, Etruscan sarcophagi in the left nave, frescoes and crypt; escaped the earthquake of 1971.
A walk through the moor between water lilies and birds.
Surfing at the pier or quiet bathroom at the Stone.

Wanted by Carlo Alberto on the proposal of Bishop Charvaz, it was completed in 1844 on a project by Ernesto Melano: neoclassical facade, unique nave under a very high dome, fresco of San Maurizio and 442 rosettes of the painter Fea, pale of Ayres, Serrangeli and Biscarra and organ Hill of 1844. Next door, the Priory with cloister covered and two sundials.

Fishermen's village born in 1885 from 45 families displaced from Asinara, at the north-western end of Sardinia: the beach of Pelosa with its Aragonese tower, Capo Falcone, ponds, the Saline beach and the Tonnara Museum; from the port you leave for the Asinara National Park.
Theatre frescoed by Bagnara, the same author of the Phoenix of Venice; it is the center of the city's cultural life.

The church houses the Civic Museum of Sacred Art: 17th century paintings, works by the Crivellesque school and the oil altarpiece on the table . Antonio Abate enthroned, S. Antonio da Padova e S. Job: (2,25 x 1,70 m) by Vincenzo Pagani (1490 circa-1568); a reliquary with remains of many saints and a fragment of cross, probably medieval, considered of the cross of Christ, gift of Niccolò IV.

The Riposto-Torre Archirafi promenade, built under Commissioner Grimaldi and extended in the sixties to the pier foraneo, leads to the quiet fishing village of Torre Archirafi, where was built the "Scalo di Alaggio"; from the walk you can watch the waves break on the lava cliffs, especially at sunset.
The cathedral on the Roman forum.

Natural rock arch about 33 meters long and a couple wide, on the border between Pavullo, Lama Mocogno and Polinago; in the surroundings are found finds from the protohistory to the Middle Ages. It appears in the frescoes of the late sixteenth century by Cesare Baglione in the Sala delle Vedute of the castle of Spezzano.
The oldest church in Tyrol, in ruins.
From the view terrace of the village, on clear days, you can see the Pontine Islands.
Lai, Nivola, Strazza and Veronesi in a country washroom.
The stone of the holy doors, in Maremma.
A high-altitude nuraghe in the Tonneri woods.

Walser valley at the extreme north of Piedmont, between Blindenhorn, Punta d'Arbola and Basodino: at Frua the Toce Falls with its 143 meters jump, at Ponte the sixteenth-century Casa Forte with the Walser Museum, at the bottom of the Riale valley, the oldest Walser settlement, and the lake of Morasco.
The neoclassical church of the San Michele hamlet.
A Roman source still alive.

Lequarci, in the locality of Santa Barbara, is described as the largest waterfall of the island: a jump of almost 100 meters, wide up to 70, then another 75 meters of descent towards numerous ponds; it is formed especially in the periods of flood. The waterfalls of Lecorci, about half a kilometer from the village under the cave of Su Marmuri, are born from the underground waters that emerge from the caves and join in Lequarci after about 3 km. You can go up the river Lequarci to the top; at the entrance some services are paid.
The Marian shrine of the village.
The poor cuisine of the Soratte.
Roman mosaics on the sea.

Large pedestrian square closed by the Church of Sant'Anna, with marble balustrade, and overlooking the Palazzo dei Baroni Noto, the Town Hall, the Palazzo Sardo and the monumental Palazzo Cocuzza, neoclassical nineteenth century. At the bottom of a large staircase, St. John the Baptist has a baroque and colonnade façade that holds the bell tower; inside stuccoes, statues in alabaster of Our Lady Assunta (16th century) and a Madonna dormant in oriental iconography wax.
Bifore, porches and palaces of a noble village.
Livia and the treasures of Grumentum.
order of the Harbour office that temporarily prohibits the bathing in some areas of the bay

Municipality of the Trieste Karst, about 18 km from Trieste, known for the Giant Grotto, discovered in 1840 and opened to the public since 1908, whose Grande Sala is indicated by Touring as the largest cavity in the world open to tourists; between Sgonico and Gabrovizza, in a dolina, the Carsiana Botanical Garden collects the spontaneous flora of the Karst.

The village of Val d'Alpone is surrounded by vineyards and cherry trees: on the hill of Piazza Castello, where the ancient manor stood, there is the Romanesque church of San Salvatore with the crypt on Roman capitals; the Enomuseum Ca' Rugate tells of a century of vinification.

Borgo delle Colline Pisane 42 km from Pisa, with a medieval castle with circular plan and one of the oldest parish churches in the territory of Pisa; around the natural reserve of Lake Santa Luce, the lavender fields of the ...Valle dei Profumi and, in Pomaia, the Buddhist Institute Lama Tzong Khapa.

It was born in the 12th century from the union of neighbouring villages, with official foundation on March 14, 1123; it passed from the pontifical state to the Oliva counts. Borgo della Riviera di Levante among the most beautiful villages in Italy, narrow between the towers of San Giorgio and Santa Croce and dominated by the Genoese fortresses of Villafranca and Monleone.

Built in 1256 in late Romanesque style with Gothic elements, with fifteenth-century pronaos on the portal, after the ancient parish church on the top had been demolished for the fortress of the federian. Inside paintings, remains of frescoes, a copy of the Madonna dell'Umiltà of the 14th century, a fifteenth-century polyptych of the Venetian school and four seventeenth-century bas-reliefs attributed to Giovanni Marchiori.
Walk on the ancient capital of Italy.
Brescian geology in a walk, at the foot of Mount Orfano.

The central square has an ancient fountain with the lion of San Marco; around streets porticoed with cafés and taverns, the Loggia della Ragione with the fresco of Contarini, Palazzo Polo with the triphores, the Zen fountain of 1571 and the fifteenth-century frescoed palaces of Via Regina Cornaro.
A panoramic walk among the churches.

The village clings to the steep side of Mount San Pancrazio and the houses seem to emerge from the rock, an example of integration between architecture and landscape. Feast of Saints Cosma and Damiano with the Parade of Conche and Conocchia; typical products honey, oil, cheese, cold cuts and truffle.
In the hamlet of Puglianella, the church houses a Madonna with a wooden Child by Nino Pisano, son of Andrea.
Church of 1660 with cover in chiancarelle like the trulli; inside frescoed vaults and an ancient bas-relief in stone with the Crucifixion.
The Sienese polyptych of the fourteenth century.
The mother church reborn after the landslide of the seventeenth century.

Borgo on a rocky spur dug by the two branches of the Lama stream, famous for its tombble lace: the triangular Piazza del Popolo with Palazzo Comunale and Teatro Serpente Aureo, the Romanesque-Gothic Santa Maria della Rocca and the museum pole of Palazzo De Castellotti.

Museum dedicated to the composer and conductor Attilio Parelli (1874-1944): more than one hundred original manuscripts, including The Lovers, Hermes and Fanfulla of Lodi, also printed scores of colleagues with dedications and autographs, booklets, family photographs, diplomas and documents, donated by the heirs to the municipality.
The church of the village on the Via Francigena del Sud.
High Romanesque bell tower with cusp and bifore; inside a triumphal crucifix of the fifteenth century among the most important works of the Valdostan heritage.
The building that gives the name to the village, with the satire of the whole world.
The mother church, sober and solemn.
The tables of the school of the village.

Castello e ricetto, a building type unique in Lombardy and spread in the nearby Piedmont: the nucleus probably dates back to the X-XII centuries; in 1404 the Folperti obtained from the Visconti to expand it and build the ricetto, then passed to the Malaspina (with portico and loggia of the fifteenth century) and in 1582 to Cardinal Tolomeo Gallio, who had built chapel, garden and stables. Visconti plant with courtyard and well in brick, battlements, corner towers, moat and barbacan with drawbridge; inside Renaissance fireplaces, loggia of Bramante style and 19th century rooms. ==References====External links==* Official website
The Sardinian Romanesque in the open countryside.
Snow and large spaces under the Carrier.
The panoramic walk among the apple orchards of Lana.

Chierese hilly country gathered around the "chiocciola" of the historic center, with the medieval tower of the castle become civic bell tower, the Baroque parish church of San Giorgio di Giovan Battista Casasopra, the farmhouse and the mill of Cesole and the small museum of rural traditions of the Balbiano winery.
A sanctuary of popular devotion in the woods.
Mills still at work.
Fontanarosa's straw cart seen up close.
The speakers of the fraction.
The late Gothic in the heart of Sardinia.
The peasant life of Tuscia in two thousand objects.

Opened on December 18, 2025 on the waterfront, it exhibits the Iulia Felix, a merchant ship of Roman age recovered in the Adriatic, to tell the economy and commerce of the Upper Adriatic in Roman times. Seasonal hours: May-September Mar-dom 11-19, October-April Friday 11-18.
Classic theater with views of the Adige.

The municipality was founded in 2014 by the union of Tremezzo, Mezzegra, Lenno and Ossuccio on the western shore of Lake Como: here are Villa Carlotta, Villa del Balbianello (FAI), the Sacro Monte di Ossuccio UNESCO heritage and the Isola Comacina, the only island of the lake, connected by Greenway.
2 € (over 65 0.50 €, free under 18 years)

The parish church of the Frassinere hamlet at 948 m, built on a Romanesque building of which remains the bell tower, very renovated; enlarged between 1744 and 1749 and rebuilt in 1862, has three naves and semicircular apse, dimensions due to the fact that Frassinere was autonomous municipality until 1936. Used again in the summer months.
It occupies the highest point of the hill of Santo Pietro Belvedere and is on two levels: at the bottom the children's games, at the top the view of the Valdera hills.
An intact 19th-century house.
The animalier loved by D'Annunzio, in his country.
At the highest point of the city, a 16th century building in Bramantesco style with a civic tower and a large internal staircase; the theater that was housed there was demolished in 1934.
A Romanesque church among high altitude pastures.
An inhabited castle, with millennial tower and historic cellars.

Two small Karst lakes in the Ustica Valley, at the foot of the Faieta Hill, formed by collapses due to the erosion of groundwater; they are a wetland protected by the Ramsar Convention, one of the six of Lazio. The Fraturno, the largest and the only accessible, has banks with poplars, reeds, horseback rides, willows and small sandy beaches; the Marraone, funnel and about 20 meters lower, can be seen only from above from a fence and in dry summers can dry up. You can reach it on foot or by mountain bike from Percile, Licenza, Mandela, Riofreddo and Cineto Romano.
Square-shaped castle with angular towers, now surrounded by dense vegetation; there is a baronial palace and the ruins of the small castle called Castellaccio.
One of the oldest and most evocative abbeys in the province.
private property building (VisitLazio)
The Dominican Middle Ages of Piacenza.
Rectangular square with the remains of the sixteenth-century fortress of Orazio Gonzaga: the entrance door, a stretch of walls, a watchtower and the church of San Nicola; wide view up to Lake Garda.
The two sandy tombs that join the promontory to the coast: the clear sand Giannella and the Feniglia reachable from Porto Ercole.
An angelic ruin that dominates the plain.
Country of Lower Brescia with the parish church of Saints Peter and Paul and the church of St. Gottardo in the ancient Lazzaretto.

In the heart of the village, on the narrow road parallel to the coast, replaced the ancient church by insufficient: authorized in 1693 by the Parliament of Taggia, it was slowly built for the whole eighteenth century by the foreman revisited Girolamo Arlotti, with the help of local families like the Philippi. It has façade with stuccoes and statues, high bell tower, single nave with side chapels and Ligurian paved church of 1760; inside the canvases of Carlo Giuseppe Aicardi (1775), sculptures of Maragliano and paintings of Morgari, and the main altar in 19th century marble.
Small Renaissance church leaning on a slope.
Family beach, quieter than Riccione.
Walk in the medieval town between doors and erker.

Municipality of the Novara hills formed by Agrate and Conturbia: in Agrate the Romanesque baptistery of St. John, with the circular base of the 10th century and the octagon of the 12th, stands in front of the parish church of San Vittore, mentioned already in 976. In Conturbia the church of San Giorgio, consecrated by Bishop Litifredo, and the Faunistic Park La Torbiera, in the peat bog where remains of stilts have emerged.

Born in the seventies on the initiative of Fr Giacomo Piazzoli, parish priest of Brembo, from a first collection of about 250 nativity scenes, today it preserves more than 900 on two floors, from the eighteenth century to contemporary artists, in a former cinema. The tour includes the great work of the Neapolitan Antonio Greco (more than 20 m2 and more than 130 statues), the reconstruction of a Bergamo workshop of late nineteenth century of plaster statues, handicraft nativity scenes of Asia, Africa, Latin America and Australia, paper nativity scenes, antique prints and finds of the Holy Land; a small room houses an electronic scenery with lights and music. Visits by reservation (tel. 035 563383).
The oratory of the high city.
The façade in pink trachyte and the fifteenth-century monstrance.

Along the road to Canelli, beyond the Belbo and in front of Gaminella, is the harshest and most arid hill of the two that act as the scenery to the moon and the bonfires; Pavese describes it with its ridges and large meadows disappearing on the peaks. At his feet the house-boat of Nuto.
Walk along the water between apple orchards and chestnuts.

A company founded in 1909 by Angelo Sirianni in a small warehouse in the historic center transformed into a joinery; today an industry that combines artisan care and processing of wood and steel, with over a thousand items exported in more than 35 countries. Open on the occasion of the 2018 FAI Fall Day.

Medieval castle on top of the hill, with more than one hundred rooms on about 10,000 square meters; the tower was born as a bulwark at the end of the ninth century and at the end of the fifteenth century the Savelli transformed it into a Renaissance baronial residence. Inside the Palazzo di Troilo, the Palatium degli Ottaviani (X-XI century), the Palazzo di Giacomo, three courtyards, a chapel and four towers, with sixteenth-century frescoes from the Raphael school wanted by Troilo Savelli. From the fortress starts the Wall of the Rescue, covered walk of 83 meters with 37 wounds, escape route in case of siege, accessible in full. Not indicated times: check on the site of the Municipality.
The former convent of San Francesco hosts a valuable collection of art and the Pinacoteca civica.
The castle and the ancient emissary of the lake.

The city of honey is about 750 metres, at the extreme south of the Langhe: here the Belbo is born, protected by the Belbo Nature Reserve with its wetlands and orchids, and in the village Villa overlooks the Cuneo plain the fortified castle of Cordero di Mondovì.
The church rested on the rock.
To be checked: visits on request or during the shows
A Maratta in the historic center.
The baroque in the main square of the village.

City of the Etna Park on a lava plateau overlooking the valley of Simeto, gathered around the Norman Castle of Piazza Umberto I, home of the Archaeological Museum; in the surroundings the medieval Bridge of the Saracens on the lava forre of the Simeto, in the city the Bellini Theatre, the Mother Church and the Monastery of Saint Lucia.
A traditional mountain country.
The blue palace of Mazzoni.

Romanesque oratory with a single nave with semicircular apse and facade in hut, quoted in 1347. On the façade traces of fifteenth-century paintings; in the basin the Christ Pantocrator with the Apostles, on the apse an Annunciation and below a Madonna del Latte attributed to Joannes Maria de Rumo; on the walls sacred images of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.
The addition of Biagio Rossetti's Erculea, considered the first example of modern urbanism: wide avenues, gardens and palaces up to the Quadrivio degli Angeli.
A 12th century church that houses important works of art.
The octagonal canvases of the Manno.

Bay of about three kilometers divided with Maracalagonis by the river Geremeas: in Quartu the beach of Kala 'e Moru, golden sand and sandy seabed, and Marongiu, light and thin sand; accessible also to people with disabilities, with parking and services; with the mistral kite and windsurf arrives.
Alleys, churches and views of the plain.
Cosmè Tura, Dosso Dossi and Garofalo in the same building as the exhibitions.
The history of Castellamonte's red earth.
The protected green above the Irno Valley.

Città dei cantieri navali sull'alto Adriatico: MuCa tells a century of great ships in the working village of Panzano, the medieval fortress watches from the Karst on the theme park of the Great War, in the center the medieval museum and the contemporary art gallery, to the sea Marina Julia.
Trenches of the Great War and views of the three branches.
The largest nuraghe of Belvì Barbagia, with a view from the plateau.
A green Patriarch on the shore of Lake Cecita.
The wooden ceiling and the view from the churchyard.

Former convent of the Carmelites with the church, restored several times, today seat of the Municipal Library and municipal offices. In the church, parish since 1950, paintings by Vincenzo Manno of 1819 (Madonna del Carmelo, Madonna and San Gaetano, Holy Family), two golden wooden candlesticks and an 18th century chair.
the MiC card reports that the City has acquired the collection and transferred it to another building; home and times to verify
A liberty spa town in Valdinievole, UNESCO World Heritage Site in Europe's Great Thermal Cities since 2021.
The Romanesque cathedral.

Set up in summer 1915 under the civil cemetery and the parish church of San Lorenzo, expanded in the 1930s with the remains of the cemeteries near the front and reordered in 1971-72: it gathers in four large crypts the remains of 2,500 Austro-Hungarian soldiers, 750 of whom unknown, along the perimeter the monuments of the cemeteries of field.

Cathedral of 1739, next to the Episcopio (1696) and the former Bishop's Seminary, frescoed in 1780 by Francesco Palumbo; it has 12 marble altars and two bell towers with semi-cupole covered with yellow-green majolica.

In 1895 16-year-old Albert Einstein walked through Rondanina, Fascia, Montebruno and Propata: the route, about 48 km in the Parco dell'Antola, was restored from the Park with signs and panoramic points. From Rondanina, in an open position on the Cassingheno valley, climb in about two hours to the Bric di Rondanina (1,340 m).
The massif that frames Alagna, with Punta Dufour at 4634 meters and Punta Gnifetti at 4554, the theatre of the history of mountaineering.
The concentric layout of the houses of Pollenzo follows the amphitheatre of ancient Pollentia; the remains of the theatre can be reached through the Albertino complex.
The cathedral in front of the sea.
Climbing 14 km without traffic on the ancient Menador road, between alpine pastures and traces of the line of the Great War front.

The village of Rezzo is home to the stone-stones active between the 14th and 15th centuries, whose works are found throughout the valley of Giara, in Mendatica and Montegrosso Pian Latte; they worked in the major yards of the Ponente until the Collegiata di Tenda. In the historic center a signposted route of the museum        .Strade di pietra .
The last of the three towers.
The medieval nucleus around the Red Hill, closed by walls with seven doors.
The sculptor of the Modena countryside.
The Civic Museums from the Longobard period to the Quadreria dell'Ottocento, up to the Sala Azzurra with the starry sky ceiling.
The mother church of the little Urbe.
Three levels of history under your feet.
In restoration since June 2025, expected duration about two years
A nineteenth-century mill that still spins the turbines.
Birdwatching in the last wetland of the former lake.
The history of the Sabini from the Paleolithic to the Middle Ages.

The castle dominates the historic centre and is one of the best preserved medieval fortresses in western Sicily. The museum exhibits above all the excavations of the excavations started in the eighties in the Strait district, known for the Neolithic ditches, and of the necropolis of Belice with grotticella tombs and chamber of the middle and late Bronze, including ceramics of the Naro-Partanna style and bell towers; didactic panels tell the peoples of Belice before the Greeks. It also houses an archive of parchments from the fourteenth century donated by the Turrisi-Griffeo family and, in the armory, a gallery with a fourteenth-century altarpiece and a San Tommaso da Villanova attributed to Silvestre Ratto da Mazara.
The view from the mast on the Marocche and Alto Garda.

Ecomuseum in an intact natural environment where the canal Scortico flows into the Canalbianco (Tartaro-Po di Levante): an example of industrial archaeology of Polesine that still regulates water for agriculture in droughts and helps to prevent floods. It is part of the Polesine Provincial Museum System and organizes educational visits on bread, ancient cereals and renewable energies.
In the parks of Nervi, the Galleria d'Arte Moderna, the Frugone Collections and the Wolfsoniana, dedicated to art, design and advertising graphics of the early twentieth century.
the description of the area of Tourism Mantova calls it Santa Maria della Carità and the date to the eighteenth century
On the highest point of the village, in white stone on a pre-existing temple of Hercules, is the oldest monument of Ausonia; at the end of September there is celebrated the feast of the patron.

In the center of the village, built around 1200 at the behest of Pomponio de Magistris, bishop of Terracina, restored and reconsecrated in 1604; the Romanesque altar has a sculptural work attributed to Bernini or his school.
Three thousand years of nolan history.
Sannite walls with views of the valley.

It rises on a hill on the valley of Vitalba, built on Norman structures: the current plant is Swabian (from 1242), hunting and leisure residence of Frederick II, with angioin additions. Rectangular plant with corner towers and two courtyards: in the greater the Fourth of the Emperor, the Fourth of the Queen and the Palatine Chapel, in the lower the mast. Since 1531 it was a feud of the Doria, in 1969 donated to the State; on the first floor it houses the Museum of Lucanian Emigration. Free admission with access to download on the platform Italian Museums or at the totem; spring-summer times Thursday-Sunday 9:30-13:30 and 15:30-19:30, autumn-winter Saturday and Sunday 9-14.
A Romanesque gem in local stone on the way of the travelers.
The Catalan market.
The church of the village of the mills.

In the village of Alpicella exhibits the finds of the Riparo under the rock of Fenestrelle, discovered in 1977 by Mario Fenoglio: the shelter was frequented in the Neolithic, then abandoned and reused by hunters and shepherds in the Bronze Age.

A marked path of 4.5 km (about 1 hour and 10, +290 m) starting from the parking lot of Gritz, next to the restored jassàra, and passing through the Dossetti, Baston and Moscarda huts to the Bocca di Selva refuge.

Digged about six meters below ground, it collects over a thousand sculptures and jewels in coral and hard stones from the fifteenth century to today, from the East to Italy; among the pieces a nineteenth-century parure for Paolina Bonaparte and a large cameo on shell engraved in ten years. The collection was born in 1934.

Next to the museum, an outdoor eco-museum that promotes agricultural practices to protect the historical agricultural landscape, such as the "Piantata Reggiana" (Piantata Reggiana), in 2011 there was inaugurated a row of ancient fruits of Emilia-Romagna.
The palace of a small papal principality.
View of the lake from above.

In Sant'Anna di Valdieri, the only town in the park all year round: itinerary, museum, bakery and shop-osteria dedicated to the cultivation and processing of rye (----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The rural life of the High Ionian in an eighteenth-century palace.
The frescoes of the Zoppo di Gangi.

Built after the middle of the seventeenth century by Cardinal Federico Caccia, he then passed to Ferrero, Gallarati Scotti and Simonetta; in 1972 the heirs of Countess Teresa Bollini Mocenigo Soranzo sold it to the municipality, which has its seat with library, museum and picture gallery. The stairs of honour in pink granite climbs into an octagonal room with four eighteenth-century statues of the Seasons; on the south façade the coats of arms of the Hunt and of Pope Innocent XII and a large baroque sundial. The romantic garden has camellias, azalee, rhododendrons and palm trees and a rare Chinese michaelia at the beginning of the camellias avenue.
The lookout on the city.

Church probably at the end of the seventeenth or early eighteenth century, destroyed by the earthquake of 1860 and rebuilt in 1878, a single nave with barrel vault, decorated in 1944-45. On the central wall the image of the Madonna and Child in coloured sandstone, found on March 25, 1621 in Capo d'Acqua; the feast is celebrated on the first or second Sunday of August.
MiC card (updated 2020) indicates the closed museum every day

On the bank of Lugagnano and along Via Roma follow Villa Mörlin Visconti (neoclassical, 1825-27), Villa Frotta Eusebio (XVIII century, with a scenographic wall masking a blind wall), Villa Trivulzio (neoclassical of the late eighteenth century, with oratory open towards the village), Villa Krentzlin (XVII-XVIII century) and Villa Clari Monzini, built in the second half of the seventeenth century, restored in 2007 and now divided into private houses, with the oratory of Sant'Anna; at the end of Via Roma the sixteenth-century Palazzo Mantegazza.

Built between the 12th and 15th centuries next to a view on the Biellese, it has a facade with buttresses, rosette and terracotta decorations around the portal. Inside, two paintings from the end of the sixteenth century attributed to the Vercellese school and the pulpit carved in 1712 by Carlo Francesco Auregio Termine, among the most important examples of Biella's wooden sculpture.
Trees become stone, just a stone's throw from the village.

Country of marble artists and sculptors in the north-east of the province of Varese, famous for the quarries of "pietra di Viggiù" worked by the Picasass and for the artists (Butti, Giudici, Longhi, Piatti, Argenti, Galli) active in Rome between 1500 and 1650; in the park of the villa of the sculptor Enrico Butti the Civic Museums Viggiutesi gather the gipsoteca with 87 its plasters and the Museum of the 20th century with the Viggiute sculpture of the 20th century.
The Roman finds of the Pegognaga plain.
the source indicates that the visit requires reservation
The center dedicated to the architect Pistoia, with windows overlooking Piazza del Duomo.
Mountain peasant life.

Recognizable for its white Baroque façade, the circular dome and the two bell towers that mark the view of the town, it was consecrated in 1801. The main altar is designed by Alessandro Antonelli and the canvas with the Estasi di Santa Teresa is by Luca Giordano.

Set up in the spa area built by Caracalla for legionaries, it exhibits Roman finds and reproductions of the military equipment of the legion dedicated to Albano from 202 A.D. Sunday opens the 2nd and 4th of the month, alternating with the Civic Museum.
The walk of about one kilometer on the trail of Philip and Philippine Lippi between the Duomo and Palazzo Pretorio.
The Italian garden, the park with large trees, bosso hedges, statues, fountains and greenhouses, with the entrance to the large eighteenth-century fountain with horseshoe; open from May to October.

It preserves the Altar of Ratchis, a Lombard masterpiece with bas-reliefs once painted, the Baptistery of Callisto with octagonal plan with seven arches on marble columns, and the treasure of goldsmiths, codes and liturgical furnishings.
The gates of the brick city.

Medieval village about 1,050 metres above the Aniene valley, the highest in the province of Rome, leads to the Parco dei Monti Simbruini and for two centuries the town of artists: from the Fortress and the Collegiate with the Museum of the Mountain to the Sculpted Mountain with sculptures and murals in the rock, up to the meadows of Campaeglio.

In an olive grove of the sixteenth century, the Leonardo Galleries, a library of 40,000 volumes, the launcher Vega, the only fragment of the Moon exposed in an Italian museum and the submarine Enrico Toti.
Church of the thirteenth century, the oldest in the city.
The imposing cathedral of Ragusa Superiore, at the intersection of Via Roma and Corso Italia, with large facade, high bell tower and a panoramic terrace.
The house of Carducci's youth.
A stretch on foot of the historical path in the green of Garfagnana.
