It gathers about 1,300 objects and photographs on the crafts and crafts of the territory and reconstructs ancient domestic environments, in 12 rooms divided into four sections: peasant civilization (tool for oil, wine and wheat), arts and crafts (carpenters, shoemakers, barbers, spinning machines and weavers, masons, watchmakers), living environments (costumes, bedrooms, kitchens) and curiosity of communication (instruments, electrical and computer equipment, video library, prints). Accessible to the disabled.
Top of the eastern Pollino.
The house of old.

The honorary column in red marble of Verona with decorations in Carrara marble, surmounted by a bronze eagle, inaugurated on 18 June 1922 with the contribution of the families of the country; on the side towards the town hall the marble statue of Carrara Restored after the early 2000s, it is one of the symbols of the community with the oratory of Monte Purga.
The story of a small imperial state between Umbria and Tuscany.

Country between the Supramonte and the Gulf of Orosei: the nuragic village of Serra Orrios, the way to Tiscali in the valley of Lanaittu and, on the sea, Cala Gonone with the Caves of Bue Marino and Cala Luna.
A rare eighteenth-century city founded, designed at a small table.

The municipality of Canavese was founded around the Abbey of Fruttuaria, founded in 1003 by Guglielmo da Volpiano and rebuilt in the eighteenth century: you can visit the abbey church with the excavations of the first abbey and the mosaic of the griffons, the surviving Romanesque bell tower and the fifteenth-century shelter.
The reclamation told by those who lived it.
Orphic laminette.
The sanctuary was born from the great flood of 1705, at the end of the tree-lined avenue.
On Mondays and Fridays the main square is filled with benches; during the year it also hosts shows, concerts and sporting events.
A thirteenth-century castle became a village.
A fresco from Perugia school.
The fauna of the Sibillini in the same palace as the art gallery.
Alleys and views of the Flumendosa.
The voice of Sardinia in its native country.
The pantheon of the illustrious Sicilians.
Sanctuary on Monte Carmine, a few kilometers from the village, surrounded by the woods of the countryside of Avigliano.
On the paths of the Great War above the lake.

Polygonal walls of the 14th-XV century, today partly incorporated into more recent buildings; going up towards the square a fifteenth-century palace with decorations in terracotta and acute arch of Sienese taste; on the square the Town Hall and Casa Licini. The tour of the center offers views of the nearby villages, the hills towards the sea and the Sibillini.
Hydro-electric basins can be reached on foot from the village of Grevo or by asphalt road from Isola di Cevo, with panoramic views of the valley bottom of Sellero.
Contemporary art in the woods, even with the dog.
Round of houses porticoed by painted facades.
Emerald sea, cliffs to reach on foot and the pond of birds.
Palace decorated by the Futurist painter Gerardo Doctors.
A 36-metre-long donkey-back bridge that crosses the Raganello stream with a single arch; symbol of the Pollino Park, its construction is linked to myths and legends.
Water, mills and first electricity.

The great early Christian cemetery; the nearby funerary area of Vigna Cassia, with a community cemetery and five private hypogeans of the III-V centuries, is visited on request to the Pontifical Commission for Sacred Archaeology.
On the highest point of the village, with Aragonese towers.
The gentlemen's bridge.
The village of Barolo.

Small village on a hill on the Tyrrhenian side of Messinese, known for its 16th century pharmacy with 238 vases of the workshop of the Patanazzi and for the castle with baronial palace that dominates the village.
Three of the rare medieval Exultet rolls.

Fishing village with narrow streets and steps towards the lake, the parish church of Saints Bartholomew and Nicola with Romanesque bell tower dating back to the 13th century and the 17th century sanctuary in a panoramic position, whose name recalls the peace of the Pyrenees of 1659; from here the ancient Strada Regina rises to the Sasso Rancio.
Animals from the park up close, among woods and old crafts.
Crystals of the High Tauern.

Borgo stop among the most beautiful villages in Italy, with a triangular plan on a hill above Valdaso, entirely surrounded by walls and marked by the Epthagonal tower of the twelfth century and the fourteenth-century Clock Tower; in the Town Hall the gallery with the great altarpiece of Vincenzo Pagani.

Akrai, the oldest sub-colony of Syracuse, was founded in 664 B.C. on the hill of the Chromon. Theater (between III and II century BC according to sources) and the bouleuterion, the decuman with lava flooring, a circular spa building, the foundations of a temple of the second half of the 6th century BC considered of Aphrodite, the side-shaped of the Carved and the Carnival with catacombs and early Christian hypogeans and the Feral Temples are visited.

In the historic centre, very wide, it has a Latin cross plan, three naves with domes and two side bell towers; the first stone was laid in the mid-sixteenth century on a place of worship of the thirteenth century. On the high altar, in a marble tabernacle, the wooden painted statue of the Madonna with the Child and a rose, brought according to the tradition by medieval sailors; during the works of 1672 under the altar there would be a vase of fragrant water, origin of devotion to the Madonna della Rosa, celebrated on Sunday before the Ascension with the blessing of roses.
The sea of Chioggia, Blue Flag, meets the Venetian lagoon; the sand is very fine, clear and rich in minerals, associated with psamotherapy. Along the dam you can see the fishing scales.

Dedicated to the Turinese painter Giacomo Vittone, who was its promoter, purchased and restored in 1965 and managed by the municipalities of Riva del Garda, Arco and Tenno: he holds a collection of works, hosts exhibitions and events and is a residence for artists visiting from all over Europe.
Alleys, fountains and the narrowest house.
The view of the fort.
The main church of the village, built around 1480 by Blessed Francesco Marino, born in Zumpano, on the model of the Mother Church of Cosenza.
An ancient parish church on the slopes of Calvana.
A fourteenth-century church on the river.
A lava flow in the woods around the volcano off.
The Last Judgement of the Gangi Zoop.

Small oratory with circular plan with hemispheric dome, completed around 1860, erected by Duke Francesco V of Austria-Este to thank for having escaped the attack on 16 November 1848 of the Mazzini Luigi Rizzati of Cavezzo. It rises in a roundabout of the State Road 12 of Canaletto.
The first cemetery built in Sardinia after the edict of Saint Cloud, not far from the center, with tombstones in Logudorian.
Next to the ethnographic museum, another restored mill houses exhibitions and cultural events.
Among the largest squares in the city, overlooking the Po and in front of the hill, with historic cafes.
The fortress dam that crosses the valley.
The sacred art of Bergamo in a unique path.
The mosaic garden overlooking the coast.

Romanesque parish already mentioned in 973 and built in the middle of the 11th century, in pebbles of river with fishbone, three naves and three apses with elevated presbytery on a vaulted crypt, the only Romanesque crypt left in Novara. The cycle of frescoes, of about 1060, is among the most important of the Romanesque in northern Italy: Last Judgment in counterfaced, Christ blessing with the Deacons, Apparitions of St. Michael in Gargano; later the Resurrection attributed to Franceschino Cagnola and St. Michael of Joannes Maria de Rumo. Abandoned in the sixteenth century for the new parish, it rises in the municipal cemetery.
The oldest church of Troy and the Easter rites.
Ales rises on the eastern slopes of Monte Arci, rich in obsidian deposits linked to prehistoric activity; the regional park includes the centuries-old Lecceta di Aquafrida.
Where it all started.
The shrine of the plateau.

Monumental entrance in golden stone on the eastern side, with a solemn and well preserved exterior façade; in the center there was the Lion of St. Mark, destroyed by Napoleon after the Treaty of Campoformio of 1797, and a reconstruction at the beginning of the bridge shows the door as it was. Next to it stands the neoclassical Caserma Francesco I (1822), today Scuola di Polizia di Stato.
Eight centuries of Sabauda history in the heart of the city.

Completed in 579 by Bishop Elijah on the site of a basilica of the fourth century and dedicated to the Aquileian protomartyrs; three naves on columns, mosaic floor with Byzantine geometric motifs, the sea wave and about 40 inscriptions of donors, golden silver altarpiece of Donato Mazzalorsa, 11th century ambo and mausoleum with Elia's monogram. The fifteenth-century bell tower is crowned by the Angelo Michele ('Anzolo San Michele'), symbol of Grado.

Centre of the Lower Modena with the 14th-century Estense fortress with a square plan, seriously affected as the historic center by the 2012 earthquake; surroundings with the botanical garden La Pica in San Biagio in Padule and the seventeenth-century church of Rivara, along the Modena-Finale Emilia bike path.
13th century ruins under the castle.
The bridge over Tanaro connecting the city to the Citadel, designed by American architect Richard Meier and opened in 2016: a single white span of over 176 meters.
One of the oldest trees in the world.
Built by Roberto il Guiscardo in 1061 on a pre-existing fortress, it remains the ruins in the highest part of the village.

On the plateau at the south entrance of the village the Requesens built it in the sixteenth century on the ruins of an Arabic fortress; destroyed by the earthquake of 1693 and rebuilt smaller, it was a convent of Minors Observing in the eighteenth century and cemetery in the nineteenth century. There are still some walls in local white stone.

Borgo about 500 meters between the Empire Valley and the Val Prino, between dry walls and Taggiasca olive groves, with 360 degrees panorama on mountains, valleys and sea; preserves the museum     Â Lazzaro Acquarone Â (sacred art and ethnography), the fifteenth-century church of the Magdalena, national monument, and the church of Santo Stefano next to the lake.
The Roman city from which Fossombrone was born.
Neoclassical Palace of 1782-92, museum house of about 8,000 square meters, with the sixteenth-century Sala dello Zodiaco; in 1810 the trial was held at Andreas Hofer.

The microclimate favors black truffle: Laconi has the most abundant harvest in Sardinia, the season goes from December to June and every June there is a dedicated festival; in the village there are oil, preserves and truffle honey.
Mandatory, when it reopens

Baths of Hellenistic age found in 1957 during the excavations in Via Europa, behind the hospital Vittorio Emanuele, and destroyed in 282 BC, when the city was razed to the ground: according to Italia.it is the oldest thermal complex so far discovered in Italy. Open every day 9-19.

Born in 1997 as a private initiative and then became public, it is in the Palazzo Fioritto and preserves about 3,000 finds, largely donated by the inhabitants, in a path from the Paleolithic to recent traditions: Roman finds, fossils and prehistoric tools, the 19th century stable-cellar, plows from the 17th to the early 20th century, the carpenter's shops, roaster, shoemaker, blacksmith and tinker, the peasant's house and the traditional Sannicandrese costume; with photo library of about 3,000 images and recordings of songs and oral tradition. Open in July, August and September from 20 to 23; in winter only by reservation (tel. 0882 472369).

In Pegli, among the most original romantic parks, wanted by the Marquis Ignazio Pallavicini and created from 1840 by Michele Canzio, set designer of the Teatro Carlo Felice; in the villa the Museum of Ligurian Archaeology.

Country 532 meters on the eastern side of Mount Guadagnolo, which owes its name to the villa where Caio Calpurnio Pisone took refuge after the conspiracy against Nerone; it houses the hemp museum, the rural church of Santa Vittoria and the eighteenth-century Madonna della Neve, from which climbs the path Karol Wojtyla towards the Mentorella.

City at the foot of the Apuan Alps born as a Roman outpost along the road between Lucca and Luni ('Campus Major'), with medieval plant, the Collegiate and the Badia di San Pietro on the Via Francigena, two civic museums, the hamlet of graffiti of Casoli and the beach of Lido di Camaiore in Versilia.

Austro-Hungarian fortress built in 1860-1861 at 1,538 meters to defend the last stretch of the road of the Tonale, the first work of the fortified system of the pass; well preserved, semicircular plant on two levels, houses an exhibition of finds and relics of the White War recovered from the recouping of Vermiglio, with introductory clips, luminous panels and touch screen station on the other forts of the area. Partially accessible.
Four centuries of culture.
The stele statues and the view of the gulf.
The peasant memory of the Morronese territory.

Built in the first decades of the 12th century by the Camaldolese monks in the plain of Saccargia, about 5 km from the village: 20 m long, 7 m wide and 14, with bichromatic façade in white limestone and black basalt and an imposing bell tower recognizable from afar. The apse preserves rare Romanesque frescoes, the only survivors in Sardinia. The feast of the Most Holy Trinity is celebrated on Sunday after Pentecost. Open every day 9-18 according to Italia.it.
A stone monastery over a castle.
The Romanesque Marche along the Potenza.
The Madonna di Calena venerated by the village.
The life of shepherds and wool.

On the hill of San Teodoro a Nicastro, fortified by the Normans in the second half of the 11th century and enlarged by Frederick II with the pentagonal mast: four cylindrical towers, bastions and buttresses with loggia; after the earthquake of 1638 lost its military function.
The hilly town of the Vomano valley: in the hamlet of Guardia Vomano stands the church of San Clemente al Vomano, from the 11th century, with the oldest Norman ciborium in Abruzzo.
The peasant past of Campidano.
Ancient Romanesque parish destroyed by the Turks in 1554, now recognized as a national monument.
A 15th century complex, born in a period of wars and epidemics, important religious, historical and ethnic testimony of the country.
the city card does not indicate times: opening linked to the events of the association A.Mu.Si
Legendary ruins on a cliff in the woods.

Irregular building built in several phases between the thirteenth and sixteenth centuries: it houses the famous Madonna with the Child who holds the grapes of Michael Pacher, and the adjoining chapel Egerer has frescoes of the school of Pacher.
Tight entrance gate (65 cm) with 8 cm step
One of the most complete frescoed cycles in Tuscany.
Roman stones and views of the valley.

Built in 1870 by engineer Timoleone Crocchi, inspired by the Pergola of Florence, and inaugurated on August 6, 1872. In 1925 a cyclone destroyed its roof; after the war it was cinema and dance hall, closed in the seventies and reopened in 1985, after the restoration, with       ÂPensaci, Giacomino! by Pirandello.
Visit only with guided tour in German on request (suedtirol.info)
Almost a thousand years of history, from Pontida's oath to the cloisters.
The gates, the tower and the castle of the village on the Fortore.
At the bottom of the Church, in the heart of the ancient castrum: here Pellizza painted between 1892 and 1901 some great social works with the peasants as models.

The oldest part of Casteggio rises on the hill of the Pistornile and its slopes. The municipal itinerary touches Vittoria Alata, the arcades built around 1767 to enlarge the Piazza del Pistornile (where the market was held on Wednesday), Casa Marangoni, which between 1896 and 1899 hosted Albert Einstein, the parish church, Palazzo Mezzabarba (original only towards Via Baratta) and the Certosa Cantù.
after years of inagibility the complex has been redevelopmentd since 2021; the source does not say if the gallery is now set up and visitable
The Romanesque outside the door.
Two karst lakes hidden in the woods.

Heart of the Calabrian side of the Pollino National Park, a village of stone houses with a view overlooking the Timpa di San Lorenzo, with most of the Raganello Gorges in its territory and the churches of San Lorenzo and Carmine.

On the eastern side of Mount Catalfano, in the locality Campofranco-Olivetano, a vast area of burials excavated in limestone, from the beginning of the third century BC at least to the end of the first century A.D.: loculi for a single burial and tombs to one or two hypogeic rooms with dromos and steps. She returned to visit, for the first time after 15 years, with a project of the East Metropolis LAG under the scientific direction of the Archaeological Park.
The golden tabernacle.
Former aqueduct transformed into a cultural space.
The place of origin of the Lot.
The oldest source of Leonessa.
The Apennine suede up close.

In the thirteenth-century castle of the Ruspolis, on two floors: urns of the necropolis of the Sorbo, orientalizing kits and the crater of Eufronio (about 515 BC) and the kylix of Onesimos, returned to Italy in 2015.
Ancient mule track recovered that starts from Campomolino and climbs to the sanctuary passing through the villages Nero, Chiotti and Chiappi, through a basin rich in vegetation.

The village is still surrounded by the walls of the medieval castle; there is the sixteenth-century town hall flanked by a high civic tower. On the hills around, patrician villas with gardens built between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries.
Fortified residence of the fifteenth century with ogival windows and terracotta decorations, seat of the Civic Museum of Archaeology, History and Art with the finds of Pollenzo.

Opened in 1996 in the rural buildings of the Palazzo Vaccà Berlinghieri and run by a local association, exhibits tools donated by the inhabitants along a path between warehouses and cellars dedicated to the sharecropping from the eighteenth to the first twentieth century, from harvest to sowing, harvest and crushing, with an underground reconstruction of the life of the farm. The Casa Museo, opened in 2005, recalls the surgeon Andrea Vaccà of the University of Pisa, doctor of Paolina Bonaparte, with surgical instruments and a library of medical treatises linked to the Pisan years of Leopardi, Byron and Shelley. In summer open on Sunday 10:30-12:30 and 15:30-19:30, other days upon reservation; free entry and guided tours.
Baroque church built in 1625 and dedicated in 1662 by the Basilian monks to their saint, whose remains it preserves; the interior is decorated with stucco.

The medieval nucleus, built according to tradition on the ancient Latin city of Apiola, is enclosed by a whole preserved city walls, with twelve cylindrical towers recently restored. Inside, paved and winding alleys, steep steps, arches and stone houses, accessible only on foot, with views of Monte Faggeto and the Gulf of Gaeta; in Piazza del Municipio a secular elm is the meeting point of the village.

Opened in 1978 in the Torre del Castello Marchesale, it extends from the ancient stables to the top of the tower: tools of blacksmiths and weavers, clothes and tools of the peasants, the reconstruction in scale 1:1 of a peasant house and a small section of finds of the Roman age of the territory; documents also the fortified architecture of the Vastese. Managed by the Vastese Foundation. According to the MiC card is open in July, August and the first weekend of September on Saturday and Sunday (9-12 and 16-19), in the other months by reservation 24 hours in advance; the municipality indicates for visits the number 350 1350970.

Also known as Duomo, it was built from 1481 on a project by Gilberto Manzi, with sixteenth-century bell tower and facade rebuilt in 1881 by Gaetano Guglielmetti; the interior is late-Gothic Lombard with Renaissance elements. In the left aisle the mausoleum of Pallavicino, with the ark of Gianlodovico and his wife Anastasia Torelli dated 1499, here transferred from 1812 after the Napoleonic suppression of the Franciscan monastery; it also houses the polyptych of 1499 by Filippo Mazzola, father of Parmigianino, and in the crypt a Christ that comes out of the tomb of 1522 attributed to Antonietto de' Renzi.

Mining equipment from the oldest to the most recent, documents, photographs and maps, drilling machinery, ventilation and transport and panels on the geology of the area. It tells of the first workings in the Mandola valley from 1600 and the industrial exploitation of Montecatini, especially from the second post-war period to 1964, to extract pyrites destined for sulphuric acid. Open all year from Monday to Friday 8.30-12.30.
The Black Madonna, a destination for pilgrims.

Less than a kilometer from the village, the Coxinas river, which is born from the peaks of Santu Miali in the area of Monti Mannu, makes three consecutive jumps for 60 meters total, the last of about 30 meters on granite rocks, under the spire called Campanas de Sisinni Conti, forming three natural pools between oleanders and holm oaks. Gabriele D'Annunzio, in Sardinia in 1882, composed with Ugo Ranieri the verses then became the sonnet  . "La Spendula" , published in Captain Fracassa. From the parking five minutes walk on paved path; picnic area and games; in summer the waterfall is illuminated in the evening.

Educational-recreational structure of the Stelvio Park where you can see deer, deer, ibexes and chamois, with information point and visitor center with panels on characteristics, habits and winter adaptation of the species, also designed for children. You can visit freely following the established route or with guided tour by reservation.

The ruins of the castle dominate the village: probably built by the Arabs and enlarged by the Normans, it rises on a more ancient fortification of uncertain origin, linked to the legendary founders of the country.

Traits of the belt of the Greek city, brought to light by Paolo Orsi between 1916 and 1921 in the locality Trappeto Vecchio: large square blocks of sandstone and limestone with semicircular towers, one of which preserved in the raised and the others in the foundations.
The walls of the Antium volsca.

In the civic palazzo "S'omu comuni" of the late nineteenth century, already school and pretura: a hall for temporary exhibitions, a hundred works of contemporary painters, many born from the annual competition of painting and sculpture, and in the council hall three seventeenth-century paintings of the Caravaggio school; an external path touches the modern sculptures in the streets of the village. Tuesday-Sunday, seasonal hours.
The botanical garden of the city, little attended.

Ceramic city from the Middle Ages, when it was called Castel delle Ripe, worked the clay of the Metauro; under the Montefeltro the shops multiplied and here was born in 1524 the ceramist Cipriano Piccolpasso. Today the majolica workshops organize courses throughout the year.
The birds of Sicily, even those disappeared.
A Roman water cathedral still in operation.
Museum of contemporary art of the village.
Chronological path on the history of past communication technologies.
The history of a Bohemian glass factory at the foot of the Genoa Valley.
Minerals and fossils from all over the world.
The hilly village, about 400 meters away, is called "Balcony of Vallesina" for its panoramic position on the Verdicchio vineyards.
The view of the Monferrato.
Agrarian and botanical science in a palace.
The view of the mountains.
Church of 1470 in the historic center, with the oldest bell tower of the church itself.
The Romanesque crypt and the seventeenth-century scagliole.
The life and work of past generations of Castanese.
Master Don Gesualdo's wedding banquet building.

Stone houses and squares along the Marsicana: Palazzo Fontana (about 1700, lowered after the earthquake of 1915), with the stone fountain of 1925, Palazzo D'Orazio, eighteenth century and municipal seat, Leonardo Dorotea square with the former town hall and the birthplace of the pastor poet Benedetto Virgilio (1600).
14th century tables and a monumental tomb.
The Colosseum in the trees.
Ancient symbol of civic power, with large frescoed rooms and the Palatine Chapel painted by Filippo Cavarozzi and Marzio Ganassini.
Abbey around which Finalpia developed in the Middle Ages, still active.

Opened in 2003 at the Bishops' Seminary of the 16th century, on three floors: the five-section route goes from the archaeologist's craft to life in an imperial Roman villa. Among the main pieces the mosaic with the Seasons and Aion by Masseria Ciccotti of Oppido Lucano; cumulative with the National Museum of Power €8.

The historical and cultural centre of Oltrepò Pavese, between plains and hills, the ancient Clastidium of the battle of 222 BC; in the upper part, around the hill of the Pistornile, the parish church of San Pietro Martire and the eighteenth-century Palazzo Certosa Cantù with the Civic Archaeological Museum, and in front of the town hall the Alata Victoria by Pier Enrico Astorri.

On a terrace of the hill, about 3 km north-west of the village, a Sicilian necropolis of the V-IV century BC and a Christian hypogeum of the 5th century A.D., two bedrooms dug into the rock, with loculi and an arcosolian sarcophagus. Free access.
Over 800 hectares of salty pools with herons, Italian knights and pink flamingos; Salina Camillone still produces by hand sweet salt, Presidio Slow Food.

Wanted by Gian Galeazzo Visconti, who laid the foundation stone on 27 August 1396, as a dynastic mausoleum to dissolve a vow of his wife Catherine; she was entrusted over time to Carthusians, Cistercians and Benedictines. The marble façade of Carrara, serpentine and porphyry has at the base medallions with heads of ancient characters and, higher up, stories of Christ and the Old Testament. The three-nave church, inspired by the Gothic Cathedral of Milan, has starry sky vaults, fourteen chapels with works by Perugino and Guercino, the funeral monument of Gian Galeazzo and that of Ludovico il Moro and Beatrice d'Este del Solari; next to the small cloister and the large cloister (1472). The €10 ticket replaced the free offer to the monastic community; from Tuesday to Sunday, winter (25/10/2026-25/3/2027) 10-16, summer 10-18, last entry 30 minutes before; online tickets to Museitaliani or on site.

Historic route set up in the ancient dormitory of monks, with illustrated panels and teaching materials: the agricultural economy of the monastery, the converts, the grandeurs and the service buildings, the daily life of the monks and the Cistercian architecture. Open every day 8.30-12 and 14.30-18.30, without reservation for individuals; guided tours of groups and schools by reservation.

The main center of the National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise, at 1167 meters at the foot of the Monte delle Vitelle, where the park was established on September 9, 1922; birthplace of Benedetto Croce, with the historic center in stone, the church of Saints Peter and Paul, Palazzo Sipari, the ruins of Castel Mancino and the Visitor Center of the Park.
The Crucifixion of 1452.
Archaeology in a historic building.
In the heart of the old town, the waterfall that creates water games at the foot of the Rocca dei Borgia.

Artificial lake in the Lumiei valley, whose waters change tonality with the seasons; you can reach from the road 52 in Ampezzo going up the gorge of the Lumiei Valley, crossed by a bridge 150 meters above the stream, or from the pure pass. Canoes, sup and skates are rented in summer.
The triptych of the Romanino school.

Seaside resort of the Dianese Gulf, between Capo Berta and Capo Cervo, with more than 3,500 meters of sandy beach from the bottoms; in the Palazzo del Parco the Museo Civico MARM tells the wreck of a Roman ship to sunk in the first century A.D. in front of the coast.
A medieval tower that today looks at the stars.
The high-medieval roots of the country among the olive trees.

Of the original complex, the Dolfin and purchased in 1734 for Leonardo Valmarana, the two boats and the small church, where the first Valmarana owners are buried: the villa was demolished in 1908 by the owner Antonio Baldan. In 1960 the sculptor Luciano Minguzzi bought the guesthouse and restored the frescoes; today the guest house hosts events and ceremonies. Private property open to the public.

Municipality of the high Friulian plain between the Meduna and Cosa streams,  the land of mosaicists and the home of the boxer Primo Carnera, whose liberty villa is today the symbol of the village; a route through the mosaics of the center.
The art of Lake Maggiore.

It was first mentioned in 1238 and built by the lords of Montalban on a cliff on the left bank of the Adige, from 1531 it was a fief in pledge of the Hendl, which gave it its present appearance; the fires of 1813 and 1824 devastated it and in 1956 the State bought the complex, restored under the Superintendence until 1995 and managed since 1999 by a cooperative. The chapel, at the end of the thirteenth century or early fourteenth century, has a frieze with the twelve Apostles in pairs and the texts of the Creed, with alternating normal and mirrorful inscriptions. Today it is the cultural center of the country, with exhibitions in spring and autumn; it can be visited only with a guide, from April to October.
The paws of the world in the country that still builds them.
Two Gothic portals on the course.
The carved portal of 1472.

Borgo del Varesotto inhabited by Golasecchiani, Insubri, Romani and Longobards: it preserves the Romanesque complex of the basilica of San Vittore and the octagonal baptistery of San Giovanni, an archaeological museum with a Lombard necropolis visible in the garden and, in the woods, the Pollini Swamp of the Ticino Park.
The town loggia.
The stone village.
Famous yield from Antonioni's red desert (1964), it must be the color of fragments of a pink micro-organism living in posidonia. Budelli, an oasis of about 25 hectares, passed to the park in 2016.
Sora's story from Volsci to paper mills.
The fresco of the Madonna del Giglio.

Lodigiano's closed courtyard farmhouse, already present in the cadastral map of 1723, with the crenellated dovecote tower and the entrance porch documented in 1897 and the stable of the beefs dated 1888; belonged among others to the Talentes and Madonini. Restored since 1981 with original construction techniques, since 1993 it is a farm-teaching farm on about 60 hectares: the former barn with barn houses the museum of agricultural and domestic tools, and you can visit the ancient peasant houses, the former stables, the wood oven, the granaries, the threshing floor and the old water mill on the roggia, certified as rice pile already in 1723.
The palace of 1270 on Piazza Silvestri, today seat of the theatre Francesco Torti.
Museum of industrial archaeology dedicated to the woolly tradition of Arpino.
The city cathedral, dating back to the seventeenth century.

Complex founded around the VI-VII century, to whose construction according to historical sources contributed the Benedictine monks of San Vincenzo al Volturno; the current church is of the XI-XII centuries and the bell tower, 25 meters high, was completed in 1329. The Benedictines remained until 1474; then, abandoned, the church was almost submerged by the debris of the torrent Musa Bridge (1845-1850) and was reopened and restored by Don Duilio Iemme since 1929. At the center is the wooden statue of the Madonna called "del Sorriso" (Smile), the main feast is September 8 and pilgrimages are frequent from May to October.

At 418 meters between holm oaks and cypresses, reachable by path 509 from Via Roma: church of the end of the thirteenth century with a Pietà of the fourteenth century, the oldest sanctuary of Liguria according to italia.it.
The puppets of the Catania tradition.
The sunset on the sea.
The bridge under the cathedral.
Diocesan museum housed in the Archbishop's Palace, next to the Cathedral.
A village of the Bronze Age of about 3,300 years ago and the museum that tells it.
Marine fossils and trails to the top.
The Baroque masterpiece of Trentino.

A long beach of black sand and pebbles in the locality of San Giuseppe, near Marina di Maratea, several times Blue Flag, with an equipped establishment; you go down a path in the vegetation and a staircase. Next to it you can find the Sciabella Cave, with an internal beach, and the Turtle Cave, which can be explored by canoe (rental on the beach).
A overpass connects the palace to a 40-hectare park with the Italian gardens, the Garden of the Paintings and the hunting lodge called    ... La Rocca .
The heart of the city, a Renaissance square already known as Piazza Grande, which hosts music festivals and open-air markets in summer.
The house of the great Modena historian.

Since 1982 on the first floor of the fifteenth-century Palazzo del Pretorio, with ogival portal and stone portico of Angera. The Roman vicus with coins and commerce, the Roman necropolis supplies, the organic remains of the Angera Panini and a 5th century Greek funeral stele of a Syrian merchant; stoneware under the porch and children's section (MABA). Closed from 20 December to 31 January.
Walk inaugurated in 1963 with a mosaic of 800 meters in ceramic stoneware made by twenty artists including Lucio Fontana, Aligi Sassu, Giuseppe Capogrossi and Emanuele Luzzati.
International temporary exhibitions and permanent collections of the major Sardinian artists of the twentieth century, including Nivola, Ciusa and Maria Lai.

A long golden sandy beach with a shallow bottom that gently slopes, suitable for children, among the first seaside resorts in Italy, frequented by royal and wealthy holidaymakers from the end of the nineteenth century; historic establishments with colored wooden cabins and an evening walk suitable for bikes, walks and skates.
The city of wine.
The medieval tower-door in the heart of Agrate.
The rocky coast of the Cape of Leuca between towers and caves.

Ancient spring on the southern side of the hill, of Roman origin: in the nineteenth century there were found remains of Roman buildings with mosaic floors and the site would host a production of bricks with the brand           . Waters, thermal and rich in carbon dioxide, flow at 28 °C and for centuries have served people, fields and livestock.
The village without car of the Valtournenche, reachable only on foot or by cable car, between wooden houses and stone.
The rooms and the park of the noble residence.
Medieval church; in the cemetery chapel there is a Christ of Pietà attributed to the Flemish painter Hans Clemer.
The living room of the village, between noble palaces and fountain.
The angioin tower back to the city.
In the Lombroso pavilion of the former San Lazaro psychiatric hospital, the history of mental illness treatment with tools and documents.
Walk in the green to the waterfall.
The house of Neapolitan music.

Villa-style noble residence on the right bank of the Strona, with original nucleus probably before 1722 (birth of Benedetto Felice Ranzoni, court doctor); facades and decorations unified in the early twentieth century. Scalone d'honore on the noble floor. Owned by the municipality since 1988, it hosts offices, cultural services and the municipal library; free access.
The sundials of the sixteenth century.
To understand the tragedy of 1944 that marked the country.
The church of the saved harvest.
The fifteenth-century church of the village of Rivalta with wooden trusses ceiling and terracotta decorations; it houses paintings by the seventeenth-century painter Ferrante of Bologna.
The Medici library opened to the public in 1571, with the vestibule and reading room designed by Michelangelo.

Country of the Val Brembana from the origins around 1100, with the fifteenth-century parish church of San Lorenzo built on the ruins of a castle, a network of museums (of the Valley, of San Lorenzo, of the Soldier, House museum Belotti), the Grottoes of the Wonders, among the first tourist caves of Italy, and the departure of the cycle path of the Val Brembana.

It occupies most of the ancient seventeenth-century convent of the Carmelites; set up since 1986 and inaugurated on 17 January 1988, it exhibits in 20 sections objects of rural life, crafts and domestic life, such as ploughs, hoes and looms. During the works there are frescoes of the cloister (1610-1627) attributed to the school of Giuseppe Sebastiani by Macerata and paintings of the mid eighteenth century of the Viterbo Domenico Corvi. Times and access on contact (tel. 0761 327677).
Church of the XIII century that preserves the triptych of the Madonna and Child and the saints Sebastiano and Rocco of Matteo da Gualdo.

18th century parish church with a single nave with three chapels per side and vaulted barrel; the square bell tower has terracotta decorations. It preserves a group of sixteenth-century statues of the Deposition, the relics of San Novello martyr donated by a Milanese family in the sixteenth century, a fresco of the Madonna with Child, a wooden crucifix of the fifteenth century and two seventeenth-century paintings of Carlo Cane.

Valico delle Prealpi Brescia between Val Trompia and Val Sabbia, about 50 km from Brescia, reachable from Collio with a winding road well signposted. In winter, the Maniva Ski area offers 40 km of slopes between 1,450 and 2,100 meters (1 black, 6 red, 8 blue) and 9 lifts, with snowshoeing also in the moonlight, ski touring, cross-country skiing, sleddog and ski schools also for disabled; in summer the Bike Park Pezzeda offers 8 slopes for 26 km in the Iron Valley network. The roads from Val Sabbia and Crocedomini are usually closed in winter.
The Resistance painted by a teacher.
One of the stages of the historic center reported by the tourist consortium of Monviso.
The Tiepolo of the stairs.
An underground route in the old stone quarries.

Campanile designed by Luigi Cagnola, the architect of the Arch of Peace in Milan, built between 1824 and 1829 in a gentle strain of Brembate: 54 meters high, circular plan with three cylinders degrading in the Doric, Ionic and Corinthian orders and a balcony of caryatids under the dome; inside, a spiral staircase of 235 steps. The tourist portal indicates it as the highest stone tower in Italy; today it has 12 bells.

Ethnographic Museum in the hamlet Colletto: objects and tools of everyday life in a set-up of other times, each documented and described in Occitan and Italian. Open every day from July to September, with guided tours on Saturday and Sunday from 16:30 to 18:30.

Teramano municipality of the Sicilian Valley at the foot of the Gran Sasso; in the Park equipped with the River Fiumetto, established in 1990, rises the medieval village of Castiglione della Valle, the ancient Castrum Leonis Vallis Sicilianae that according to tradition hosted Lucrezia Borgia, with the church of San Michele Arcangelo of the twelfth century.
Two scientific university museums in Via Archirafi: the Museum of Zoology Pietro Doderlein (b. 16-18) and the Museum of Mineralogy (b. ANNEX

Founded in the 11th century by the abbot Giovanni V of Santa Scolastica, since 1456 it was the residence of the Commendator Abbots, including Rodrigo Borgia, then Pope Alexander VI; it was restored in the mid-eighteenth century by Giovannangelo Braschi, then Pope Pius VI. It dominates the medieval village.
The Roman city under the walls.
The fortified residence of the lords of Alexander.
The avant-gardes of the 1950s and 1960s in a house of the sixteenth century.

Small agricultural village of Canavese, about 20 km from Ivrea, known for the MACAM, museum of contemporary art in the open air born in 1985 with more than one hundred works, especially frescoes, painted on the walls of the houses; on the hill remains the tower of the ancient castle of Valperga, today bell tower of the cemetery, and in the village the Baroque parish church of San Maurizio.
The Venetian landscape, from lagoons to the Alps, seen by the painters of the twentieth century.

Visitor center of the Stelvio National Park in the ancient Lahnersäge sawmill, where until the eighties the peasants of the valley brought the wood to be cut: it explains the importance and the functions of the wood and offers virtual excursions in the park environments. Hours 9.30-12.30 and 14.30-17.30 in the summer and winter seasons; closed from November to New Year and in April.

In the highest point of the old town, among the oaks of the Empire woods, with views of the valley of Baronia di Vico. The first document on the fortress dates back to 1078, when it was sold to Roberto il Guiscardo; it was a stronghold of Baronia and then a residence of barons and marquises, until the remains of stones and bricks caused its abandonment. There are still the cylindrical tower on the east side, the belt with six large windows and parts of the living environments; it is freely seen from the outside.

Started in 1598 and inaugurated in 1612, with a Latin plan with three naves on stone pillars; 1818 central altar, tombs with barrel vault and Sacramento Chapel with stucco dome and frescoes in the lunettes.

Born in 2002 with the event "There was once Christmas" and since 2014 set up in the Oratory S. Paolo, is entirely self-built, set in the Waldensian valleys with a section dedicated to the Germanasca Valley, and is registered with the Italian Association of Friends of the Nativity scene. According to the Town Hall page ( 2019 poster) it is open from 8 December to 6 January on Saturday and Sunday from 15 to 18, with visits for schools and groups by reservation.
16th century frescoes on the rock.

Wanted in the second half of the seventeenth century by Petracone V Caracciolo on the site of the castle of the Orsini, it has a baroque façade with pilasters on two levels divided by a balcony with wrought iron railing; inside the Chapel of the Dukes and the halls of the Arcadia, the Myth and the Bible, partly decorated by Domenico Carella in 1771-76. It houses the Town Hall and, in the atrium, works and concerts of the Festival of the Itria Valley.

Trail 313 from the locality Piazzetto (via Guarda): passes through the fifteenth-century building of Anveno, Cascina Anveno (775 m) and Passata (960 m) to Punta Almana (1391 m), with iron cross and wide view on clear days. About 2.30 hours.
In the medieval Palazzo Spini Feroni, the museum opened in 1995 by the Ferragamo family on the history of the "star shoemaker" and of the made in Italy.

The ancient Abella to the slopes of the Avella Mountains, in the upper valley of the Clanio: the Roman amphitheatre leaning against the walls, the funerary monuments of the late-Republic and imperial ages and, on the hill, the castle of San Michele with the Lombard and Norman surroundings.

Former fishing village on the western shore of the largest and deepest river of the Sardinian north-east, less than ten kilometers from Arzachena: the port is a promenade and from here leave the trips to the National Park of the Archipelago of La Maddalena. Next to the port, the beach is of the city of the sea, with a low backdrop suitable for snorkelling; to the north, the promontory of Punta Occhione looks at the Rock of the Bear.
The silk of the sea.
Church with circular plan, built entirely of bricks with dome in pozzolana, built in the area known as ...Largo della Croce.
Ancient house with ethnographic museum on rural culture and exhibition space.
The sacred art of working land.
Pyramid domes on the sea.
Contemporary art in the center.
The literary living room where D'Annunzio and Pirandello passed.
The castle that dominates the village.
The Dominican church and convent arose around 1360 at the behest of the widow of the Marquis Giorgio I Del Carretto; the convent was imprisoned from 1863 to 1964.
The fishermen's peninsula.
The UNESCO heart of the city.

In the former primary school, designed for about 25 years by naturalist Ivan Fossa. On three floors: zoology of the vertebrates of Belluno; insects, molluscs, geology, mineralogy, paleontology (with a rare jaw of dental) and Roman finds from the site of Staol of Curago; botany with dioramas, mushrooms, xiloteca and fishes, including the Sampierolo, endemic to Lake Santa Croce. Guided tours by reservation for groups of at least 6 people.
A cave between prehistory and micaelic cult.
The art of the village in a former church.
In the castle the library with miniature incunabula and books of the sixteenth century.
Digged gorge in the mountains by the Marmore stream, 3 km from Valtournenche on the road to Breuil-Cervinia; entrance fee.
The memory of the tobacconists of the Liri valley.
In the Parco dei Monti Lucretili, a fortified settlement inhabited between 1200 and 1400, of which the crenellated walls and a cistern remain.
Municipal museum with collections of mineralogy and natural sciences, which offers an overview of the fauna and minerals of the area. Visiting hours should be requested from the museum.
center severely damaged by the earthquake 2016, parts in red zone without access to the public and reconstruction started in 2025 (Sibillini Park, Marche Region)
The sixteenth-century church on the Levrange plateau.

The center gathers around Piazza Pasotti and the Civic Tower, the highest point of the village and still today leads to the village; among the buildings there are Palazzo Venturini and several manor villas.
Exhibitions in the castle.
The highest magnetite mine in Europe, with more than 100 km of galleries in Monte Creya, can be visited with guide; exhibition center of the mining park.

Already Piazza da' Piedi, it is the center of the village from the eighteenth century and you enter it from Porta dei Marsi; the porticos were closed in 1810 by order of Gioacchino Murat and around 1825 the fountain with the obelisk replaced an ancient stone seat.

Already existing in the seventeenth century and seat of the Confraternita dei Disciplinati, it was renewed in 1782 at the expense of Marquis Luigi Malaspina. The exposed brick façade has a neoclassical pediment and a sundial from 1848 of Stura di Moncalvo, restored, with the motto The interior with a single nave, with pilasters in fake marble and ionic capitals in stucco, is frescoed by the saintly painter Paolo Maggi, author of the altarpieces of the Adoration of the Magi and the Virgin with Saints Rocco and Sebastiano; there is also a Lingiardi organ.
Medici fortress on mighty walls, then prison and residence of the Vicar, today with an interactive educational museum.
MiC card (updated to 2021) only indicates Monday opening in the morning

Outdoor art path started in 2012 by the Municipality in the pine forest of Pur, along the stream Assat towards Malga Cita: sculptures and installations in stone, iron and wood (trees, stone cows, giant violins, a swing forest), enriched every summer by site-specific works of invited artists.
Monferrato and Cardinal Massaja in a multimedia key.
Unpublished timetables (the MiC card reports every day as closed): tel. 0824 993649
One of the symbols of the city, in modern Romanesque style, with the façade marked by the reinforced concrete pillars designed by Riccardo Morandi.

City on the lagoon between the tomboli of Giannella and Feniglia, already capital of the Spanish State of the Presidians: bastions and Spanish gates, the Mill that emerges from the water, the oasis of flamingos and, in Ansedonia, the Roman colony of Cosa.
The rocks and the walls of the stronghold of Ruggero.
The stone of martyrdom.

Built in the seventeenth century by the Bartolini family on a rural building, it is reached by a long avenue of cypresses: the central body on three floors is flanked by two square towers connected by a porch and loggia. The lounge has allegorical and landscape frescoes from the mid-eighteenth century by Francesco Chiarottini and Giambattista Canal, restored since 1987; today it is home and restaurant.

With 1526 meters it is one of the highest peaks of the Umbrian-Marche Apennines: valleys, forre, natural arches and canyons in limestone, some caves that can be visited (in one were found cave bear bones, today in the civic museum). The summit is occupied by antennas and fenced; on the north-east side, between 1290 and 1430 meters, the ski resort with the Mandrion ski lift and 5 slopes.

Fishermen's village with marina and small beach, reached by stairs; above the village the sanctuary of Santa Maria della Lobra, dating back to 1528, built on a temple perhaps dedicated to Minerva, which gave the name to the city (Lobra da In front is the Scoglio del Vervece, where every year the fallen of the sea are remembered; the cliffs are a good point for the sunset. The walk from Piazza Vescovado is the shortest and most accessible of the Marine Protected Area.

Borgo della Piana Rotaliana, the vineyard that Goethe called the most beautiful in Europe and the land of Teroldego, with the ancient district of Piaz, the Castle of the Tower, the church of San Pietro sul Colle and the bridge suspended towards the Toresela; from the early nineteenth century it distills Villa de Varda, with its family museum.
Fine sand and shallow water for the whole family.
A walk between doors and palaces on the tuff.

Panoramic path well signposted of about 3 km, less than an hour, that starts from the SP53 and crosses the Reserve of Monte Barone between almond trees, Aleppo pines and olive trees with views of the bay; at the junction, on the right, you go down to the beach of Vignanotica, long beach at the outlet of the valley, with summer services. Free access according to the Park.

Heart of rock art in the Camonica Valley, the first Italian UNESCO site (1979): the Naquane Park, the Cemmo Masses and the maps of Bedolina, the National Museum of Prehistory and two Romanesque masterpieces, the Pieve di San Siro and the monastery of San Salvatore.
In Chapel, about 5 km from the center: probably a Benedictine cenobium, with abbey title under the Chapter of Santa Sofia of Benevento.
One of the oldest parishes of Ravennate, with a single nave with polygonal apse rebuilt in the early sixteenth century.
Small church under the Fortress, built in the sixteenth century instead of a votive aedicule: octagonal plan covered by an eight-sliced dome, with the sacristy leaning on one of the facades.
Trekking between forre, caves and hermitages.
Excavations from the ancient hospital under a 15th century loggia.
Small church with dome shaped like trullo, overlooking the sea and the valley of Stilaro.
Church built between the end of the sixteenth century and the beginning of the seventeenth century, just outside the ancient nucleus, with baroque altars.
To build the Cathedral Sixto V he made a hill flat; on the square the bronze monument of Pericles Fazzini, a rotating sculpture that projects the profile of the pope on always different views.

In the village of Villa da Piedi, you can reach via Sotto Castello, dominated by the walls of the Fortress of the XV century; the church dates back to the mid-nineteenth century and rises on a more ancient structure, built between the sixteenth and seventeenth century.

The village preserves traces of the walls with towers of the 13th-XIV century, which had six doors: in the district Castellara remains the only ancient door, with sharp arch. The marquisal palace, probably from 1543-1584, closes the third floor of Mezzo and is the backdrop to the square; in Piazza Platea Magna the town hall of late XII-early XIII century houses on the first floor the church of San Michele Arcangelo, with the Ridotto placed on the back. In the eighteenth century, the bourgeois families, including the de Lellis, built palaces by Lombard masters, with cellars turned into exposed bricks once oil mills and warehouses. From the viewpoints you can see the sea, the Majella, the Gran Sasso and the Pescara valley.

Opened in 2016 in the former city Brefotropio, it exhibits in a permanent way more than one hundred works of art confiscated from organized crime: the first museum reality entirely dedicated to a cultural heritage confiscated.
Industrial archaeology became a library.

Designed by the architect Giovanni Greppi and sculptor Giannino Castiglioni and inaugurated on 19 September 1938 on the slopes of Mount Six Busi, it collects the remains of 100,187 soldiers who fell in the area: about 40,000 known in the 22 steps in karst stone with names on bronze plates, about 60,000 unknown on the top near the three crosses and the chapel, which became church in 2014. The complex includes the tombs of the Duke of Aosta and five generals and the Heroic Way with 38 bronze tombstones of the battles of the Karst and the Isonzo; on the nearby Colle di Sant'Elia stood the first Cimitero degli Invitati with over thirty thousand corpses. Restored in 2021, always open.
A long beach equipped for families.

Borgo della Tuscia overlooking the Valle dei Calanchi and Civita di Bagnoregio, 110 km from Rome: around Piazza San Giovanni the church of San Giovanni Battista, born from a Benedictine cell of the IX century, the Palazzo Monaldeschi and the fountain of Pucciotta; the Naturalistic Museum accompanies the Monaldeschi Tower and the Balza Natural Monument of Seppie.
The city's big lead mine.
The historic centre preserves the ancient village with lively streets and squares; in the main square the ceremony of the Busecca opens the Carnival. The Magni Park overlooks the left bank of Sesia.

In the ravine of Coriglione there is the rock village of Santa Maria di Constantinople, in that of Santo Stefano the homonymous village in cave; in the countryside around the village the rock settlements, some older than the more than one hundred farms, many fortified.
The remains of the theatre of the II century AD in the center of the city, which could accommodate about 3,000 spectators.

Pieve da origini tra VII e VIII secolo, tra i titoli più antichi della diocese di Città di Castello, con portale romanico del 1279; transformed at the beginning of the twentieth century, has a single nave with oval vaults, a fresco of the Martyrdom of San Sebastiano attributed to Raffaellino del Colle and a copy of the polyptych of Ottaviano Nelli, whose original is at the National Gallery of Umbria.
The forms of the karst of the gravines.
The frescoes of the Master of Lerma in an isolated parish.
19th century funeral architecture by Vantini.
The complement of the visit to the basilica.

The Palazzo delle Esposizioni hosts exhibitions and events, including an accordion and an organ that entered the Guinness of Records; every September the International Accordion Award attracts musicians from all over the world and in June the European Music Festival is held.

A small museum between the church and the municipality (former convent of the Augustinians next to the parish church of Sant'Agostino, renovated in the eighteenth century): it exhibits paintings, sacred objects and vestments of the church's treasure.
A path through wash basins, fountains and mills, with a stream flowing under an ancient bridge.
The Romanesque in the country.

On the first floor of the eighteenth-century Palazzo Corielli, the art master Guerrino Lovato rebuilt his famous Venetian workshop of masks made of mache, transferred to Malo and entrusted to the Municipality to tie it to the local tradition of Carnival; inaugurated on September 25, 2011, it preserves about 250 mache works, about 500 dies, a library-archive, tools and antique furniture. Guided tours by booking for groups up to 25 people; closed in August, Easter and Christmas.
Lawn and pier on the lake, away from the crowd.

In Valdadige, on the banks of the Adige, Dolcè preserves Volargne Villa del Bene, with the portal attributed to Sanmicheli and the 16th century frescoes of Brusasorzi, and the secular cypresses of the public park; in Ceraino the remains of the Chiusa, an Austrian fortress on the river gorge.

It was the cathedral of the diocese of Trevico from 1058 to 1818, when the original Greek cross plant had already been transformed into a long central nave; several times rebuilt after the earthquakes, it collapsed in the roof with the 1980 earthquake and was reopened to worship on August 8, 1998. Facade in stone and eighteenth-century bell tower with civic clock; inside the main altar in precious marbles with the canvas of the Assumption, the wooden choir of the eighteenth century, the bishop's throne and, in the chapel of the Rosary, the baptismal font in stone of 1618; the parish archive preserves miniature books and medieval parchments. Open during function hours.

Well temple of the late Bronze Age in blocks of basalt and limestone: atrium with seats, 12 steps staircase and circular chamber in tholos; next to a second well, a large fence and huts, and in the church of St. Anastasia, rebuilt in the fifteenth century, another nuragic well.
A Greek theatre in a solemn landscape.
In the Bastione Lalio of the castle, more than 130 artifacts among inscriptions, sculptures and mosaics of the Roman villa of Barcola.

The parish preserves the image of Our Lady of Graces with the bare breasts, which some scholars link to the cult of Artemis. In the village there is also the church of St. John the Baptist, Santa Maria del Monte of the 18th century, the chapel with the newsstand of the 12th century Madonna della Stella and the sanctuary of the Saints Cosma and Damiano.
The top symbol of the Val di Viù.
The village of the Trivulzio on foot.

A large hall dedicated to Alfredo Binda, winner of three World Championships and five Italian Tours: jerseys and Italian champions, saddles, shoes, goggles and above all the two bikes of the World Championships of 1930 and 1932. The collection is completed by the phone that Binda played in the band of Cittiglio, editions of the Gazzetta dello Sport, diplomas, photographs and materials on his career as technical commissioner of the National.
The ancient nucleus preserves traces of the long history of the village: stone doors, towers, arches and irregular alleys.
A medieval church with two souls, Romanesque and Gothic.

Born in 1910 at the will of the notary Camillo Leone, between the sixteenth century Casa Alciati frescoed, the eighteenth century Palazzo Langosco and the rationalist sleeve of the 1930s: finds and arts applied from prehistory to the nineteenth century.
The history of the internees of San Donato.
A village built by the mine.
Medieval frescoes in a place out of time.
The castle with views of the Brenta Dolomites.
Burri's complete route.

There are traces of the ancient walls, the Bolli and Boccali towers and the restored Porta Vecchia, between medieval alleys and squares; in the center the Town Hall of 1871 and several Art Deco buildings.
A short stop in the countryside between Ferrara and Portomaggiore.
Three cloisters and masterpieces of the Brescia Renaissance in a still alive monastery.

On the first hills of Modena, the capital of ceramics: the Castle of Spezzano dei Pio di Savoia with the Sala delle Vedute and the Museo della Ceramica, the Baroque sanctuary of the Blessed Virgin of the Castle and the mud volcanoes of the reserve of the Salse di Nirano.
An underground sanctuary used for five thousand years.
Olivetti's cars.
Built in 1663 by vote, after the country had been spared by the plague.
The symbol of the Waldensian memory.

In an Austrian military building of the early nineteenth century, already barracks of French cavalry and then military hospital, restored in 1999: exhibits the finds of the Verona plain collected in the last thirty years, about 5,000 years of history from the ancient Neolithic (V millennium BC) to the late Iron Age (II-I century BC). Workshops for families and schools; since 2010 it is part of the Legnago Museums network managed by Fondazione Fioroni.

Ancient Messapian centre, an important military, political and religious centre between the 4th and 3rd centuries BC, today the city of art and gastronomy is known for its cookie. The ducal castle dominates the medieval old town with the Allegretti palaces (seat of the Pinacoteca Emilio Notte), Epifani and Vitale; around terraces with trulli, mirrors, caves and rock churches.

Museum in a 16th-century defensive tower in one of the most panoramic squares in the historic centre, founded in 1987 and re-arranged in 2004: the exhibits, in chronological order and in windows obtained in the ancient fire vents, range from the stone instruments of the Middle Paleolithic of Torre Talao to the community of the hill of Petrosa (VII-VI century BC) to Ponticello in the Roman age; there are also exhibits of the archaeological Park of Laos. Open Monday-Friday 8.30-15, closed Saturday and Sunday.
The Roman Romagna in a hillside village.

It was elevated to archpretura in 1690, it was demolished and rebuilt larger in 1862-1865 on a project by the Roman Luigi Crescia, consecrated in 1873 and reopened in 1887 after the earthquake that destroyed the pictorial cycle of Lazaro De Maestri. It has three naves with twenty columns with Corinthian capitals; frescoes by Raffaele Resio in the central nave and apse, decorated by Antonio and Francesco Bertolotto, a Deposition by Giovanni Battista Casoni, the main altar by Giuseppe Gaggini (in 1694) and the marble pulpit by Gio Maria Augustallo. The 17th-century churchyard is made of white and black pebbles.

The door of the East at the end of the Appian Way: the Roman Columns on the Scalinata Virgiliana, Piazza Duomo with the cathedral and the Ribezzo Museum, the Roman remains of San Pietro degli Schiavoni, the Swabian Castle, the Forte a Mare and the Monument to the Marinaio d'Italia on the port.
A few hundred meters from the old town, on a plateau sheltered from the winds; of ancient origin, it was rebuilt after 1530 and dedicated to San Martino di Tours.

The beaches of Scalea, about 8 km long, are of dark pebbles; the cliff of the Ajnella is one of the free beaches most loved on the Riviera dei Cedri. Along the coast, the Pecora Cave opens between the Bay of Carpino and the Beach, the "Piscina" is a stretch with rocky edges similar to a large cistern and the Bay of Dragons owes its name to the rocks that recall mythological creatures.

In the historic centre, it houses paintings by Moroni, Salmeggia, Cavagna, Zucco, Cignaroli, Barbello and Paduanino and frescoes by the recently discovered Marinoni workshop. Di Moroni the Crucifix between the Saints Bernardino and Antonio da Padova (about 1553-1575), the Trinity (1555), destined to the church of Fiobbio, and a standard painted on both sides in the sacristy.

Founded in 2004 on the initiative of the parish priest Fr Francesco Ciabattoni, it is set up in the nave of the former Collegiate with frescoes from the 14th to the 16th century; it collects paintings, relics and works of the parish of San Nicolò di Bari, including a wooden crucifix of the 13th century, the 16th century statue of the Madonna of Loreto and a section on St. James of the Marca.

The factory was built in 1885 by Gerolamo Taddei for Alessandro Cruto, to produce on an international scale its carbon filament bulbs; the building remained almost intact, with the chimney of the high factory. Since 1996 it houses a museum in three sections: the life of Cruto and the impact of the factory on Alpignano, the history of lighting with instruments and lamps, the invention in its historical context.

The old village, perched on the upper part of the southern buttress of the Soratte, is closed by well-preserved walls interrupted by three gates: Porta Valle (or San Silvestro), Porta La Dentro (or Sant'Edisto) and Porta Costa (or Santa Maria).

On the slopes of Monte Aguzzo among the oak woods, initiated by the hermit Mainardo in 1082; the cloister, built between 1229 and 1232 and attributed to the Roman master Pietro de Maria, is a rare example of Romanesque architecture and sculpture.
China from all over the world.
Borgates, pylons and secular larches on foot.
A dome of 60 meters in the plain.

Borgo dell'Alto Ionio Cosentino on the slopes of the Pollino National Park, about 20 km from the sea, Orange Flag of Touring; it dominates the fifteenth-century castle of the Sanseverino and the Mother Church of San Giorgio of Norman origin, while Palazzo Giannettasio houses the Museum of peasant civilization.
At the north-western edge of the town of Acquarica del Capo, it preserves the remains of a Norman tower, an ancient crypt and the little church of St. Mary of Oils, very remodeled.
A panoramic stop on the hills of the Bormida Valley.
The fortress symbol of Corleone.
The Gonzaga Palace of Castel Goffredo, with the frescoed loggia.

One of the most famous monastic settlements of the ancient Duchy of Amalfi, leaning on a rocky wall between Capo d'Orso and the centre of Maiori; its value lies in the medieval pictorial cycles preserved inside. The tours are guided and by reservation at the tourist office of the Municipality; the Touring indicates opening Wednesday and Saturday 15:30-18:30 and Sunday 10-13, on request the other days, closed from November to March, free admission.

One of the last pastures of the Apuan Alps, in the Park, between Pania della Croce, Monte Corchia and Freddone under the Pizzo delle Saette; inhabited by shepherds until the 1940s and abandoned after the war, preserves ruins, terraces, mule tracks, charcoal and metati for chestnut flour. Two shelters, Robbio and Quiete, offer overnight stay.
Four centuries of garrisons.

Pontifical fortress wanted by Cardinal Egidio Albornoz and completed in 1378, with a project probably attributed to Gattapone; it hosts an exhibition on daily life in the Middle Ages and from 2023 the SAM Street Art museum.
The small Roman covered theatre in the heart of the city.
The fourteenth-century parish church in front of the palace.
Hot water in the white rocks.
Mon closed · mar-mer 14-19 · Thu 14-20 · ven-dom: see site
The medieval mosaics of the months.

About 8,200 hectares to the extreme south of the province, a few kilometers from the sea, among the green rocks of the Voltri Group where the Alps and the Apennines meet; oak woods, chestnuts, beech and black pines, artificial lakes of the Gorzente and rare flora such as the violet of Bertoloni. They live roe deer, wild boars and sometimes the wolf; symbol of the park is the biancon. The administrative seat is in Bosio.
A walk through the sixteenth-century corners of the country.
The Roman door intact.
The last of the eight mills.
For those who have seen San Domenico and want more.

The city of marble at the foot of the Apuan Islands: the Cathedral of St. Andrew with black and white marble bands, the Academy of Fine Arts in the Palace of Cybo-Malaspina, the museums of marble and Michelangelo and, above the city, the basins of Colonnata and Fantiscritti with quarries to visit.
Vallone of settlements and Stadel Walser, with the chapel of Santa Margherita linked to the legend of the process to the devil.
From the Tyrrhenian to Montecassino in a view.
A crystal cave inside a mine.
Set up in a 19th-century manor house, it tells of the agro-pastoral life and the tradition of Fonni.

Testimony of the Dominican presence, it combines Renaissance and Baroque elements: facade with stuccoes and a refined portal, interior with a single nave with frescoes on St. Dominic, the apostles and the Dominican saints, side altars with marble decorations and statues.
The reservoir on the lake.
A thousand-year-old abbey in front of the mountains of Gran Sasso.
Ridolfi and Callido organs.

Borgo della valle del Savovato, in Cosentino: the Mother Church of the patron saints Saints Peter and Paul, the Convent of Saint Anthony in the upper part of the village and the Museum of the peasant civilization of Savovato tell its religious and peasant history.

Complex of the XV-XIX centuries, already of the Pio di Savoia, along the road that runs from Rovereto along the left bank of the Secchia towards Concordia: remarkable the fortified system with four surviving towers and the Oratory of the Immaculate.
The green lung of the Florentines.
On the hill of the Fortress, work of A. Carlini inaugurated in 1898, recalls the clash of 8 and 9 May 1848 between Austrian troops and the Pontifical Dragons.

Along the side of the Temple-Cathedral, in front of the so-called Capitolium, two rooms of the gallery of Roman substruction, called "Favisse" (Favisse), exhibit the mosaics of a domus of the second century AD found in Via dei SS. Four; it is the third exhibition venue of the civic museum.
The emigrated painter who returned to his village.

Started by Carlo Gesualdo with the adjoining Dominican monastery and completed by Nicolò Ludovisi in the first half of the seventeenth century, at the same level of the castle: nine baroque altars in polychrome marble plus three others, wooden choir inlaid and the statue of Saint Vincenzo Ferreri, celebrated on the last Sunday of August with the Flight of the Angel. Visits by reservation.
The Ambrosian Museum of Sacred Art in the cloisters of Sant'Eustorgio, part of one of the oldest monumental complexes in the city.
It has a sixteenth-century bell tower with majolica cusp and a Madonna attributed to Domenico Gagini.
The central square.
Small church built in 1530 during an epidemic of plague, with the date on the architrave of the portal.
Drink the water at the source.
Piazza Tonda with its fountain, where every September 8 the districts compete in the Palio after the parade in costume.
Itineraries on foot in the Padule di Fucecchio, which Feel Florence indicates as the largest inland marsh in Italy, between the municipalities of Cerreto Guidi and Fucecchio.
Dominican frescoes in a single nave.

Inaugurated on December 18, 1935, a year after the laying of the first stone, Pontinia preserves intact the original nucleus: the Town Hall with the fascist vintage writings on the walls, the Post Office, the cinema-theatre, the parish church of Sant'Anna and the tower of the aqueduct.
The sixteenth-century church in the hamlet of Ripa Alta, from which starts the old mule track that descends to Gromo.
The villa of the writer Garibaldi.
Monumental holes and trees under Mount Labbro.
The village divided between Orsini and Colonna.
The widest view of Irpinia.
The sulphurous bath by the sea.
Industrial archaeology on the river.
The Baroque façade of the center.

Piazzette with noble palaces in trachyte and limestone, volcanic stone buildings and architraves carved by local stonemasons with motifs of Catalan school. In the village also the churches of Santa Maria degli Angeli, Santa Croce and San Giuseppe.

Romanesque church of the Monferrino group, with origins in the 11th-XII century: it served a castrum of the bishop of Pavia, had parish functions and cemetery, appears in the census of 1507, and remained isolated in the open countryside with the displacement of the country. Single rectangular nave with semicircular apse in brick and stone masonry, monolithic peducci, carved capitals and three monofores; under the floor an ossuary turned into a barrel. Restored since 1982, it hosts cultural events and exhibitions; for openings contact the Municipality.
The oldest Byzantine frescoes in Puglia.
The villa outside the walls.
A church with a seventeenth-century flavour.

Well-preserved medieval center to which you can access from the Gate of the Valley; the original walls are seen from the turn of Via Civita, the outer belt is crossed from the gates of the Valley, Iron and Olive and the inner one from the Gate of the Clock. Alleys and stairs in stone with portals, ogival arches and ancient shops.
The Roero Rocks, on foot or by bike.
In the Camaldolese abbey of the sixteenth century, about 850,000 volumes, manuscripts from the 10th century and the Aula Magna, one of the most beautiful rooms for the bibliophiles.

Born from the reconstruction of the castle of the Anguillara, of which remain basement and ground floor, was purchased by the Justinians in 1595: the Marquis Vincenzo added the noble floor connected to the Italian garden with fountains, avenues and water games; the Odescalchi gave it to the State in 2003. On the sides of the portal four marble heads of the II century A.D.; in the halls the Fall of Fetonte by Francesco Albani (1609), the Hall of Love and Psyche by Bernardo Castello (1605), the Hall of Eternal Happiness by Paolo Guidotti (1610), the Camerino di Diana di Domenichino (1609) and decorations by Antonio Tempesta; on the ground floor a private theater with wooden boxes, under renovation. Open Mar-dom 8.30-12.30, Monday closed; booking not required.
From the walls, Apennines and Adriatic together.
The coves can only be reached on foot.
High altitude flowers within walking distance.

Common on the slopes of Vesuvius, in the National Park, where the Archaeological Park of Pompeii manages the Roman farm of Villa Regina and the Antiquarium dedicated to life in the Vesuvian countryside before 79 AD; next, the Museum of the National Park of Vesuvius.
Masterpieces of ancient art.
The public green above the villa of Pompey.
Oratory of the fourteenth century that houses a wooden altar of the fifteenth century.
A small church born from a legend of the stream.
In the hamlet of Torrita, ceramic workshops, weaving to the frame, kitchen and other held by local women.

The reinforced walls between 1456 and 1460 by Giovanni II Caracciolo on the Norman circuit restored by Frederick II; the Venosina Gate is the only one of the four doors that survived the earthquake of 1851 and is still in use.
The Talos vase in an intact nineteenth-century museum.

Reserve of about 1,100 hectares established in 2005 between Roseto, Cologna Spiaggia and Montepagano, with hilly and coastal landscapes, embryonic and consolidated dunes and about 120 plant species, many rare in Abruzzo; on the protected beach nests the friar. The project "Viti in Riserva" recovers abandoned vineyards.
The main street of the historic center that leads to Palazzo Chiericati and the Olympic Theatre, among palaces, shops and cafes.

Centro del Frignano in the Modena Apennines: the castle of Montecuccolo with its fortified village and museum centre, the Romanesque parish church of Renno, the natural reserve of Sassoguiano and the Devil's Bridge, a natural rock arch on the border with Lama Mocogno and Polinago.
The pediment of the temple is the strong piece.

On the site of the achaea colony founded in the 7th century BC, one of the most prosperous of Magna Grecia, where Sibari, Thurii and Copy overlapped; the remains of the most recent cities are visible in the area called "Cavallo" .
The prehistory of the lower Garda in a small civic museum.
Villa-castle of Michelozzo for Cosimo il Vecchio, with crenellated tower, Italian garden and 17th century pergola, 500 meters above Mugello.
The country church of the plateau.
The village of the tower.

Late medieval village of houses leaning on the hill at the foot of the Pollino, called "Presepe del Pollino" after the visit of Escher in 1930; among the majolica domes of the Magdalena, the collegiate of St. Nicholas and Saints Peter and Paul with the marbles of Pietro Bernini, the Norman-Svevo castle and the ruins of the monastery of Colloreto.
A small treasure chest of sacred art.
In the former Late Dogotic Hospital of Santa Maria del Buon Gesù, paintings and frescoes by different artists.
Alberti's last work.
The Venetian square.
The fourteenth-century fortress in the upper part of the village, set of some scenes of Ladyhawke, with views of the Arda Valley.
Only the ruins remain of the Casale di Rocca Niceforo; the name recalls the Byzantine general Niceforo Foca il Vecchio, who led the campaign against the Saracens in 885-886.

The centre of medieval plant has chessboard streets and narrow houses, gathered around the Renaissance castle; at the end of July there is the Palio dei Conti Oliva, which evokes the life of court of the fifteenth century.

Also known as Palazzo dei Marchesi, it has a large loggia that houses the Fonti di Sopra, built in 1233, fed by the waters of Poggio di Montieri; a plaque on the façade recalls its construction and a marble coat of arms with the lion rampant the conquest of Sienese country. The foundations date back to 1621, when Vincenzo Salviati bought the marquisato by Cosimo II; in the first decades of the twentieth century it was renovated in neo-Renaissance style.
Gothic, started in 1390 and never ended up on the façade. Inside the sundial of Cassini, 67.27 m, the longest in the world, and the Chapel of the Magi.
City of the arcades in the valley between Salerno and the Coast, with the Benedictine Abbey of the SS. Trinity founded in 1011 by Saint Alferio and the walled village of Corpo di Cava.

The city of travertine and the hundred towers: Piazza del Popolo with Caffè Meletti, Piazza Arringo with the Cathedral of Sant'Emidio and the polyptychs of Carlo Crivelli, the Roman bridge of Solestà and the Quintana of August.
Medieval village above the valley of Cecina, 12 km from the sea, overlooking the islands of the Archipelago.
Visitable in limited days and hours

The pedestrian heart of the city, overlooking the Town Hall, built in the nineteenth century from the former Franciscan monastery of the fourteenth century, the church of St. Francis and the seventeenth century church of the Holy Spirit with a Renaissance portal to bas-reliefs. At the centre is the baroque column of Sant'Oronzo, about 20 meters high, carved in 1771 by Ostuni Giuseppe Greco as a thank you to the patron for having saved the city from the plague, with four statues of saints and on top the blessed saint.
A walk through the portals and coats of arms of Salento.
Romanesque, declared a national monument, connected to the new Baroque parish by a Via Crucis.
A small village of delight.
