In some halls of the Town Hall it collects furnishings and liturgical objects of the churches of the territory and private, from the fourteenth to the twentieth century; among the most interesting pieces the vestments with the coat of arms of the Doria and the bronze bell of San Bartolomeo fused in 1355.
The cathedral with its two-order façade, destroyed by the bombings of September 1943 and rebuilt since 1950; the famous bronze gate of the central portal is now rebuilt inside.
The flavors of the woods of Terminillo.

It houses a planetarium installed in 1994, indicated as the first in Piedmont for the study of stars; in the following years an antenna of radio astronomy was added and, in 1998, a tower with dome in fiberglass with optical instruments to observe and photograph objects of the deep sky. Open by reservation.

Built in 1496, it preserves on the main altar a polychrome marble triptych of the Gagini, a Madonna with a marble Child attributed to Domenico Gagini, a wooden crucifix Christ of the seventeenth century and a fifteenth-century fresco of the Madonna enthroned.
The carnival museum.

In the Adamello Brenta Nature Park, just outside Stenico, a 4.2 km ring walk (about 2 hours, 149 m of difference in altitude, suitable for families) climbs along a dirt road towards the Rio Bianco waterfall, crosses a stretch dug into the rock and reaches the botanical garden with educational positions on the medicinal plants and flora of the park, then continue in the BoscoArteStenico. From the parking lot of the Park information point.

Born as a watchtower and then bastion of the defensive walls of the village, it has the current appearance of the late fifteenth century, designed by Francesco di Giorgio Martini, with elements of the almond style attributed to the same architect.

In the Ducal Palace, summer residence of the Visconti-Sforza with facade rebuilt in 1625 by Francesco Maria Richini; set up by Luca Beltrami in 1911, it is permanently open since 2008. On the ground floor the Gipsoteca with about 200 casts of facade reliefs and cloisters; on the first floor the Pinacoteca with fourteenth-century frescoes by Bernardino de Rossi, the Madonna enthroned by Bartolomeo Montagna (1490 circa), the Santi Ambrogio and Martino attributed to Luini, the form of the Flagellation by Antonio Mantegazza and the Studiolo frescoed in the sixteenth century with the Sogno di Costantino. From January 2, 2026 open from Tuesday to Sunday 10-16, closed on Monday.

Already palace of Counts Zorzi, who ruled Mel for three centuries, started in 1510 and today municipal seat; the room on the first floor has frescoes by Marco da Mel with episodes of the Orlando Furioso (1545).
From the Dolomites to the Ortles in one look.

Green area near the center dedicated to the botanist of Villamaina Giovanni Gussone (1787-1866), professor at the Frederick II and court botanist, who identified in the area of the Mephyte the broom he called Anxantic Genista. The main avenues of olive trees, football and basketball courts, bowls, children's games and a small outdoor amphitheatre.
The perimeter of the ancient city.
A parish church with an unusual plant in the heart of the village.

A peasant house where the saint was born in Brendola in 1888 and died in Treviso in 1922, she spent her first youth; next door a small church was built where many faithful come to pray. The house is preserved almost intact, with the small doors, beds and utensils of the peasant life of the time and some civil and religious clothes of the saint; numerous ex-votes, especially for intercessions in favour of children, which the saint assisted as a nurse. Beatified by Pius XII in 1952 and canonized by John XXIII on May 11, 1961, the place is cared for by the Dorotean Sisters.
Eight centuries of civil architecture.
Not open to worship, under renovation for damage to the 1980 earthquake
Today the public wash-house preserves the original medieval fountains and a fresco of the Madonna with the Child.
The mirror of water in the shape of a heart.
A stage of the medieval route.

Completed in 1642 on a project by Francesco Contini, architect of Barberini, as entrance of the new Piazza del Sole in front of Santa Maria degli Angeli; it is decorated with the great sun and the three bees of the Barberini heraldic. Next, the archaeological area restored with the ancient ramp in basoli and a polygonal bastion of the walls.
A walk in the shade of the pine trees.
the MiC card, updated to June 2020, reports "closed" every day: check the opening on tel. 0761 459041
Hundred years of memory.
A village marked by the history of the Risorgimento.

Regional Museum of Veneto Agricoltura on two floors, in a building of the early fifties: it tells the human presence in Cansiglio from Prehistory to the present day, including the long phase of the Republic of Venice.

One of the most important villages in Piedmont, the kingdom of Barbera: the Fortress with the castle of the Asinari, linked to the Countess of Castiglione and the seat of the ICIF cooking school, the Museum of Barbera in the municipal palace, the hamlets of Loreto and Burio and the panorama of Bricco Lù.
Walk in the woods along the Degano.
Baroque have and majolica.

Tibetan bridge opened in summer 2016 on the Ragaiolo river: 100 meters of walkway about 60 meters high (1.366 m high) above the waterfalls, crossed in every season, even with snowshoes. About 30 minutes walk from the car park of Plan (Rabbi Fonti), passing through the Venetian sawmill of the Bègoi, or from the parking of the thermal baths; you can continue to the Fratte or Stablasolo hut and the Saént waterfalls. Not recommended for those suffering from dizziness; dogs should be carried in their arms.

It rises on the area of the ancient Roman Forum; here on 26 December 1194 Frederick II of Swabia was born, under a great imperial pavilion. The Cathedral of San Settimio, the Rococo Palazzo Balleani, the convent of San Floriano, dedicated to the patron saint, and Palazzo Ripanti, are just a few steps away.

Necropolis with eleven burials (770-750 BC), the greatest testimony of Phoenicians, Punics and Romans in the area; in the territory there are also neolithic domus de janas and nuraghi Atzori and Bacu Ollasta with villages of huts.
In the Asproni Institute, Art Nouveau palace of the early twentieth century: minerals, reconstructions of mine environments and original machinery.
In Poggio San Romualdo, it dates back to about 1000.
Unique building, with architectural references to the East.
The oldest collection of machines and models dedicated to Leonardo engineer and scientist, between Palazzina Uzielli and Castello dei Conti Guidi.
Historical residence of Bergamo Alta with frescoed rooms, period furnishings, an art collection on the Moroni family and terraced gardens; exhibitions in collaboration with the FAI.
Enter a mining gallery in the Middle Ages.
A path between military ruins and ancient borders over the country.
The Count's palace, now the town hall, with the museum dedicated to the extraction of mercury on the Amiata between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

Borgo del Fermano mentioned since 1050, linked in the thirteenth century to Brunforte: in the Pinacoteca del Palazzo Comunale is now guarded the Polittico di Carlo Crivelli of 1468, his first work known in the Marches; remains of the castle with Porta Sant'Antonio and the Museum of the ancient crafts. Historical center, monuments and museums are partially usable.
One of the most beautiful medieval squares in Italy.

The village was born on the Roman station Ad Ensem della Flaminia preserves the Civic Tower of the fourteenth century, the last surviving door of the ancient castle, the church of Sant'Antonio Abate of 1665, the parish church of Saints Philip and James of the sixteenth century with numerous works of art and the church of Mount Calvario of the seventeenth century.
The Baroque Cathedral of the Rione Valle.

Symbol of the city at the entrance of the acropolis, in front of Palazzo Spagna: a deer and the figure of Atteone placed after 1866 on a Roman funerary stele of the first half of the first century BC; not far, in Largo Garibaldi, a nineteenth-century slab with the deer rests on a Roman funerary shrine surmounted by a tuft.
The religious heart of the city of the popes.
From 17 November 2025 the theatre is temporarily closed for works

The municipality of Val di Funes at the foot of the Odle: in Tiso the Geodi Museum formed over 290 million years ago, in Santa Maddalena the late Dogotic church of 1492 and the church of San Giovanni in Ranui of 1744, from which starts the path to the Geisler Alm mountain hut.
The Friulian "puszta."
Visitable only by appointment (sindaco@comune.lacedonia.av.it)
A walk between water and views of the valley.

Romanesque church of the thirteenth century, enlarged and partly rebuilt around 1575 (data engraved on the facade), with rose window and double-fore bell tower; the frescoes are by Jacopo Siculo, including the Dormitio Virginis of 1536 in the apse basin.

From the 14th century, renovated around 1584; the altarpiece with the Madonna and Child between the Saints Giovanni Battista and Sebastiano was painted in 1482 by the pupil with his son Lattanzio Pagani.
A Roman bridge of Flaminia still standing.
€10 whole; €8 reduced (on Wednesday for all); only Palazzo del Fulgor €2; Art Card €14
The inmate graffiti and Sacconi's firm.

Built between 1332 and 1349 on a project by Angelo da Orvieto with the Gattapone, it dominates Piazza Grande; from the ground floor to the last it houses the archaeological museum, where the Eugubine Tables in Umbrian language (III-I century BC) and the art gallery are exhibited.
The chamber graves of the ancient city.

The Park's integral reserve between Opi and Civitella Alfedena: limestone amphitheatre and dolomia under Mount Sterpi d'Alto and the Balzo della Chiesa, between beech woods and black pines, where you can spot the chamois. You can visit only on foot and on the paths, also starting from Civitella; an easy path along the creek Scerto leads to the waterfalls, active all year round.
Even ski in the evening on the long illuminated track of Baradello.

Of the castle, perhaps wanted by a bishop of Turin around the Mille and confirmed to Bishop Charles by Frederick I in 1159, remains parts of the underground and external bastion, capitals, fragments of balustrade and other finds scattered in the park and in the gallery called Maria Bricca. It was declared national good after the Napoleonic occupation and was sold in 1808 and partly dismantled; in 1811 the Marquis Agostino Lascaris of Ventimiglia built the villa there. According to tradition, in 1706 the local Maria Bricca led the Piedmontese troops through the underground passages to the ballroom occupied by French officers.
The ancient village of the saint.

Defined the world's largest private rose garden, born in 1967 from the collections of Professor Gianfranco Fineschi: thousands of varieties (over 6,500 according to the card) from all continents, even rare, ordered in 21 sectors according to the classification, with plates indicating the name, age and creator of each rose. The best period is the main flowering, May-June.
The real center of Treviso, medieval piazza-salotto with the Palazzo dei Trecento and the Palazzo del Podestà with the 48 meters Civic Tower.
The two doors of Cassaro, from the palace to the sea.

Locality of the Riviera delle Palme with about 5 km of fine sandy beach, promenade of palm trees and Liberty villas, and behind the medieval village overlooking the sea: the Torrione della Battaglia with the works of Pericle Fazzini, the Museo Sistino dedicated to Pope Sixtus V, the church of Saint Lucia and the Orange Theatre.

It rises on the promontory, on the site of the ancient acropolis; destroyed by pirates, it was rebuilt in the middle of the sixteenth century, with a Latin cross with three naves and large windows. It preserves the wooden statue of the Black Madonna, of probable oriental origin; the pilgrimages culminate on 7 and 8 September.
Parish of the 13th century modified in the 16th century, with Gothic façade and rose window, Renaissance portal and unique nave with Baroque decorations and a canvas of the Assumption.

Blue giant bench, more than two meters high, of the network created by American designer Chris Bangle (the first was installed in Clavesana in 2010); placed in a panoramic point, allows you to look at the landscape from a different perspective. With the Big Bench passport you collect the stamps of the benches.
Historic building of the 15th century, one of the most important in the city.
The city lounge between liberty and neoclassical.
The botanical garden in the Palazzo di Brera, together with the INAF Astronomical Observatory.
The mother church of the village, above the museum.
The church of the patron, of Norman origin.

On the hill of the same name near the cemetery of Bardino Vecchio there are the ruins of a 'bastita' built during the War of the Final in the middle of the XV century: a fortification of 500 square meters, 80 m of perimeter and at least 6 m of height, depicted in the municipal coat of arms. A short ring starts from the square of Bardino Vecchio (oratory of San Carlo Borromeo and parish church of San Giovanni Battista), climbs steep among the pines up to the ruins and descends next to a cross on the precipice dated 1933-1934, returning between olive groves and woods along the Liguria Path. Free access on path in the woods, not accessible by wheelchair.
The fortress of Valentino.
Inside the popular theatre of the Apennine knights.

Built in the first century AD and remained in use until the beginning of the V, it was one of the most important Roman residential buildings on Garda, belonged to the Nonii of Brescia (probably to Marco Nonio Macrino, console in 154). The visitable sector preserves environments with pavement mosaics and remains of parietal paintings; further north there was a basin-fountain about 47 meters long. Open on Saturday and Sunday from May to September, 10-12 and 15-18.

Ring of about 2 and a half hours (change in altitude 450 m, for medium hikers, recommended from May to October) with departure and arrival in the village Ussolo, where you can see a fresco of Giors Boneto on an ancient tavern and the martyrdom of Santo Stefano painted in the nineteenth century on the facade of the parish. The path touches the chapel of Sant'Anna in the Vallone hamlet and numerous votive pylons, largely after the 17th century, including one with sundial at Grange Draio and two frescoes by the twentieth century painter Gauteri at Grange Passo and Grange Chioligiera.
The prehistoric valley before climbing to the caves.
The village church, a stone's throw from the castle.
The traces of the knights in the Brianza countryside.
Medieval convent with the chapel of San Giovanni frescoed by the Giotto school and a frescoed cloister accessible from Piazza Domenicani.

14th century church on Mount Asprano, where the castle of Castrum Coeli stood abandoned by the inhabitants who founded the village. On Monday in Pasquetta you will encounter the processions of Colle San Magno and Castrocielo for the ... Kiss of the Madonnas, with two identical statues of the Virgin who exchange a kiss.
A hydraulic work of the Renaissance.
See the restoration of the wounded heritage closely.
A canvas attributed to De Magistris.
renovation works in progress in the convent: only the church can be visited; normally access by reservation; the MiC indicates closed every day
The belvedere on the sea from the churchyard.
The historic cellars.
The symbol of Sulmona on Ovid Course.
The castle that houses the museums of the city.

Built at the end of the 12th century by the Counts Atti for the Camaldolese monks with stones of Sentinum, it is one of the most important Romanesque buildings of the Marche: an inscribed Greek cross plan, four pillars with semi-colons of granite, capitals of Lombard taste (one with the Crucifixion), narthex with carved portal; it contains frescoes of the Fabrian school, the altarpiece of San Benedetto di Agabiti (1524) and a 17th century carved and gilded palotto.
It dates back to the thirteenth century, when the village developed around the marina.
One of the largest nuraghi in Sardinia, with the dome intact.

On the hill remain traces of a place of worship of the 5th century B.C.: on the surface were found a gorgonion and ceramic pieces of the V-IV century B.C., while the precise function of the structure remains uncertain.
Along Via Roma, it houses the tomb of the last Duke of Urbino and on the main altar a Crucifix attributed to the Barocci school; in the right chapel the Madonna delle Nubi by Federico Barocci.
A wild gorge near the city.
Reachable with the hiking itineraries.
The "garden of wonders" wanted by Francesco I de' Medici, with the Colossus of the Apennines of Giambologna, part of the UNESCO site of the Medici villas and gardens.
The echo of the legend of Dionysius.
Over twenty murals in the historic center.

The house where Antonio Gramsci was born (1891-1937) is marked by a plaque. The space dedicated to him, the "Piano d'uso collectivee A. Gramsci is designed by the sculptor Giò Pomodoro and inaugurated on May 1, 1977, it has triangular plant with a fountain and a fireplace and was built with the participation of the whole population.

Three oratories of the historical center indicated by the Municipality among the main monuments: Oratorio del SS. Rosary in Santa Cita (Via Valverde 3), Oratory of the SS. Rosario in San Domenico (Via dei Bambinai 2) and Oratorio di San Lorenzo (Via dell'Immacolatella 5).
The nativity scene living in the castle.

One of the oldest churches in Viterbo, mentioned as early as 1068, with the apse protruding from the medieval walls, two Romanesque pergamous and an altar composed of parts of the IV and V centuries; next, the Baroque Porta Romana with the statue of Santa Rosa.
The rationalist fountain of Cesare Cattaneo and Mario Radice, symbol of the city of the twentieth century.
Situated in Broglio, where finds of a Greek necropolis and remains of mycenaean age have been found.
An English leader in the heart of Romagna.
The symbol of Altopascio, the tower of the bell that guided the travelers.
Under the crystal floor of the covered square you can see the remains from the Villanovian age to the Roman Bononia, up to the botanical garden of Aldrovandi.

At number 17 of Chemin Royal, once a Calvinist temple: in the sixteenth century Chianale was the only place in the valley with freedom of worship.

The only town in Campania (Katundi), with the Mother Church of St. Bartholomew dominating the upper part of the village, the sixteenth-century Palazzo Lusi with its archaeological exhibition, the Museo Vedovato in Palazzo Caccese and the last kalives, ancient stone houses of the Arbëreshë community.

A walk by the sea from which you can look at the boats that depart from one of the major fishing ports of the Mediterranean, with about 300 fishing boats; on the seafront the church of San Vito, patron of the city, and in the restaurants the red shrimp of Mazara.

Porta della Sardegna nord-oriente and economic center of Gallura, overlooking the marine area of Tavolara: the Romanesque basilica of San Simplicio, the archaeological museum on the islet of Peddone with the Roman ships sunk by the Vandals, the remains of the Roman city, the castle of Pedres and a rich nuragic heritage, between beaches like Pittulongu and Porto Istana and villages like San Pantaleo and Porto Rotondo.

The 12th century, rebuilt in 1234 by the monks of the Abbey of Fiastra and modified by Antonio Lombardo, has terracotta façade with rosette. Inside the glazed terracotta altar of Mattia della Robbia, the Coronation of Maria di Giacomo da Recanati, a Callido organ of 1775 and the astile cross of Lorenzo d'Ascoli (1414).
The town of Chiavari, linked to the Fieschi, with the medieval village of San Salvatore gathered around the basilica, the church of San Salvatore il Vecchio and the Comital Palace.

In the eighteenth century Palazzo Allegretti, near the fourteenth-century Piazza Vecchia, with a façade in gentle stone and two portals surmounted by the coats of arms Allegretti and Cenci. He collects works by contemporary artists and especially by the futurist Emilio Notte (Ceglie 1891 - Naples 1982), including "Piazza Mercatale di Prato" (1916), "Zodiac" (1929) and "Triptych of the Crucifixion" (1972). In the building also the municipal library.

Two routes between Moncrivello and Villareggia, with GPX tracks and map on the site of the Municipality. The Blue, without too steep stretches, is suitable for walkers, runners, cyclists and horses, you walk in the two senses and touches the two churches on the hill, panoramic points on the Alps, the plain, the Dora and the vineyards of Erbaluce and Nebbiolo, and a long stretch of the Naviglio di Ivrea; connected to the White Stones Path (about 15 km more) reaches about 25 km. Red alternates short climbs and technical descents, for experienced cyclists or hikers.

The castrum of Alichia, along the road to Cirò, was built in the middle of the fifteenth century and was a temple and then the Knights of Malta. The sanctuary on the hill of Bonaria founded in 1324 by the Aragonese, with the wooden statue of Our Lady that would save Spanish sailors in 1370 and gave the name to Buenos Aires; next to the white basilica started in 1704, with steps and panorama of the sea.

Center of the Gran Paradiso National Park in a house built by the municipality, dedicated to the biodiversity of the Soana Valley: ecosystems, products of the territory, history, traditions, legends and ancient crafts, with traditional furnishings, panels, collections of insects and a space where artisans and producers show their techniques. Times to ask in the center (tel. 0124 817377).
The history of the riding school in Pinerolo.

Set up by the former partisans of the ANPI after three years of collection and inaugurated in 1983, it tells the Resistenza in Ossola with hundreds of documents and photographs on the formations Garibaldi, Valtoce and Valdossola, photos of the fallen of the province, didactic paintings and materials on deportation, including a model of the crematorium of Dachau. Open from September to July only by reservation (tel. 340 5314140), closed in August.

The Lao runs 51 km from the province of Potenza to the Tyrrhenian Sea near Scalea; in the Natural Reserve of the Valle del Rijeka Lao its rapids, between gorges and canyons, are destination for rafting and canoeing.

Municipality of the coast domizio with the beaches of Baia Domizia and Baia Felice, overlooking the Aurunci Mountains and the Gulf of Gaeta; in Punta San Limato the remains of a Roman maritime villa of ancient Sinuessa.

Country of Gargano from the white houses on the hills, called "Terra delle almondi" or "Farfalla bianca del Gargano" , surrounded by centuries-old olive groves and overlooking a large beach; in its territory the Bay of Zagare with the faraglioni, the path to Vignanotica, the ruins of the abbey of Monte Sacro and the National Archaeological Museum with the Sansone collection.

Romanesque abbey on the left bank of the Esinante, documented by the 11th century (consecrated in 1086) and rebuilt in the thirteenth century: three naves and three apses, classroom for the laity, Gothic presbytery raised for the monks and crypt; until 1442 rivalled with Apiro. On May 25, the feast of the saint, the first ray of sun enters from an opening above the apse and illuminates a circle engraved in the stone.

Medieval village about 1000 meters on the Prenestini Mountains, with the Church of Santa Maria Maddalena and the Palazzo Barberini seat of the Naturalistic Museum; in the territory the hamlet of Guadagnolo, the Sanctuary of Mentorella and the Castagneto Prenestino.
The Romanesque on the Montorfano.
The castle on the Amerina street, which owes its name to the family of Pope Alexander VI, author of the first major modifications in 1479.

Built in 1939 by engineer Barbaro of Messina, with a churchyard, staircase and three portals; on the main altar the canvas of Bonanno of Messina in 1945 with the appearance of the Sacred Heart. Open during functions.

A well-preserved medieval centre built around the castle, built around the year 1000 on Roman ruins, with walls and a high watchtower; free municipality from 1500, from the 16th century was part of the Papal State until 1860.

Ancient limestone quarries from the Greek era today lush gardens: the side of Paradise with the Ear of Dionysius, a cave with surprising acoustics, the cave of Cordari, Salnitro, Intagliatella and Santa Venera.

Borgo della Maremma on the slopes of Monte Amiata, between Valle dell'Ombrone and Val d'Orcia, in the Montecucco area; in the center the Clock Tower and the church of San Michele Arcangelo, in the territory the fortified villages of Porrona, Sasso d'Ombrone and Castiglioncello Bandini, the Museum House of Monticello Amiata and the Reserve of Poggio all'Olmo.

The centre of Brindisi with its roots in the Iron Age, whose historic centre was profoundly transformed in the 17th and 18th centuries, when the Mesagnese architect Francesco Capodieci guided the reconstruction of many Baroque churches; among the main destinations the Norman-Svevo Castle with the archaeological museum MATER, the Mother Church of All Saints and the archaeological area of Vico Quercia.

Founded shortly after the year 1000 and remodeled in the following centuries, it houses a small canvas of the Assumption of the Virgin by Giovan Battista Moroni and a fresco of the fifteenth century Pietà.
The island in front of the village.

It dates back to the thirteenth century and rises on the remains of an ancient abbey; after a fire in the seventeenth century was rebuilt in 1691 by Urbano Fieschi, Count of Lavagna and Marquis of the fief of Savignon. Inside seventeenth-century paintings, including a canvas by Giovanni Battista Carlone, a Visitation of Saint Catherine from Genoa and a wooden statue of the 17th century Immaculate attributed to the school of Maragliano. Info: tel. 010 936627.
The road built in 1536 next to the ancient walls, from Piazza Trieste and Trento to Piazza Dante; the metro has stations that are works of art, like Toledo.

Museum and cultural center of printing and printing managed by the Italian mortgage Foundation, with museum, gallery, archive, library, print shop in mobile characters and auditoriums; the catalog includes characters, machines, books and printed books and stories of printers, and organize workshops of printing and letterpress printing. Open from Monday to Saturday 9-13 and 14-18, closed on Sundays and holidays; free under 8 years and for disabled.
Renaissance Palace of the XV century designed by Francesco di Giorgio Martini; inside the Teatro G. Perugini, called the smallest theatre in the Marche region.

A cylindrical tower on a quadrangular bastion, on a rock on a slope overlooking the Tyrrhenian coast; it was the upstream garrison that protected the village and housed the residence of the feudal lord, while the coastal towers controlled the sea. The origins are attributed to the Norman era and then Swabian.

Path set up by the vibrant hunting club: the halls exhibit trophies, embalmed specimens, weapons and hunting gear, ancient cartridges, books, prints and calls, each with caption; it welcomes schoolchildren and groups for hunting and naturalistic lessons, including protected species.

The path, which takes its name from the novel "The Lost Girl" inspired by the village, leads to the locality Cervi and Casa Lawrence, a villa where the writer D.H. Lawrence stayed with his wife Frieda in 1919.

Arco is considered the world capital of sport climbing, with cliffs equipped in the surrounding area; since 1986 it hosts every year at the end of summer the Rock Master, international climbing competition, in the Rock Master Climbing Stadium.
The first, Baroque in 1647, with a martyrdom of San Sebastiano from the Piola school; the second, documented since 1585 and rebuilt in the eighteenth century, with altars and a Crucifix.

Country of Tuscia at the foot of Mount Fogliano, between the via Cassia and the via Francigena: the Romanesque San Francesco with the crypt excavated in the tuff, the church of Santa Maria di Foro Cassio with the Madonna attributed to the young Masaccio, and in the territory the Etruscan tombs facade of Norchia and the great mound of Grotta Porcina.
A destination for a panoramic hike over the castle.
Inaugurated in 1997 by the Economic Society in the palace of Via Ravaschieri and in the garden.

19th century building started in 1862, after the insurrection of 1860 led by Giustino Croce; it hosts a permanent exhibition of sculptures and paintings by contemporary artists.
An outdoor break between thematic areas dedicated to biodiversity.

Piazza Riolfatti is the heart of the village, with the fountain-washer framed by a double row of Hippocastani; the center is decorated with marble fountains, including the large water fountain, and noble palaces: Palazzo Guerrieri Gonzaga in via Cavolavilla, built around the seventeenth century by the counts of Festivals of Braunsfeld, Palazzo Camelli (now Town Hall), Palazzo Madernini and Palazzo Marzani.
The point where the Roman settlers founded the city over two thousand years ago, tracing the streets with the groma, the instrument of the geometries.

Residency of the counts of Arc between the XII and XVII century, is today a vast ruin of walls, cisterns, prison (Prigione del Sasso), Torre Grande and fortress with the Renghera tower, whose bell called the peasants to prayer. In the residential body near the Torre Grande one of the most important cycles frescoed profane of the fourteenth century in the alpine area, with courteous scenes of life, departures to checkers and battles; from the Prato della Lizza and a glass platform the view extends over the plane of Sarca to Garda. Walk up among the olive trees in 20-30 minutes; free entry with Garda Trentino Guest Card.
An ancient fortress with its necropolis.

Valley with intact landscapes and bare, first winding and steep, which in Lignan opens in a vast panoramic plateau.

Baths of 19th century origin born to take advantage of the sulphuric water that flows at the foot of the sanctuary.

The marble of the Shroud and the knives of Frabosa.

Gipsoteca di arte contemporanea in sette sale nel parco della villa di Enrico Butti (Viggiù 1847-1932), student and then professor of sculpture in Brera, author of the Minatore (Grand Prix at the Paris Universal Exposition of 1889) and the monument to Verdi in Milan (1913). It preserves 87 original models in plaster and some paintings, donated by the sculptor to the Municipality in 1926; in 2002-2004 the restoration added three rooms for the plasters of the monument to Verdi. Hours: Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 14-18.30, Wednesday and Saturday 10-12 and 14-18.30; Sunday closed in winter.

Country of the Enne hinterland linked to the ancient Morgantina, a Sicilian and Greek city excavated by the University of Princeton since 1955: in the Archaeological Museum, in the former convent of the Capuchins, the goddess of Morgantina has returned; in the village the churches of San Domenico, Sant'Anna and Santa Maria La Cava with the Adelasia Tower and the ruins of Castellaccio.

Built in the 16th century as a cooperative by the inhabitants on the push of the parish priest Don Taialacqua, it still works with water: the wheel moves a rod that transforms the rotation in the motion of the blade; it produced the axes called Molvene, sold in the area of Riva del Garda. A visitor centre explains the operation and role of wood in the Trentino economy; the valley is still called Val delle Seghe.
Well-preserved Nuraghi in the Tirso valley.
Castrum Lapidum founded in 1062 after the Norman conquest with stones of the Campania Amphitheatre; hospital in 1734 and arsenal since 1806, its tower is national monument since 1875.
Cutrofiano ceramic, from terracotta to whistle.

In a barracks of the mid-nineteenth century that incorporates the tower of Sant'Erasmo, where in 1278 Roberto d'Angiò was born, above the Capitolium del Foro: finds of the excavations of necropolis, sacred areas and amphitheatre and the exhibition "I Segni del Paesaggio: L'Appia e Capua" .
The hunting palace of the Bourbons and the horses of Persano.
A water mill that still grinds chestnuts.
The oldest settlement in Salerno.

The birthplace of San Francesco di Paola, patron saint of Calabria, on the Tyrrhenian coast: the Sanctuary in the gorge of the Isca stream, the point of arrival of the Way of San Francesco, the historic center with Piazza del Popolo and the Fountain of Pisciarieddi, the castle of probable Norman origins, the Byzantine underground church of Sotterra and the long beach of Marina di Paola.

WWF nature reserve along the road to Molveno, just a few minutes drive from the village: a flat ring of about 3 km (about an hour) with panels on flora and fauna; in the lake trout and salmerini, boats and fishing.

The castle, built on sections of the Hellenistic walls on the rocky plateau of the mountain, was taken to the Saracens by the Grand Count Ruggero with the help of the Basilian monks; the fortified citadel extended for over a kilometer from the Mother Church to the ruins of the Church of the Name of Jesus, protected by overhanging walls and walls with towers. There are also sections of the city and the Hellenistic-Roman walls of the 4th century BC.

From 2000 on the ground floor and basement of the Town Hall, exhibits finds of the territory from the protohistory (XIII century BC) to the high Middle Ages (VI century A.D.). The ground floor is dedicated to the factory of Scoppieto, active from the end of the 1st century BC to 70-80 A.D.: production cycle of the sealed earth, model of Roman furnace and trade along the Tiber until Alexandria of Egypt, with models of ships.
Village on a hill overlooking Lake Barrea, with narrow well-maintained streets, a tower of the 14th century and the church of San Nicola, as well as shops of local products and museums.

It was one of the main fortifications of the Federici family and, renovated over time, became a noble residence; In Lombardy it dates back to the 12th century.

At the entrance of the village: built by the Pisans at the end of the thirteenth century in late Romanesque forms and then adapted in Gothic style; the current appearance derives from renovations. In Piazza Santa Maria the procession de s'Incontrau ends at Easter.
Rococo eighteenth-century residence with Italian garden and four rooms dedicated to the seasons.
Robbian terracotta.

Founded around 1135 by Saint Bernard of Chiaravalle at the request of the bishop of Piacenza Arduino and completed in the following century; the monks, removed in Napoleonic age, returned in 1937. The Basilica of the Assumption, in bricks with three naves, marks the passage from the Romanesque to the Gothic; in the octagonal chapel near the sacristy frescoes of fourteenth-century influence of Giotto. The 13th-century cloister, intact on the entire perimeter and built according to a complex numerical symbolism, is among the best preserved of its time; completes the complex the chapter room. For the Corpus Domini (between May and June) the nave is covered with a carpet of petals that reproduces paintings and sacred images. Open 8.30-12 and 14.30-18.30, on Thursdays only in the morning; free parking; shop with liquors and herbal teas of monks.

The Town Hall in the former oratory of San Filippo Neri, Palazzo Stancanelli on the main square, Palazzo Salvo Risicato in via del Duomo, restored by the Municipality, and the eighteenth-century Casa Fontana under the Duomo, surrounded by a wall with openings adorned with sandstone sculptures.
The shape of the medieval city still legible.
Neapolitan art inside the anti-Turkish tower.

14th century brick chapel with round apse, built on the base of an 11th century watchtower. The cycle of interior frescoes is dated 1451 and signed   .Frater Enricus Pinxit: in the Gothic apse the Christ Judge in almond between angels and symbols of the Evangelists, on the walls scenes of the legend of the Pilgrim of Compostela and St. James Major, in memory of the pilgrimage route called Roa Marenca. You can visit independently by booking date and time with the app "Churches with open doors" and by framing the QR code at the entrance.
Museum set up in a mill that preserves objects of the peasant life of the last century.

Long walk with palm trees and benches on the Gulf of Naples, dominated by Vesuvius; on clear days you can see Capri, Ischia and the Sorrento peninsula. The beach is free of black volcanic sand and establishments for a fee, and the nearby port, one of the most important in Campania, at sunset is animated by seagulls, boats and fishermen. Museum recently established with a photographic exhibition on the processing of chestnuts from the early twentieth century.

Satin to the ground by the earthquake of 1783, it was rebuilt lower on a project by Vincenzo Ferrarese for Ferdinand IV, with a chessboard system, squares, tree-lined avenues and fountains; the earthquake of 1908 destroyed almost all the churches except those of Carmel and Santa Maria di Portosalvo.
One of the symbols of Lecco, now home to the Mountain Museum and temporary exhibitions.

Opened at the end of 2005 in the underground rooms of the ancient Palazzo Canestrari, it collects household objects of the copper forcese handicrafts, including the stills called "tamburla" (tamburla) used to distill the mixture from wine. The educators and artisans of the Terravita association organize workshops for children and young people (SpazioLab).
Anselmo's birthplace.

Along the Black that preserves traces of the ancient walls and one of the four original entrance doors, with the churches of St. Paternian and St. Lawrence and the former church of Saints Mary and Jesus.

Fraction with a medieval castle and the church of San Biagio of the twelfth century, linked to Franciscan history.

It is located in the Munich Plant, a former industrial plant destroyed by a fire in 1922 and completely restored in the early 2000s, which also houses municipal offices, a conference room and the historical archive of the municipality.
Taste the vine that bears the name of the village.

At about 1,800 meters, you can reach from Linguaglossa with the Mareneve road: in winter ski resort (steps between 1,800 and 2,317 meters), in summer off-road buses to the base of summit craters (about 3,100 m) and trails to the Observatory of Pizzi Deneri (2,900 m), on the edge of the Valle del Leone, and to Monte Nero delle Concazze and the abyss of the eruption of 1923.
Built in 1220, the year of the Late Romanesque bell tower, it was rebuilt in the eighteenth century. It is among the stages not to be missed in the historic center.
Encircled on a spur overlooking the Campidano, with paved roads, stone houses with portals and manor houses like the seventeenth-century Casa Pilloni.
A Roman village on the slopes of Subasio, right from Baglioni until 1583: the Baglioni Chapel frescoed by Pinturicchio, the Roman gates and Villa Fidelia.
The house where Johann Wolfgang Goethe lived during his stay in Rome, with Andy Warhol's screen portrait of 1982.

currently undergoing restoration (FAI), no information on openings
