Borgo 828 meters in the Cilento National Park, Vallo di Diano and Alburni, second highest municipality in the province of Salerno, with a medieval center dominated by the Norman castle, ancient churches linked to Greek monks and Templars and the Antiquarium with the remains of the funerary monument of the Insteii.

Built by Giovanni Battista Groppi in 1761 on a panoramic terrace preceded by cypresses: it preserves a Santa Rosalia by Pietro Novelli, a mystical wedding of Saint Catherine of Camillo Procaccini and the tomb of Marta Tana of Santena, mother of Saint Louis.

Rebuilt between 1460 and 1491 by the jurist Bartolomeo Barattieri, ambassador of Piacenza to Pope Julius II, as the epigraph in the Courtyard of the Knights recalls; he remained at the Barattieri until 1993. Rectangular plant with entrance mast and two round towers on the north side, square courtyard with double order of arches; you can visit it entirely, with over 30 rooms furnished and decorated, including two Halls of Honor, the Hall of Arms and the Library with about 2,000 volumes from the early times of printing. In the basement there is the exhibition "China Millennial" with more than 40 copies of Xi'an terracotta warriors; the guided tour lasts about an hour and a quarter.
The Mercy of John by Mel.
Dante on the walls.

The most panoramic historical village of the municipality, between the valleys of Enza and Termina: castle on Monte Lugol founded at the beginning of the thirteenth century by Atto Baratto (today private residence, not visitable), watchtower of the Guardiola documented from the early fourteenth century and sixteenth-century church of San Lorenzo on Mount Oca. Nine panels and a guide describe the routes on foot and by mountain bike; here it is said to be born Fanfulla, hero of the Challenge of Barletta.

Borgo della pordenona plain crossed by the Reghena, born from a Roman military district on the road between Iulia Concordia and Norico; it grew around the Benedictine abbey of Santa Maria in Sylvis, in the Middle Ages among the major religious centers of Friuli, fortified after the incursions of the Hungarians and frescoed in the fourteenth century by the school of Giotto.

High-altitude natural lake at 1,775 meters, among the most evocative of the northern Apennines: from the Doganaccia (1.547 m, reached by cable car) the path no. 66 rooms for the Arcana Cross and the Calanca in about 1 hour and 10 minutes, 8 km round trip.
Architecture of the twentieth century in the station.
The most authentic Rome.

Built in 1822 by Paolina Bonaparte Borghese, it houses the Archaeological and Man Museum, the Museum of musical instruments, the monumental apartments of Paolina and the atelier of the painter Alfredo Catarsini; in front, the monument to the poet Shelley, died in a shipwreck offshore in 1822.
Museum renovated with the artist's first works and paintings of legends, female figures and landscapes.

Almost all underground route under the streets of the village, between olive mills excavated between the 15th and 19th centuries and recently restored, reminiscent of the weight of oil in the economy of the Land of Otranto; you can visit with guided tours.

Built between 1752 and 1764 on a project by Domenico Schiavi, it contains works by the Venetian painters Bassano, Diziani and Novelli, frescoes by Angelo Schiavi, a altarpiece by Fontebasso, paintings by the Evangelists and Apostles by Nicola Grassi and a sixteenth-century aquasantiera attributed to Bernardino da Bissone.
The crypt with the relics of the patroness.

In the Palazzo delle Opere Pie dell'Isola Maggiore he exhibits embroidery from the early twentieth century of the school founded by Elena Guglielmi, daughter of Senator Giacinto Guglielmi, where the fishermen's daughters learned the "Irish Point" in crochet; the school had international recognitions.

Historical cable in Tupinet, on the road to the Montano Park, abandoned after the Second World War: the route shows with wooden figures the manual phases of stone processing in the nineteenth century, with original elements of the quarry and panels. Along the main road there is a rebuilt lime furnace. Visits only in small groups, with authorized guide and favorable time (information Office Il Barba).

Hiking route of about 6 km that connects the Ariostesca Rocca to the Fortezza di Mont'Alfonso: from the Rocca follow via Farini and cross the bridge over the Turrite Secca, where the white-red trails begin, then a dirt road leads to the village of Torrite, from which it climbs to the Fortezza. In Castelnuovo there are also the Via Matildica del Volto Santo and the Via del Volto Santo, which ends at the Duomo of Lucca.
By bike between fountains and farmhouses of the Bassa.
Ancient mill with a wooden castle on which lay the two millstones for flour. Open at local events or on request for schools; accessible on one floor.
In the Casa-Torre a route reconstructs the history of Rocca Pia; audio guides are available. MiC card updated to 2021, without timetable: contact the museum (tel. 0864 203005).
Beautiful to photograph with afternoon light.
The museum next to the excavations.
In the former church of San Romano, the treasures of the Duomo, including the organ doors of Cosmè Tura with the Annunciation and San Giorgio and the dragon (1469).

Church of 1910 was created to replace an ancient medieval chapel of Santa Giuliana, the city's compatron, along the path of the aqueduct from Arcopinto to Atella; it is linked to the funaries of Piazza Miseno. The circular plant recalls the Pantheon of Rome and the basilica of St. Francis of Paola in Naples.
A tour of palaces, fountains and memories of the Knights of Malta.
From the early Christian Martyrion to the medieval tombs.

Beech of about 150 hectares in the Bracciano-Martignano Regional Natural Park, since 2017 part of the UNESCO site of the ancient primordial beech forests of the Carpathians and other regions of Europe, with beech trees next to oaks and pine trees. It crosses the CAI 175C trail, a 8.4 km ring (about 2 hours, 205 m of climb, difficulty T) that starts from the main square under the municipality and is walkable, by bike and horseback, with picnic area and water point in the locality Cerratina.
The nineteenth-century residences of merchants who replaced the old warehouses, including Palazzo Carciotti, Palazzo Gopcevich and Palazzo Scaramangà.

Gothic church of the thirteenth century in bricks: in the Bacci chapel the cycle of the Legend of the True Cross by Piero della Francesca (1452-1466), one of the masterpieces of Renaissance painting; also an Annunciation attributed to Signorelli.
In the historic centre, built in the 20th century on a structure of the sixteenth century; on 18 May the feast of St. Gavino is solemnly celebrated.
A reborn castle as an artist's house.

The village is located on a Roman villa of the second half of the first century BC: the remains, with mosaic floors, are visible in a building of Via del Tribunale, a private patrician house near Piazza Garibaldi.

Country of Alta Pusteria at the foot of the Sesto Dolomites, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: from the Val Fiscalina, in the Tre Cime Nature Park, you climb to the Tre Cime, while the iconic Sesto iconic trail marks the hours with its peaks; in the village the parish with the macabre dance of Rudolf Stolz and the museum dedicated to the painter, at the height of the Reinhold Messner Haus on Mount Elmo and the open-air museum of the Great War.

Fasano fraction inside the Dune Costiere Park, with fine and clear sand, dunes of Mediterranean maquis and sloping seabed suitable for children; several times Blue Flag and Green Flag, is also known for its thermal baths. The 35-metre-high lighthouse was built in 1928 and is the symbol of the Fasano Navy.
The astronomical clock of the sixteenth century.
Tarquinia beach, suitable for relaxing walks.
The monumental heart of the village, above the hall of the Biga.
A church on the temple of Cybele.

The seaside resort of the Riviera delle Palme with the medieval fortified village of Marano (Cupra Alta) on the hill, a free commune from the 11th century with fortified port, and to the north the Archaeological Park of the Roman Cupra Maritima, with the Forum and the remains of a temple; in the village the Piceno Malacological Museum, with over 900,000 shells.
The walled village of the Knights of Malta.
The clear sea between pumice and lard.
The eight-century layers of fiefdoms on the hill of Motta.

The small village of Alto Molise on the border with Abruzzo, about 960 meters on the northern slopes of Monte Miglio, destroyed by the bombings of 1943 and surrounded by woods of beech and oaks famous for the white truffle; on the mountain the polygonal walls of Sanniti, in the village the Civic Museum built with the stones of the rubble and, to the north, the astronomical observatory "Leopoldo Del Re" .

On the cliff under the tower, preceded by a large garden with centuries-old plants, it was the seat of the baronial power of the Duchy of Carpineto and in the seventeenth century it was bought by the Municipality; there was transcribed the act of peace of 1477 between Carpineto and the neighboring communities. Today it hosts the museum "Reggia dei Volsci" (Flights Reggia). The tower, part of the medieval castrum, has a sixteenth-century clock by master Caesar from Subiaco and a 17th-century majolica exhibition.

Borgo Bandiera Arancione in the heart of the Pollino National Park, with views of the Serra del Prete, the Serra Dolcedorme and Monte Pollino: the Sanctuary of Madonna del Pollino, the Bosco Magnano and the panoramic Ride Ride ride by Carsten Höller.

A single arched bridge, lowered and slightly sharp on the Rio Vallunga near the hamlet Vernè, of a system certainly before the nineteenth century and once very frequented along a commercial itinerary; it is made of local stone split with original parapets and is still accessible. It is reached in short with a path in the woods along the river.
Ancient eighteenth-century residence of the Saluzzo-Paesana, completely restored, today municipal library and exhibition space.
12th century church with a wooden crucifix attributed to Pietro Cavallini, the Evangelists of Domenico Brogi and frescoes by Dilvo Lotti.
The prehistory and Roman age of Lomellina in a single museum.
Borgo that preserves evidence of his Middle Ages.
Two villages walled above the Cesano.
A frescoed boat in front of the Brenta industrial archaeology.
The Perugino in a small village museum.
The Roman Turin.
The church with the paintings of Ludovico Lana, linked to Modena between Renaissance and Baroque, theme of the municipal thematic visits.
The cycle of the Passion of Fermo Stella on the tramezzo.

In the Castle on the promontory of Baia, which preserves the remains of a Roman villa of the II-I century BC with mosaic floors, the route tells Cuma, Puteoli and Liternum; from the Piazza d'Armi the view sweeps over the gulf of Naples.

Naturalistic and ethnographic itinerary restored by the CAI of Ormea, with low levels and divisible in stages: from Piazza della Libertà touches the villages Pronai, Chioraira, Aimoni and Biranco with a stretch of balcony on the Tanaro Valley, to Ponte di Nava. Visit Cuneese indicates it in about 40 km (about 32 km and 1,540 m of difference in altitude in the mountain bike card, recommended from April to November).
Three Greek temples standing in the meadows.
The nut oil mill.

Inaugurated on July 24, 2022 in the San Luigi hamlet, it is the second "Big Bench" for everyone after that of Paroldo: a giant bench designed for anyone who can get up there, even in a wheelchair, thanks to a small access ramp, to the openable backrest and to a part of the seat in the plane where he can station the wheelchair.

On the top of Mount Spineto (459 m), where the inhabitants took refuge in 1155 when a department of Federico Barbarossa sacked and burned Stazzano: in thanksgiving they built a chapel to the Madonna. The sanctuary was wanted by Monsignor Paolo Arese, Bishop of Tortona from 1620 to 1644; today it has three naves and three altars. According to the municipality, the view that you can enjoy on clear days is enough alone to justify the climb.
the gate opens only for guided tours booked by phone with the Library (030 984488)
Panoramic villages on the heights of Lesa, starting point for easy excursions on the paths of the territory.

Built in 1735 by the Bigotti family next to its own palace, it is one of the most important examples of Baroque in the Diano Valley: exterior with Corinthian pilasters and capitals, interior decorated with stuccoes and altar with wooden inlays alternating with polychrome marbles.

12 km long path along the irrigation canal from Cermes to Tel, at the entrance of the Val Venosta, half coast with wide views of the Merano basin, the Dolomites and the Gruppo di Tessa; along the tavern and inn path with gardens and panoramic terraces.

Historic bar-tavern founded by the monks in the eighteenth century, considered the place of origin of the almond wine, probably invented by the owner Don Vincenzo Blandano; it preserves an album of signatures of illustrious visitors since 1907.
Carlo Alberto's palace of stays and his terrace park.
World War II material, including trucks, tanks, a helicopter and two aircraft.

Duke's city of Farnese and Bourbon, UNESCO Creative City for Gastronomy since 2015. A unique ticket from the Civic Museums opens six museums, including the Chamber of São Paulo and the house of Toscanini.
The Bergamo wooden sculpture.
The baroque stuccoes and the relics of the saint.
The statues and portraits of the Roman city.

Medieval fortification built by the Veronas, symbol of the village: there are still crenellated walls and towers, at the top of a village of streets and alleys that go up to the castle; inside the walls stands the church of San Biagio, linked to the religious origins of the village. From the top there is a wide panorama of the Mincio valley. Free admission (pleasant offers), with opening of the clock tower on Sundays and holidays afternoons from Pasquetta at the end of August and during the Grape Festival in September.
Montegrotto is known throughout Europe for its mud therapy and its waters were exploited already in Roman times; today it has over 240 thermal pools and numerous activities related to wellness.
In the eclectic villa of 1887 surrounded by a large park: graphics, painting and Italian sculpture of the twentieth century and contemporary.

In via Rubadello, a few kilometers from the centre, an area of ecological rebalancing that recreates the typical environments of the Po Valley, with nature trails and observation points; the oasis Le Cicogne has stork aviary, house and garden of butterflies, area for ungulates, lakes and a classroom. Guided tours and for schools by reservation (Environment Office of the Municipality or Le Cicogne Association).
The museum dedicated to the agropastoral culture of the territory, indicated among the places of culture of the city.

The church of the capital was designed by architect Gianni Avon; in front, three lindens symbol of the Holy Trinity recall the ancient custom of linden as a meeting place. In Hrastje there is the "Villaggio Mozzoni-Crespi" (Village Mozzoni-Crespi), built after the earthquake and donated by the owners.
Twenty thousand objects of artisan Sicily.
€7 full, €5 reduced, €2 from 18 to 25 years (with the Surgeon's Domus)

Small agricultural town of Lomellina dominated by an imposing castle with shelter, one of the most significant fortified complexes of the province of Pavia, where they stayed Isabella d'Aragona, Massimiliano I of Habsburg and Carlo V; inside the Strada family preserves an archaeological museum with finds of the Lomellina.
The Norman Abbey of Pisticci.

At Punta Alice, at the mouth of Lipuda, the remains of the sanctuary that tradition binds to Filottote, founder of Krimisa. The archaic temple of the end of the sixth century BC (cell of about 27 x 7.90 m) was expanded at the end of the fourth century BC, after the conquest of Bretty, in a stone doric peripter temple of about 46 x 19 m; Paul Orsi identified it in the excavations of 1924. From here comes the acrolith of Apollo, a Greek work of 440-430 B.C.
The hill of Infinity.

Seven "perdas fittas" are 1,2 to 2,2 meters high on the side of the Zerfaliu basin, carved with hammers with protoanthropomorphic traits and dated between IV and III millennium B.C.; about 200 meters a dolmen tunnel about 9 meters long, whose kits are in part at the Menhir Museum. You can reach from Laconi towards the farm Genna 'e Corte, then walk over a gate.
Pedal on the old railroad.
A century of photography and cinema told by the devices.

The capital of the Longobard Duchy on the Umbra Valley: the Basilica of San Salvatore, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Duomo with frescoes by Filippo Lippi, the Albornoziana Rock and the Tower Bridge; since 1958 the city of the Festival of the Two Worlds.
The Romanesque church of San Giusto inside the walls and the Gothic loggia of the Judges next to the entrance door.

Natural arc with a light of about 40 meters, minimum thickness of 9 meters and width of 20 meters, indicated as the largest in Europe: according to one hypothesis it is what remains of an ancient karst cave (covolo) eroded by water, according to another is linked to the earthquake of 1223. Under the collapsed boulders at the base and in two caves were found remains of the Paleolithic, exposed in the nearby museums. Andrea Mantegna depicted it in the frescoes of the Chamber of the Sposi in Mantua and the tradition has it that Dante, exile to Verona guest of Cangrande della Scala, was inspired by the Malebolge. Walking paths and stairs with stone signs descend under the arch; accessible 24 hours a day, with parking at the Trattoria Ponte di Veja.
A scenic baroque staircase.

Built in 1731-1735 by Filippo Barigioni and included in the network of the historical residences of Lazio: on the first floor Roman and medieval marbles under the coats of arms of Pope Julius II, Henry VIII and Cardinal Christopher Bainbridge, who had jurisdiction over Vetralla in 1511.
The only temple church in Piedmont.
The mother church of the diocese, begun in 1604 and completed in 1825 by Vantini.
The private chapel of the Clarisse with a trilobed plan, unique in the region, decorated with stuccoes, gilding and mosaic floor; the former monastery is now a cultural center.
season 2026 from March 15 to November 8, closed in winter (schlosstirol.it)

In the former town hall, a four-storey eighteenth-century palace with elements of the noble carnival house, which became an exhibition venue in 1992; the name means "How We Were." It reconstructs the life of local communities with kitchen, bedroom, hut and haymaking, wool processing, Gerle manufacturing, crafts and a sector particularly rich in costumes and accessories; in the same building an exhibition by photographer Gino Del Fabbro and the cast of a stone found in Pierabech with prints of tetrapod of the lower Triassic (about 250 million years ago). It is part of the CarniaMusei network; information to the Tourist Office (0433 72202).
Built between 1722 and 1749 by the Confraternita degli Agonizzazioni (or St. Joseph), with a bell tower of 1804; it was named ducal oratory by Don Ferdinando di Borbone, confirmed by Maria Luigia.
Ancient portal covered with thick carvings of Byzantine, classical and Islamic inspiration: the sources suggest to stop to admire it before passing under it.
The flowered monophora.

The historic centre of Castello, in a panoramic position, with bars and restaurants; among the things to see the red civic tower and the churches of the Madonna del Soccorso and Santa Maria Assunta. At the end of November-December there are the Christmas markets of Santa Claus Castle.

Built in 1279, during the prosperity of the village, it rises just outside the walls: a large building, mainly in terracotta, with stone facade and Romanesque and Gothic elements. It is very popular for weddings and choral concerts.
Contemporary art in a former industrial complex.
Two-wheeled walking shops.

The Roman colony, perhaps founded by Caesar or Ottaviano and at its apogee at the beginning of the III century AD, was the main port of call of the Roman Sardinia: you can visit the central baths called the Palazzo di Re Barbaro, the Maetzke and Pallottino thermal baths with four columns of the peristyle, the Domus of Orpheus with the mosaic of the poet playing the lira and the Domus of the mosaics, paved streets and workshops. On the Riu Mannu the bridge of the first century A.D., seven arches for 135 meters, is the largest Roman bridge on the island and was used until the mid-Twentieth century; remains traces of the aqueduct and the necropolis of Tanca Borgona, with 32 frescoed and mosaic burials. Guided tours from Tuesday to Saturday at 9:30, 10:30, 12:15, optional booking.

Dedicated to the nearby Bosco dell'Alevé, it reproduces in real scale a stretch of December in a single large diorama that can be walked along a path painted between the pine trees and a rocky wall typical of the highest altitudes. Among the vegetation the animals of the forest, dead specimens due to accidental causes (investments, power lines, windows) and prepared for popularity. Managed by the Monviso Park.
As was lived in Carnia, in the northernmost country of the region.

Three rooms annexed to the civic library of Palazzo Luisia exhibit about fifty works donated by the Vigonese painter Michele Baretta (1916-1987), mostly preparatory studies for sacred frescoes performed between 1936 and 1962; the library also preserves the cartoons of his frescoes.
A little-known church in the center.

In the historic center the Bronze Horse of Nina Akamu inspired by the Sforza monument, the Piazza dei Guidi designed by Mimmo Paladino and, behind the castle tower, the Man of Vinci by Mario Ceroli who reinterprets the Vitruvian Man.
The chivalrous ride of the neighborhoods of Arezzo that runs in Piazza Grande, signalled by Visit Tuscany among the things not to be missed.
The court manufacture founded by Ferdinand I in 1588 for the clerk in hard stones: work benches, instruments and masterpieces of inlay.
closed from 15 September 2026 for extraordinary works at the water tanks to protect amphibians, reopened in spring 2027
last stretch of access on dirt and sandy roads
The history of the Unity of Italy.
Private property, visit by reservation.
A Roman dome among the houses.
The walled village of longevity.
Free entrance; boat crossing for a fee
A defensive tower became a prison.
Entirely frescoed in 1416 by Jacopo and Lorenzo Salimbeni, from walls to ceiling.
You can see it from afar in the plain.
The nineteenth-century theatre of the city.

Municipality of Val d'Ega with the Baroque sanctuary of Pietralba, linked to the apparition of 1553 and visited by John Paul II in 1988, the Romanesque church of Sant'Elena frescoed around 1400 by the school of Bolzano and the museum of sacred art in the tower of Castel Thurn.
Five Lots and a 70-meter rococo gallery.

Bread country on the Ionian side of Pollino, 650 meters on the slopes of Mount Sellaro and dominated by the remains of a medieval castle; above the village the rock sanctuary of Santa Maria delle Armi, under the Ninfe Cave with its sulphurous waters, and two small museums dedicated to bread and loricate pine.

Drenchia stretches on the ridge of a Moorish amphitheatre in the highest part of the Natisone Valleys; the villages of Obenetto and Cras preserve the traditional rural architecture of the valleys, made of stone houses. The territory houses two votive churches, Santa Maria Assunta and San Volfango, and numerous panoramic paths towards the Kolovrat and a stretch of the Path of Peace.
A park of twentieth century sculptures, pioneer of contemporary art museums in Italy.

Wanted in 1823 by Carlo Maria Gambarini for himself and the family, designed by Giovanni Battista Capitanio and built under the direction of Giuseppe Catto; sculptures by Antonio Gelpi il Giovane, including two painful winged figures and the great statue of Time on the pediment, and Masonic and esoteric symbols. Inside there is an octagonal chapel with the tombs of the Gambarini by Luigi Cocchi and a bust by Rosa Tarsis Cagnola by Vincenzo Vela; in the crypt is buried the music critic and composer Franco Abbiati.
The story of Armerina Square.

The 12th-century Mastio of the Arab-Norman citadel, seat of the Captain of Justice and under the Borbons sentmental prison until the 1970s. It houses the Civic Art Gallery "Gaetano Zito" (since 2022) with the Portrait of Paolo III Farnese in Tiziano, the only work of the painter to the south of Naples; the Archaeological Antiquarium with exhibits of about 6,000 years from the excavations of the Universities of Messina and Cambridge; the Civic Lapidarium and the exhibition of the ancient book, with a History of Italy of Guicciardini of 1604. Times indicated: 10-13 and 16.30-19.30.

Borgo with Roman traces and medieval walls, known for over 500 years for its ceramic and majolica handicrafts, woodworking and the restoration of antique furniture; in mid-July it hosts the Exhibition of antiques, restoration and artistic handicrafts. Among the palaces, Palazzo Narducci of the sixteenth century with portal in rustic stone and Palazzo Lazzarini, already of the Lazzarini in 1342.
In Via Siccardi, the last preserved access to the ancient village, whose walls were demolished in 1487.

The only Liberty-style villa in Breganze, with a corner tower, built at the beginning of the twentieth century and the headquarters of the command of the Genio in the Great War; today it houses the Astico Mountain Union. In the garden, the ancient 19th century icebox, semi-basement and brick, restored and open for events such as the San Martino Fair.

Opened in 1963, it exhibits the sculptural groups found in 1957 in the cave of the villa of Tiberio, over 15,000 fragments of marble with episodes of Ulysses: the Palladio Rat, the Pasquino group, Scilla and the Blind of Polyphemus, from which comes the famous head of Ulysses who named the Ulysses Riviera. Closed on Monday.

Oratorio eighteenth-century on the old road between Miasino and Ameno, with a small porch reached by stairs; it is part of a circular devotional itinerary with three chapels. At the bottom of the aisle, wooden altar and a painting attributed to the Morazzone.

Borgo della Valceresio surrounded by mountains and hills, a stone's throw from Lake Ceresio, known for Villa Cicogna Mozzoni, one of the most famous villas of delight in Lombardy; in the village the church of San Giuseppe, considered the oldest building, and the parish church of San Giorgio.
One of the ancient gates of the village.
Flaminio market.
The cloister with the stories of Saint Benedict, in silence.
The wooden baroque reborn after the landslide.
Mills and sweaters coming back to the streets.

Teaching exhibition in three rooms of the Museo della Terra di Venzone, born in Udine in 1986-87 from the Friulano Museum of Natural History: models and dioramas on forest ecosystems, fauna and the uses of trees, over 300 models of mushrooms and a section on the forest in myth. Open on Saturday 14-18 and, from May to October, Sundays and holidays 14-18; other days by reservation.
Romanesque abbeys and a 14th century castle.
A couple of kilometers from the village, ruins of a strategic fortress, probably belonged to the ancient Peligni, on a cliff near the springs of Sangro; from the site you can enjoy a beautiful view.

Path through the woods above the cycle path and the hamlets of Roda and Bosin, between dry walls covered with moss, ferns, strawberries and wild raspberries and small streams that cross the path. The point of return is the Rio Sadole, which is born at the foot of Mount Cauriol; among the trees open glimpses of Ziano.
The promenade of the city and the old port that leads to the Fort of Santa Tecla; the marina is Portosole.

On the hill of the same name (223 m) about two miles from the centre, founded in the first decades of the seventeenth century by the Camaldolese of Monte Corona and completed in 1627; the church of the Savior was rebuilt in 1741 by Gian Francesco Buonamici. Cristina stayed there in 1657.
The sanctuary with 360 degree views.
Church to the north of the village, outside the walls, dating back to about the year 1000, which replaced an older church in San Donato Vecchio, near Mount Bolzano.
The Jewish Bari.

The remains of the ancient city near San Vittorino, with the Roman theatre and amphitheatre; recent excavations have revealed tombs and buildings of the VII century BC near the church of San Vittorino. Managed by the National Museum of Abruzzo.
Memory of the first great siege of the fortress.

The smallest town in South Tyrol, in the upper Val Venosta, preserves intact the sixteenth-century walls with three tower-doors, rebuilt at the behest of Massimiliano I after the battle of Calva in 1499: inside, the street of the porticos of the market of 1291 and the Renaissance residences; outside the walls, the parish church of San Pancrazio and the church of San Giacomo in Söles.
Romanesque church of the fourteenth century.
The ruins of the monastery of manuscripts.

Medieval village of the Barbagia di Seulo, over 700 meters on the plateau of on Taccu and among the most beautiful villages in Italy, born around 1335 around the church of San Valentino: the waterfall in the center of the village, the seventeenth-century mill, the museum house of Aunt Cramella, the caves Is Janas and, on the border with Seulo, Su Stampu de su Turrunu.
The village of masks between murals and shops.
The lion attributed to Michelangelo.

Built between the 13th and 16th centuries, with three naves divided by octagonal pillars, with façade in stone from the end of the 16th century with carved frame and sundial; the vault is entirely covered with stuccoes, the Baroque pulpit was decorated by Abruzzo carvers and the bell tower is the second highest in the valley after that of the Annunziata di Sulmona.

About 12 hectares with 80 botanical environments in four thematic areas; in the castle, where Empress Elizabeth stayed between 1870 and 1889, the Touriseum, the first museum of the Alpine arch dedicated to the history of tourism.
The sanctuary on the cliff overlooking the valley.

Built between 1700 and 1736 and dedicated to the patron, it preserves many works: two curtains with the effigy of San Pantaleone by the master Vito Formisano, San Pantaleone that heals the blind ... by Giuseppe De Mattia, the conversion of San Pantaleone by the Salerno Stefano Trapanese and an ampolla with the blood of the saint.

The lakes of Bracciano and Martignano occupy the basin of the Sabatino volcano extinguished and form a regional natural park out of ten municipalities; in the waters of pikes, tenches, koregoni, perch and eels, among the birds folague, ducks, flares and raptors as brown and buzzard nibble. You can practice sailing, canoeing, hiking, horse riding and sport fishing, with beaches and sports clubs on the shores.

City in the middle of the Bergamo plain, home of tenor Giovan Battista Rubini, with the medieval old town, the Visconti fortress with four towers and the museum in the neoclassical palace of the singer.
The most famous canyon of the Sibillini.
Swamps and dunes between Porto Cesareo and Punta Prosciutto.
Sacred caves and views to the Gulf of Policastro.
The historic cemetery of the city, where Giovanni Verga has been resting for a century under a simple marble slab.
The Italian realism of the post-war period in the prize paid in kind.
The most photographed square, day and evening.
Exhibitions and concerts in the village.

Valsugana's thermal resort, the European aristocracy's destination between the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, with arsenal-ferruginous waters of Levico and Vetriolo and the Habsburg Park, the largest historical garden in the province; the lake, Blue Flag, is just a few minutes walk from the centre, while on the hills are the Austro-Hungarian fort of the Benne, the frescoed church of San Biagio and the ruins of Castel Selva.

Founded in the fourteenth century by the Confraternita dei Battuti, with the portal of 1510 of Pilacorte, the side door of 1555 with San Rocco, fourteenth-century frescoes and the wooden Crucifix that gives it its name.
Founded in the seventeenth century by the Knights of Malta, with the dome covered with Caltagirone ceramics.
A quiet village between Baldo and Garda.
Built in 1568 by the Marquis of Brienza Giambattista Caracciolo with castle material, it has a diamond-pointed bug portal with the inscription of 1568; in 1826 carbon meetings were held.
Legends and woods on the traces of the charcoal trees.
The house of the father of Verism in the heart of the historic center, with original interiors and the rich private library, a stone's throw from the ancient theatre and Via Crociferi.
Walk between nature and travertine.

Municipality of Valle Orco 62 km from Turin, one of the largest in Italy (13,274 hectares, almost one hundred hamlets), which rises from 539 meters of the valley floor to 3,692 of the Torre del Gran San Pietro; to the north the Vallone di Piantonetto is part of the Gran Paradiso National Park. In the capital is the 17th-century parish church of San Pietro in Vincoli, the sanctuary of the Madonna del Cantellino and the Park visitor centre dedicated to chimney sweeps.
The oil of the village, told in an old mill.
Oratory built in 1544 and linked to the Confraternity of the Body and Blood of Christ.
The fortress of the Borgia.

A huge accumulation of boulders of an ancient landslide creates caves and niches so cold that ice is formed even in the middle of summer; for this reason, about 500 meters grow plants typical of 1500 meters. You can walk from Rottenburg Square in about 2 hours (mark 15A and 15) or with a ring of about 4 hours from San Nicolò.
The village of pastel houses.
The history of the village, from the Messapi to the Renaissance, in a single museum.

Borgo on the hills of Oltrepò Pavese dominated by a castle of the sixteenth century, one of the best preserved in the area; just outside, the view of the Costa del Vento offers a 360 degree view of the hills.
identified with the Ethnographic Museum Vallivo della Valmasino by name and ethnographic section, to be confirmed
In Travagola, built on the ruins of a medieval castle after, from 1420, Venice ordered its demolition; it preserves the altarpiece of the Belluno painter Francesco Frigimelica
No (Guided Foundation Walks on Calendar)
Nature and a medieval aqueduct.

It was mentioned already in a diploma of Charlemagne of 792 and consecrated in 1248, revealed with the excavations of 1980-81 a cistern before the fifth century, a furnace for the bronze of the sixth and the phases of the church from the early medieval hall to the Romanesque building of the XII-XIII centuries. The current layout, with a Latin cross with a single nave, dates back to 1871-1883, with pentagonal bell tower renovated in the sixteenth century and a southern Gothic portal with carved architraves (bue, eagle, sun and moon). Inside, a chapel with Stories of the Virgin frescoed at the end of the fourteenth century by a painter from Friuli, paintings by G.B. Grassi dedicated to San Lorenzo and remains of a wooden ancon of 1558.
The daily life of a mountain country in a house of the seventeenth century.

The center preserves architectural remains of the sixteenth century and the gates of the walls (Porta di Lecce, Porta di Gallipoli, Porta Falsa). Among the palaces: Palazzo D'Alfonso in Piazza Umberto I, with two-faced portal and fresco "La Primavera" by Agesilao Flora; Palazzo Ramis with the sixteenth-century high relief of Annunciation and Deposition; the Palazzo dei Veneziani with the icon of San Marco; the Rua Chiesa Madre with the external fresco of the Crucifixion; Palazzo Ardito with baroque masks.
The Greek city under the feet.
Where Luigi Galvani did his experiments in 1787-88.
Noli's towers.

Parish church built since 1873 extending an ancient circular stone chapel with bell tower, perhaps part of the castle, partly on the area of the old cemetery; in Byzantine style, it is decorated by the Perugians Francesco Biscarini and Raffaele Angeletti, with three terracotta altars and a pipe organ of Nicomede Agati di Pistoia.
Snorkeling among the granites under a Spanish tower.
An artist of the twentieth century in the Baroque church he chose.
Black stone and frescoes in the churches of the village.

Museum diffused in the center of the village starting from the suspended olive tree: a specimen of Seggian olive tree with its roots hung in the ancient water tank, nourished by water vapor and nebulized nutrients, presented as the largest plant in the world supported with aeroponic technique, a project born with the neurobiologist Stefano Mancuso. The heart is the ancient oil mill and orciaia, with tasting of the oil Seggiano DOP.
The Morenic Amphitheatre from above, a stone's throw from the village.
Maratti in his hometown.
The medieval village of Monteleone, Orange Flag, leaning against the fortress, and the small fortified village of Sorrivoli around the Malatesta fortress.
An eighteenth-century church with Baroque details, a landmark of the community of the country.
The Giotteschi frescoes of the Hat.
The signal tower.

Cathedral of the sixteenth century in Catalan Gothic style, overlooking the sea, with bell tower covered with majolica. The retablo is attributed to the Master of Castelsardo, active before 1492; the eighteenth-century altars are carved in juniper wood. In the crypts is the museum dedicated to the Master of Castelsardo.

A small town on the edge of the Pollino National Park, known for its peperone di Senise; next to the village the Senise dam forms the lake of Monte Cotugno, the largest artificial lake on clay in Europe. In the historic centre, next to the Mother Church, the Ethnographic Museum tells about the peasant civilization of the Senese.
Walk on the original base of Queen Viarum.
A theatre in an ancient church.
The artists' square.
Above Crosa, the 3.5-metre-high mill and stone cross placed in 1664 by Capuchin friars returning from the Holy Land, visible from all over Verezzi.

It is located in the Franciscan monastery founded at the beginning of the 13th century, among the first made with Saint Francis still alive. Renovated, it houses a documentation centre on the Middle Ages in Gallura and exhibits the ex-vote to the Madonna bambina.
The largest fortified structure in Europe: three strong, three small and two batteries connected by a covered staircase of about 4000 steps in a gallery of almost two kilometers; inside two museums.
The village of surgeons between castle and viewpoint.

Small museum in several sections: wood, stone and glass sculptures of local artists and craftsmen; modern with the first computers, typewriters, projectors, telephones and a Lambretta; the peasant civilization with a nineteenth century bedroom; local stories and folklore, with an old organ, a crucifix of 1930, war relics and straw panels linked to the Giglio of August; a small picture gallery. No reservation; phone 0825 826015.
Art Nouveau itinerary in the center, from Casa Piontelli to the former Fiat garage in via Solferino.
The navy sentinel.

The wooded hill of porphyry in the village, with the ruins of the destroyed castle that gave the name to Castelrotto: a path of about 20 minutes from the center climbs between the rocks with seven chapels of the Calvary of the late seventeenth century (mountain of Olives, flagellation, coronation of thorns, burial) to a tower; at the top view on the roofs, the bell tower, the tip of Santner and the Sciliar. There are also a recreation area and a playground.

The remains of ancient Egnazia, excavated from 1912, include Messapian walls and necropolis, the Via Traiana, the Civil Basilica with the Sala delle Tre Grazie, the Sacellus of the Eastern Gods, the cryptoporic, the thermal baths and the Christian basilicas of the IV-VI centuries. The museum, built in 1975 and named after the Superintendent Giuseppe Andreassi, tells in ten rooms the Messapian, Roman, Late Antique and Medieval era, with the marble head of Attis and the mosaic of the Three Graces. Open every day 8:30-19:30.

Collection ranging from the great cetaceans of the Mediterranean, such as sperm whale, whale and dolphin, to sea turtles, shells, fossils and fishing instruments; on the upper floor an area for the care and recovery of sea turtles.

Common at the gates of Varese, between the Romanesque church of San Pietro in Silvis, already parish church of the village, the eighteenth-century church of the Santi Re Magi along Via Olona and Monte Monarco, a short panoramic ascent on the lakes of Varesotto.
The Canavesio polyptych.

Opened in 1996 at the will of Ludovico Corrao and today run by the Orestiadi Foundation, it occupies the former rural lighthouse Di Stefano. It brings together objects of use, costumes, writings, ceramics, fabrics, sculptures and contemporary installations from Sicily, Tunisia, Morocco, Palestine, Egypt, Spain and Albania, with works by Accardi, Dorazio, Turcato, Consagra, Schifano, Boetti, Isgrò and Beuys; outside the 'Montagna di sale' by Mimmo Paladino, created for the Orestiadi of 1990. He received an ICOM prize for cultural mediation. Open from Tuesday to Sunday 9-13 and 15-18, Monday closed.
Once Piazza San Martino, you can reach Corso Vittorio Emanuele and is dominated by the Collegiate Church of San Martino, with the University Palace and next to the Civic Tower.
The mosaics under the bell tower.

Palazzo Pinto, designed in 1897 for Francesco Pinto on Piazza Leonardo Netti and purchased by the Municipality in 1958, is now Palazzo della Cultura with Library and Historical Archives. The Monument to the Fallen, the work of sculptor Antonio Bassi, was inaugurated on May 24, 1937 in the square in front of Palazzo Gentile. Casa Larocca, municipal seat since 1860, now houses the tourist infopoint.
The seventeenth-century churches of the country.
A fire red landscape created by the mines.
Protected area of over 1,000 hectares among Mediterranean maquis, brooms, oaks and cork, inhabited by wild boars, foxes and weavers; there passes the historical path of the Leopold Aqueduct.

Rebuilt between 1725 and 1792 on a Romanesque building, with the contribution of Sottis, Plantery, Vittone (which is attributed to the elliptical dome) and Dellala; the medieval bell tower was long also civic tower. It contains nineteenth-century frescoes by Gabriele Ferrero, a Madonna del Rosario from the early seventeenth century attributed to Moncalvo or daughter Orsola, a wooden crucifix considered by Carlo Giuseppe Plura, a baptismal font with two sixteenth-century tanks and the organ of 1868. Here he was baptized San Domenico Savio on April 2, 1842.

Inside the walls from the middle of the fourteenth century, a facade with a shack with a horned rose window and a Latin cross plan; it preserves a table with Christ crucified between the Saints Rocco and Jerome.
The Loan of fishermen and sailors.
The Pilacorte portal.
For the eighteenth-century paintings rediscovered.

The first literary bench in Liguria, dedicated to the writer Francesco Biamonti: it is made of stone, is located in the courtyard of the town hall and has been decorated by two artists with images of landscapes and phrases in Ligurian dialect.
The fifteenth-century judgment and the hair bridge.
In the deconsecrated church of Sant'Elisabetta, a collection of gramophones, radios and apparatus to listen to and reproduce the sound from the nineteenth century to today.

Opened in 1774 and expanded in 1890 (re-opened with the Verdi Finder), reopened in 2003 after the restorations: 375 seats with U stage, two rows of stages and gallery; season of prose, opera, dance and dialect theatre.

The manorist palace-villa built between 1578 and 1585 by Santacroce, with a loggia with five arches; the project is traditionally attributed to Vignola, but the Ministry excludes it because it died in 1573. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the Altieri, with Carlo Fontana, added the northern wings with the courtyard, the clock tower, the entrance with basalt bridge and the fountain of the square. The rooms have stuccoes and frescoes with landscapes and fairy tales of Esopo; the Galleria Altieri, initiated by Cardinal Paluzzo Altieri, exhibits about 240 portraits of all the Popes from St. Peter to Francis, the only complete collection of the genre, with copies from Raffaello, Tiziano and Caravaggio. In the garden a rate of over 100 years. Open Tuesday-Sunday 8.30-19.30 (ticket office until 6.30 p.m.), closed on Monday.
Posillipo's postcard.
In the village are distilled liqueurs with volcanic herbs, which can be bought at the distillery of the Russian Brothers, reported by italia.it on the itinerary between Etna and Taormina.
The oldest memories in the country.
A church with a trullo roof.
Put your hand in the Mouth.

Inaugurated in 1934 and re-arranged in 1983 in the former choir of the church of Santa Maria del Suffragio: documents, weapons, flags, photographs and relics from the battle of Castiglione (1796) to the Risorgimento and the world wars, including a bolt of the engine of the plane of Francesco Baracca. Open only on Sunday afternoon from April to early October.
Remains of a villa of Roman age, recorded among the archaeological areas of the city by the University of Padua.

The fifteenth-century palace on Piazza Matteotti: on the first floor the collection of Marche engravers from 1550 to today, on the second the Civic Art Collection, about thirty works including three tables by Pietro Paolo Agabiti and two paintings by Giovan Battista Salvi called the Sassoferrato (1609-1685).
from €10
Medieval village of the Val di Cornia surrounded by walls, among cork woods that give it its name; City of Wine, Oil and Slow Food.
The stories of San Rocco in a church of the fifteenth century.
A Roman house under the historic center.

Ancient Saracen tower, 13 metres high, probably erected against pirates, for centuries the tallest building in Lavagna; restored for the Jubilee of 2000, in a garden in the historic center, hosts cultural events, the slate works of the sculptor Francesco Dallorso and the archaeological collection Rodolfo Alloisio with Tuscan ceramics and Ligurian majolica. In the summer open Thursday-Saturday 20:30-22:30.
The fountains of the center.

The agricultural landscape of drywalls.

Church of the 11th century with three naves leading to the presbytery, where the Norman ciborium is preserved carved in the 12th century by Roberto di Ruggero, the oldest in Abruzzo.
A small village theatre.

Crateric lake at the bottom of an ancient volcano active up to 30,000 years ago, surrounded by reeds and greenhouses of strawberries, in the Park of the Roman Castles suitable for excursions, trekking and mountain biking.
About 3 km walk from Mergellina to via Nazario Sauro, with Vesuvio, Castel dell'Ovo, Capri and Posillipo in front of the eyes.
The Roman Locri.
On the course near Ponte Vecchio, built in the fifteenth century and rebuilt in the nineteenth century, with paintings by Emilio Scherer.
The history of copper that made Isili famous.

It preserves the image of Our Lady of the Flood of Graces, an unknown author; the gold crowns, stolen in 1867, were made with donations from the citizens, and Mgr. Giovannetti tells you a miracle during the plague of 1656.

The white DOC Colli Albani, also superior sparkling wine, the ancient Albano praised by Orazio and loved by the artists of the Grand Tour; in the kitchen the roman broccoli (capoccione) is attuned, cooked in wine.
A green walk a few steps from the sea.
Romanesque church in Piazza Garibaldi with its particular façade, with the sixteenth-century urn of the Sienese school of Blessed Bonizzella Cacciaconti.

Small village on a high hill of just over 100 meters, with name that goes back to an Etruscan family and walls preserved by the role of control in the Middle Ages; the small Romanesque church of San Niccolò holds an important wooden crucifix and from there opens the panorama on the Valdinievole. In autumn there is the Castagnata.

Baroque church with seventeenth-century façade and bell tower in front of 1751, enlarged after a pastoral visit of 1584 judged it too small. It preserves an organ restored in 1762 surmounted by the wooden statue of San Romano del Seicento, the choir benches and an altar of the stoning of Santo Stefano.
Fortified village of the early sixteenth century around a thirteenth-century tower, with terrace garden on the Tyrrhenian Sea; open especially for events.
An easy walk in the shade.
The 19th century theatre inside the Fortress.

On the island at the eastern end of the lagoon, guarded by Franciscan Friars Minor: according to tradition in 582, the patriarch Elijah had it built a first church after the discovery of an image of Our Lady brought by the waters. From 1237 it is the destination of the Perdòn, procession of boats of the first Sunday of July. Line boat in about 25 minutes.
An abbey in the Fermana countryside.
A small oratory of medieval origin in the countryside.

An asphalted track of about 23 km from Zogno to Piazza Brembana along the Brembo and the track of the old abandoned railway, with many tunnels and a maximum altitude difference of 230 meters, suitable for those with little experience. Tocca San Pellegrino Terme, where it runs for short stretches on ordinary road, San Giovanni Bianco and the village of Cornello dei Tasso; on summer Sundays it is very frequented.
Canova's atelier.
The church in the fortified heart of the village, with the Renaissance portal.
The sacristies inlaid among the richest in Lombardy, with Tintoretto and Palma the Elder.
The oldest street in the city, which once led to the sixteenth-century castle of which the Guevara Tower remains.
The Riace Bronzes.

Sanctuary of Our Lady of the Snow and the Emigrant, with documented origins in 1484 and altar rebuilt in 1778-1779; it houses 68 bronze plates with the names of migrants dead at work, a Madonna with the Child and altars with St. Sebastian and the Visitation. Outside, two monuments of the sculptor Jacques Peraducto and the façade painted in 2004 by Costanza Maria Tibaldeschi; feast on the first Sunday of August.
An oratory of unbroken fraternity.
Medieval churches over Nuragic monuments.
The farmhouses scattered between the hill and the villa.
The dome that refers to Brunelleschi.
A fern of the Tertiary era.
At the summit, about 800 meters away, the church of San Gavino upstream, where it is celebrated on May 1st; the mountain has twenty routes nailed and is frequented for climbing and paragliding.
The San Sebastiano attributed to Mattia Preti.

At the highest point of the country; the first fortification, before the Thousand, was of the Roman prince and senator Alberico. The columns, lords from the fifteenth century, the walls with circular towers and Alessandro and Sciarra Colonna transformed it into a Renaissance palace. It preserves frescoed rooms, ancient prisons, a small medieval church and the Sala Pinta, frescoed by Federico Zuccari with the foundation of Rome, Roman legends, battles and the possessions of the Colonna.
The designer of ... Die Zeit in his town.

A Franciscan monastery has been built on the Dosso di Lavedo since the 13th century, transformed at the end of the 18th century by Cardinal Angelo Maria Durini into a literary retreat with the Panoramic Loggia. After several families, in 1974 it was bought by explorer Guido Monzino, the first Italian on Everest, who left it at FAI (1988). You can visit interiors with 18th century French furnishings, tapestries from Beauvais and extra-European art, the Museum of Shipments with the North Pole sleigh 1971 and the garden with topiary prunings and terraces on the lake.
Ruins of a medieval house near the Trinity hamlet, considered the symbol of the municipality.

Late medieval church (XV-XVI century) that houses the relics of the saints owners, remodelled in baroque forms in the Six and eighteenth centuries and brought back in 1933 to the original appearance by eliminating the baroque additions. The hut façade has horizontal bands white and black, rosette and pinnacles in terracotta; inside marble panels, golden mosaics and frescoes in Gothic style between neo-Gothic and neo-Romanesque. The baroque altar of purging souls remains, two fifteenth-century wooden statues of the patrons on the sides of a great Crucifix co-eval and the high altar surmounted by silver saints and bishops.
One of the quietest villages in the valley.
The venue of exhibitions of design and architecture, among the attractions of the city.

Founded in 1964 by pharmacist Gianfranco Gioitti with Livio Poldini and Stanislao Budin and opened to the public since 1978, it occupies a karst dolina of 5,000 square meters where 15 environments of the Karst are rebuilt to collect and illustrate the spontaneous flora; there were recorded 77 species of butterflies. Managed by the Region through the Rogos Cooperative.
A 14th century Celestinian monastery.
Temporary exhibitions in downtown.

The highest lighthouse in the Mediterranean, the second in Europe and the third oldest among those still active; at the base, in the fortifications, the museum and an urban park, with ascent to the first terrace.

Called "Oriental" because near the ancient east gate of the city, inaugurated in 1899 in the space of the cloister of the convent of N.S. of the Consolation; on the raised floor the MOG with traditional cuisine. An entrance is on Via XX Settembre.

At about 8 km from the village and 900 meters above sea level, cited in a document dated 1581 as "Ecclesiam Sancti Angeli" (Ecclesiam Sancti Angeli), a place of worship of St. Michael linked to a nearby spring and to the stillicide in the cave; the excavations returned flints, ceramics of the Bronze Age and traces of hermits and shepherds.
Enotri, Greci and Lucani.

Center on the first hills west of the Piana di Catania, 270 meters, founded by the Marquis Ottavio Gravina to welcome those who had lost their home with the earthquake of 1693 and the flows of Etna; on the central square the Mother Church of the Nativity of Mary with the seventeenth-century bell tower, not far away the church of the Immaculate which houses the parish of the patron Saint Joseph (March 19).

On over 40 hectares at the foot of the hill, the city was born as a small Lucan center in the third century BC, crossed by Hannibal in the second Punic war, rebuilt Roman colony in the middle of the first century BC and became the main center of southern Lucania. Theatre, italic temple, domus with mosaics, hole with Capitolium, Augusteum, basilica, curia and thermal baths, Major Baths with mosaics and marbles, the first cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta and one of the oldest masonry amphitheaters known.

Centre of the Lanzo Valleys and terminus of the Turin-Ceres railway: in the Town Hall square the Museum of the Lanzo Valleys, then the eighteenth-century parish church of the Assumption, the donkey-back bridge of the Vana (1740), the station of 1915 and, in the village Voragno, the Chapel of the Holy Shroud with probably sixteenth-century frescoes.

An easy ring of about 3 hours and 250 m of difference in altitude, proposed by the Park with meeting in Borgo Povici di Sotto: touches Borgo Cros, village abandoned after the earthquake of 1976 with houses then renovated in respect of the original characteristics, and continues on catwalks, mule tracks and grassy hills; on the return you will meet the large gravel beehive of Rio Putto, the Rio Serai and the Resartico stream.

The Sardinian Athens by Grazia Deledda, Sebastiano Satta and Francesco Ciusa: the birthplace of the writer, the MAN, the Museo Ciusa al Tribu, the Ethnographic Museum Sardo, the Archaeological Museum Asproni and Mount Ortobene with the statue of the Redeemer.
The majolica floor.
A tradition to see with children.
A Romanesque sanctuary overlooking the wildest part of the Nero.

The glass village of Val Bormida: the first furnaces date back to the 11th century and the Statuti of the University of Glass in 1495; today the tradition lives in the Museum of Altar Art of Villa Rosa, in the glass shops and in the churches of the medieval village, with the 17th century parish church of Sant'Eugenius.

Opened on 23 January 2000 in the local limestone building designed by Pietro Favia, it is named after Franco Anelli (1899-1977), discoverer and spreader of the caves. It exhibits fossils, minerals, concretions and historical evidences, with the 3D reconstruction of three caves; it offers guided tours, educational workshops and speleotouristic visits in the side branches of the caves. You visit after the cave tour.

Porta del Casentino for those arriving from Arezzo, on the left bank of the Arno at the foot of the Alpe di Catenaia: the castle built before the 1000 at the control of the river, the thirteenth-century church of Santa Maria della Visitazione with the Documentation Centre of Archaeological Culture, and in the surroundings the neo-medieval castle of Valenzano and that of the Fioraia in Castelnuovo.

A fauna park of about five hectares with a three-kilometre route, divided between the Farm (domestic animals and ancient breeds such as the Pisa cow and the Amiatino donkey) and the Zoo for geographical areas, with over 150 species and a small museum of vintage photos and agricultural tools.

The ancient Venusia, a Latin colony from 291 B.C. and home of Orazio, in the Vulture: the Abbey of the Holy Trinity with the Unfinished of Normans, the castle of Pirro del Balzo with the archaeological museum and the Palaeolithic park of Notarchiricus.
Sailing and canoeing in the crater.
Ruins of a 15th century castle belonged to the lords of Baschi, of which remains sections of the walls.

In a hydraulic tollgate of the early twentieth century overlooking the Padule di Scarlino: amphorae, ceramics and objects fallen into the sea during the loading and unloading of the ships, recovered in diving excavations of 2000-2001 in the ancient commercial port, in the rada of Portiglioni; it also tells the work of underwater archaeologists with instruments, techniques and reconstructions. Open every day 10-13 and 16-19 according to the card of italia.it.
From the top you can see up to San Marino and the Adriatic.

Cities 23 km from Rome, built around Palazzo Orsini Barberini, fortress of the Orsini of the 13th century transformed by the Barberinis into a ducal residence, today the town hall and seat of the Archaeological and Multimedia Museum; in the center the Cathedral of Santa Maria Maddalena, Porta Garibaldi, which recalls the taking of the city by Garibaldi on 26 October 1867, and Piazza del Popolo with the Fountain of the Lions; around, the reserves of Macchia di Gattaceca and Macchia del Barco and, in November, the Fasti d'Autunno.
The carved altar of Ferdinand Moscow.

San Salvatore is recognizable for the high Romanesque bell tower and preserves the great fresco of the  "Pietà" with Saints attributed to Piermatteo d'Amelia; to the same Renaissance painter is attributed the "Madonna on throne" with Child in the chapel of San Lanno, dedicated to the patron saint of the village.

Gallery of the Via Flaminia excavated in chisel and pick in limestone at the will of Vespasiano, completed in 76 A.D. next to a more ancient passage, at the narrowest point of the gorge (the . ........................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................ Approximately 38 metres long, 5,47 metres wide and about 6 metres high, it retains on the walls the signs of the Roman tools and an inscription at the north-east entrance that reminds of their construction; it is still accessible by pedestrians and vehicles. The small gallery, from the first half of the first century AD, is seen from the street and can be visited with guided tour.

Borgo delle Madonie dominated by the Castello dei Ventimiglia, with the fourteenth-century Torre dei Ventimiglia becoming a bell tower, the Mother Church with the Last Judgment of Giuseppe Salerno, the eighteenth-century Palazzo Bongiorno and the four museums of Palazzo Sgadari.
Park near the river Isonzo.
The memory of the Winter Line.

A limestone-granite relief, 560 metres high and about 4 km long, in the territory of Olbia, called the smallest kingdom in the world. According to the tradition, Carlo Alberto made its inhabitants Giuseppe Bertoleoni, whose descendants are still the only residents. It arrives at Spalmatore di terra, with marina and refreshment points; every July it hosts the film festival "One night in Italy." It gives the name to the marine protected area Tavolara-Punta Coda Cavallo, suitable for boat excursions, diving and snorkeling.
A walk to the sanctuary.
The historic park of the city, with pond and large trees, close to the center.
Six thousand years of history on one hill.

Established in 1990, 11,200 hectares entirely in the municipality of Cortina, it is owned and managed by the Regole d'Ampezzo and includes the groups of Crystal, Tofane and Lagazuoi; it is part of the System 5 (northern Dolomites) of the UNESCO site and has as symbol the Sempervivum dolomiticum, plant present only in the Dolomites of Ampezzo. It offers eight via ferrate, six other equipped routes, eleven shelters and in winter seven km of cross-country trails.
A Roman port still in use, beautiful at sunset.

museum and archaeological area of Santa Restituta closed for the redevelopment project (July 2025); finds transferred to Villa Arbusto; available a virtual tour at the tower info point

Cittadina dell'Alto Garda among the olive trees, with a mild climate that made it a place of care and today the world capital of sport climbing: the castle of the counts of Arc with the fourteenth-century frescoes of courteous life, the Civic Gallery dedicated to Giovanni Segantini, born here in 1858, the Arboreto of the Archducale Park and the fifteenth-century sanctuary of the Madonna delle Grazie.

Castle-country of the Valnerina on a hill, with the walls and fortified thirteenth century, houses in clear stone joined by passages and arches, churches frescoed by Cola di Pietro and Jacopo Siculo and the Casa dei Racconti dedicated to oral narration; in June the festival of cheese Fior di Cacio.
In the south-east wing of the castle, he collects trophies and relics on the life and career of Achille Varzi, born in Galliate. Open on Sunday afternoons from 3:30 pm.
Completed in the 15th century, it preserves the frescoes of Bonifacio Bembo in the Chapel Cavalcabò and the altarpiece of Perugino in 1494.

In the basement of Palazzo Mercuri reconstructs the workshops of the ancient crafts: ropemaker, blacksmith, print on fabric, with attention to ebony, wrought iron and goldsmithery.

The only fortified settlement of the Teutonic Order still existing in the Mediterranean area, born from the command created between 1226 and 1231 on lands donated by Frederick II: the 24-metre tower, of the 13th-XIV century, incorporates the choir of a pre-existing church with remains of a cycle of frescoes of the late thirteenth century (saints, Passion, Lignum vitae) and graffiti in German. The complex includes the Palazzo dell'Abate of 1570, the eighteenth-century loggia and the sixteenth-century church; since 2016 there has been a museum with mainly Renaissance ceramics and archaeological finds.

Birthplace of Giuseppe Maria Galanti (1743-1806), economist and historian illuminist, with environments, gardens and cellars.
The residence chosen by the Prince Sabaudo.
The Venetian Renaissance walls, about 11 kilometers long with 19 bastions and 6 surviving doors, to walk on a walk around the city.
A stone stable of 91 meters in altitude.

The Piazza del Duomo with the Preda Ringadora; in the Palazzo Comunale you can visit the historical halls, the abducted bucket and the municipal vinegar mill.

Phoenician walls of the 8th - 7th century BC in front of the Mother Church.

Borgo at 856 meters on the Rhaetian side of the Valtellina, Slow Town and home of the Pizzoccheri, which according to tradition gave the name to the valley; in the center the Renaissance Palazzo Besta, the only state museum in the province of Sondrio, the tower      Âde li beli miri Â Â and a sacred enclosure with the church of Sant'Eufemia and the Romanesque San Pietro.

On the main square, baroqued by Donato Sarnicola in 1732, with neoclassical façade of 1844 and dome (1794) and bell tower (1817) covered with polychrome majolica in 1862. It preserves the polyptych of Bartolomeo Vivarini painted in Murano in 1477 (25 figures of saints, since 1995 in the chapel of San Silvestro), the Madonna of the Angels by Antonello Gagini (1505), the pulpit of 1792 by Agostino Fusco and two angels attributed to Pietro Bernini or one of his students.
A Renaissance triptych in a country oratory.

A stone village over 700 metres at the foot of Monte Scalambra, overlooking the Sacco valley, on the Via Francigena del Nord; it houses the permanent exposition of theatrical costumes by Beatrice Minori, the hermitage of St. Michael the Archangel in the rock and the churches of St. Quiricus and St. Peter the Apostle. At Christmas the alleys host the ethnographic nativity scene, from 8 December to 6 January.

The Benedictine complex of Santa Maria already existed around 540, when St. Silverius was buried there; in the thirteenth century the Cistercians sent by Innocent III settled there and in the fifteenth century the monastery was transferred to Formia. The church of St. Joseph was built in 1828 and consecrated in 1895.

Along the road between Collio and Memmo, started in the middle of the fifteenth century as a simple chapel and then enlarged: Romanesque church with sober architecture, with linear facade, rose window and portal in grey stone. It was declared a national monument in 1912, during World War I it was requisitioned and used as a stable for the horses of the artillery. Visits on request.

Building of the fourteenth century with ceilings and wooden beams and facade with two arched windows with stone posts, south of the tower-door of the ancient village of Torre Ratti. Since 30 October 2016, the Toy Museum has hosted 250 unique pieces of Pop Art inspiration made of recycled materials and donated by the painter Enrico Debenedetti. Visit by reservation.
The tour of the walls between doors and bastions.

After a landslide in 1965 the professor of science Don Antonio Canova found the first fossil, a fragment of fish; since 1970 the area has been protected and dug by the Civic Museum of Natural Sciences of Bergamo, which conserves thousands of fossils of the Triassic (about 220 million years ago): fish, crustaceans, molluscs, reptiles and plants. In 1973 there were found the remains of the Eudimorphodon ranzii, the oldest pterosaur in the world. Opened in 2002, it is a geosite of international importance: visitor center with multilingual panels, LIS and Braille supports, interactive stations and microscopes, naturalistic path to the fossiliferous site and simulated excavation area; free guided tours and workshops during the summer weekends (2026: 13 June-27 September, 14-19). Accessible to the disabled.

Frazione about 3 km from Bisegna, with ancient houses gathered around the church of San Sebastiano; in the area there are also the churches of the Madonna of Loreto and San Sebastiano to the river.

The holiday resort of the Monregalese Valleys since the end of the nineteenth century, at the foot of the Moro and Malanotte mountains: in Val Corsaglia the Grotta di Bossea, the first tourist cave of Italy, in the village the Ecomuseum of Marble with the Verzino used by Guarini for the Chapel of the Shroud, in Fontane the ethnographic museum Cesare Vinaj.

Ring of 6 km (about 2 hours, +192 m) of the path Walkbosco n. 1 starting from Piazza della Chiesa: for old mule tracks, reach the Coletta district (1113 m), the Biancari with an ancient six-arched portico, the Tander, Der, Lesi and Croce districts, between woods and a vajo.
