The new Cathedral of the city, dated 1606 and rebuilt in 1936.
A walk over the lake.

Born in 2004 in Ferrera, it documents the millennial history of the Moncenisio and Val Cenischia pass as a frontier land: via del sale, Via Francigena, Chemin de la Ramasse, Chemin des Marrons, Fell railroad, exile and Glorious Return of the Valdesi, mountain crafts and popular traditions. The route includes the documentation centre in the former after-work, an exhibition on work in the former mill, the old restored common oven and, at the entrance of the village, an outdoor exhibition on the Fell railroad that from 1866 to 1871 connected Susa to Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne. Opening hours 2026: from May to September Friday 14-19, Saturday and Sunday 10-18; from October to April Tuesday 10-12, Friday 14-19, Saturday 10-18.

Born from the vow of the priest Adam Morfino (1533) to found a hospital with chapel, it became parish in 1615 and was rebuilt between 1692 and 1705; the facade is of 1782. A Latin cross with three aisles and monolithic columns of red marble of Bonifato, has stuccoes of Vincenzo and Gabriele Messina of Serpotti's school, frescoes of Antonio Grano and paintings of Giuseppe Felice (1701-1703). It preserves the  "Madonna del Miele" (Madonna of Honey), painted in about 1300, the oldest of Alcamo, coming from the first mother church of Santa Maria della Stella.

In the hamlet of Segno, it dates back to the 10th century and was rebuilt in 1711 in Baroque forms; it retains an Annunciation attributed to the Cambiaso, the Baptism of Christ of Barabino, eighteenth-century statues of the Madonna del Rosario, St. Anthony of Padua and St. Maurizio and a wooden Crucifix attributed to Maragliano.
The Romanesque masterpiece of the Eastern Alps.
The baroque living room.

On the main square of the historic center, of medieval origin with bell tower of the fourteenth century and sixteenth-century forms, with three naves on pillars; it preserves two frescoes by Donato Palmieri, a major altar in marble of the eighteenth century and the dark chamber sundial inserted in the floor in 1796 on the model of that of Santa Maria degli Angeli in Rome.

Ancient feud of Montefeltro on a hill on the border between Marche and Umbria, along the Via Flaminia: Piazza Luceoli, the Collegiate Church of San Giovanni Battista, the archaeological museum in the former Augustinian monastery, the Good Friday Turb and the reserve of the Tecchie Wood at the foot of Catria.

Fortified village with a regular system with parallel blocks of the early sixteenth century. In the village the oratory of Sant'Antonio in Piazza Garibaldi (1696, project by Francesco Galli Bibiena), the church of the Blessed Virgin of Carmine founded in 1661 by Diofebo III Meli Lupi with Baroque altar, the church of San Giacomo (1755-1769) with organ of the brothers Serassi and the Park of the Remembrances of 1926.
The frescoed halls of the municipality.

On the Ionian coast, where the Greek colonies of Siris and Herakleia arose: the National Museum of Siritide with the archaeological park of the acropolis and the shrines, the castle on the hill of Heraclea, the reserve of the Pantano Wood and the beaches of Lido di Policoro.
€4, reduced €3
The vineyard on the hill of Vomero, one of the unusual places of Naples.
The Templar sanctuary on the hill.

Fortified villages on the ancient transhumance of Mount Coscerno, known for the churches with pictorial cycles in part attributed to Giovanni di Pietro known as Spain: Santa Cristina and Santa Maria delle Grazie a Caso, San Michele Arcangelo a Gavelli.
The Baroque jewel that closes the center.
The seventeenth-century wooden ancone of the high altar.

Gorge 12 km long and wide up to 500 meters, covered with vegetation. The Lipu Oasis, about 800 hectares on the southern edge of the village, has a panoramic point, a tour centre with diorama and educational paths; there live vaccaio, cricket, wolf, otter and istrice. From the viewpoint start path no. 2 (about 1 km downhill and uphill) and a challenging excursion of 7 km; in the gravina there are churches and rock crypts. Visits by reservation with the Oasis manager.
Trekking between Sardinian deer and eagles.
A closed agricultural village-court, with palace, church and park on the Orba.
The centre of medieval plant with the districts Capo d'Atri, Santa Maria and San Giovanni, where some alleys are so narrow that you pass one at a time.

Built in 1040 in the Byzantine period and rebuilt between the Five and the eighteenth century in Baroque style, it preserves the domes with trullo of concentric circles of tiles and the bell tower with cuspidate tower; inside, with a Latin cross with three naves, the Madonna of the Rosary of the late eighteenth century, a wooden St. Nicholas and a painting of the Trinity of the eighteenth century.
The ruins of the castle incorporated in the fabric of the village and the semicircle of the ancient walls, between stone houses and terracotta almost intact.
Country of the Amiata grown around its Benedictine abbey, one of the oldest and largest in Italy.
Unspoilt nature just a stone's throw from the village.
A 30 million-year-old fossil fish.
The Bear Cave, for experienced hikers.

The parish church was rebuilt in the second half of the eighteenth century on the project of the architect Giovanni Miazzi from Bassano and remained without facade until 1857. The front, designed by the Vicenza engineer Luigi Dalla Vecchia thanks to a legacy of Dr. Bortolo Barbieri and completed in 1858 (as the inscription above the portal recalls), has giant Corinthian pilgrims on high stands and a eardrum with tooth frame, cherubs and festoons; From the Old Age he also extended the church about six meters long and built the stairway. The three statues of the saints held on the pediment were placed in 1912-1913.

The tour of Lake Orta (39.6 km, on foot and by mountain bike, free access, departure from the Forum of Omegna) enters the municipality from the hamlet Pascolo and runs along the coast near Punta Casario, the fountain of San Giulio and the villas Guadagnini and Castelnuovo; after a dirt climb reaches Lagna and runs along the oratory of San Rocco. Along the stretch you will find the beaches of Pascolo and Prarolo, the port of Lagna and the Roman Bridge.
By bike in the countryside of Bassa.
The chapel on the path.
The oldest Benedictine monastery in the world.

Mother Church dedicated to the Immaculate Conception, celebrated on 8 December with a procession; not far from the town hall, overlooks the central square dedicated to Francesco Caligiuri. It houses a half-busted statue of St. Francis of Paola of the seventeenth century, donated by the Marquis Mottola with notary act of 1782. Main entrance to stairway, ramp to the secondary entrance.
A villa of Lombard delight with its village.

Re-opened with a new layout in the historical site of Via Cappuccini, it traces through the funerary furnishings the history of the town from the IX to the V-IV century BC, when the Greek and Magnogrec figurative ceramic appears in the tombs. Among the pieces exhibited are the cinerary urn of the tomb 14 (900-850 BC), the model of the hut of the tomb 63 of Sant'Antonio (850-75 BC) and a black figured attic lekythos of the collection Sabia (550 BC). Open Mon-Sat 9-13.
The village with the castle and the terracotta statue of Grandma Lucia, among the Supertuscan cellars.

In the upper part of the village, recently restored, with the ochre color shaded of white and grey that makes it visible also by Soriano Calabro. The portico with ionic columns and arches leads to a back courtyard with a view of the Upper Valley of the Messa and the Convent of San Domenico di Soriano. Inside a wooden crucifix with a full figure of the end of the sixteenth century, attributed to Müller, active also to the Certosa di Serra San Bruno.

A village of the Seriana Valley at the foot of Monte Bue, along the cycle path of Serio, known for the paleontological park where the Eudimorphodon ranzii, the oldest pterosaur in the world, was discovered; in the village the church of San Zenone, the medieval Torre del Mazzo and the nineteenth-century cotton mill Valty-Wildy.

Ancient medieval center on a hill between Majella and Adriatic, where on May 25, 1550 St. Camillo de Lellis, founder of the Camillians, was born: the birthplace and the shrine-convento he wanted are the main destinations, together with the church of Sant'Urbano, linked to the Festa dei Bandersi, the palaces of the center and the calanchi of the Ripe dello Spagnolo.
It keeps numerous processional statues of the eighteenth century of fine craftsmanship.
About 4 km from the centre of Quarazze along Monte Benedetto, between native and Mediterranean plants; the physician and botanist Franz Tappeiner wanted it in the Habsburg era.
On the hill that dominates the village stood the ancient medieval walled village; on the highlands Grand Duke Ferdinando I de' Medici had built a villa that still dominates them today.
The oldest church.

In the heart of the Alburni Mountains, inside the Cilento National Park, Vallo di Diano and Alburni, Corleto Monforte has been hosting since 1997 the Museo naturalistico degli Alburni, with over 1,300 vertebrates and 20,000 insects of European fauna, and just outside the village the Sanctuary of Maria SS.ma della Selice, overlooking the valleys of Fasanella and Calore.
The walled village overlooking the sea.
The point where Venice ended and Padua began.
A 16th century sawmill still in operation.
Municipality of Alta Val Varaita on the border with France, with the lake between the woods and the hamlet of Chianale, stone village at 1800 meters among the most beautiful villages in Italy.

Hiking trail (difficulty E) that climbs from Voltaggio (353 m) in about 2 hours and 30 minutes, with about 750 m of altitude difference, to the summit of Monte Tobbio (1,092 m): chestnut wood, clearing of the former Cascina Colletta, ridge of the Costa di Cravara with views of the Devil's pulpit, Passo della Dagliola. On top of a small chapel and a refuge always open; on clear days the view ranges from the lakes of the Gorzente to the Ligurian Sea, the Po Valley and the Alps.
The civic museum of rural civilization set up in the farmhouse Il Cambonino Vecchio, among the museums indicated by the tourist portal of Cremona.

The palace houses four museums: the Archaeological Museum with finds of the territory, the Pinacoteca Gianbecchina, the Museum of Arms and the Ethno-anthropological Museum with objects related to bread and pastoral care.
At the Palazzo del Monferrato, the cycling history of Alexandria from the 1867 speedy to the champions Fausto Coppi and Costante Girardengo.
The Sidicini civilization.
after the earthquake of 2016 the monuments are partially usable (Let's Marche); the card of the Park describes the state prior to the earthquake
The square was designed in the middle of the sixteenth century, porticoed on two sides, with the Duomo and the Bishop's Palace.
Molise village near Campobasso with the parish church of San Lorenzo Martire next to the former ducal palace and, on Mount Vairano towards Baranello, the walls of a city of the Sanniti Pentri.
The 14th century palace and its paintings.

The mountain of the legends of the giant Baranci: a chairlift climbs to the summit, where there are panoramic paths and for families, the ring path In winter easy slopes and one of the longest toboggan runs in South Tyrol.
One of the most important monuments of Basilicata.
The highest village, gathered around the sanctuary of the Blessed Virgin of the Graces of Valsorda; in Borgo Poggiolo the sources of San Bernardo.
Seeing the two baptisteries on the same day tells the two rival churches of the Ravenna Gota.
The village on the hills between Rubicone and Pisciatello dominated by the quadrilateral fortress of the Malatesta, restored in 2003: a balcony to the sea.

At 730 meters above sea level, it rises on the tomb of Blessed Rizzerio, born in Muccia and companion of Saint Francis, who left the noble origins to live as a hermit in a cave of the hills of Muccia. The church of San Giacomo Maggiore that kept its remains was demolished in 1948-49; the surgeon Cesare Lami found cave and tomb and rebuilt the church on the ancient foundations. The tower is a symbol of the vanity of material goods, and today it hosts theatres for events and tourist reception.
A workshop known for its goat cheese and homemade durum wheat bread, cooked with mother yeast in a straw oven dating back to 1526.

Exhibitive route in the castle, led by Antonio Adriano, which reconstructs the long-lasting history of the landscape of Langhe and Roero through documents and material and intangible knowledge, putting the peasants at the centre as protagonists.

Built by Duke Bonifacio Caetani in 1560 incorporating the medieval fortress of the Frangipane, on a project by Francesco da Volterra, he lost in the Second World War the oldest part with the rooms painted by Girolamo Siciolante, Stefano Dupérac and perhaps the Zuccari brothers. The Zuccari Room remains with the large fresco of the Caetani's pontoons in the eighteenth century, the trompe-l'oeil of the Loggia Room, the court porticoed with a Roman well and access to the Torre Frangipane, and under the building a network of caves about fifteen meters deep where at Christmas the crib is set up. It hosts exhibitions, concerts, the Cisterna Film Festival and the municipal library.

Maybe of origin from the 11th century, as chapel of the hospice of the monks of San Faustino, with the current architecture of the early eighteenth century; it preserves a altarpiece with the patron saint of Giuseppe Tortelli.
Monastery of 1,500 square meters that today hosts the Musical Academy of the Vallo di Diano.

The country dome, dedicated to the Conversion of St. Paul, is one of the most important sacred buildings in South Tyrol: the parish, one of the richest in the province since about 1147, built a church oversized in over 250 years, German late dogotics in the base and in the central and baroque Italian body in the onion dome. The bell tower 86 meters high has nine bells, including the second largest in South Tyrol (3.8 tons, merged from Grassmayr to Innsbruck); the interior is a three-nave hall church with a major altar and two side of Michael Stolz, noble coats of arms, busts of the apostles and a Madonna with the Child of the fifteenth century. Guided tour once a week and audio guide.
The majolica cloister.

Protected wetland of about 360 hectares at the southern edge of Lake Iseo, from which separates a thin morainic cordon, between the municipalities of Iseo, Provaglio d'Iseo and Corte Franca: swampy soils, reeds and water mirrors born where in the nineteenth century peat was extracted for the ironworks of Brescia. Known as a wetland of international importance, ZSC and ZPS, it hosts red herons, swamp hawks, brown and tarabous nibble, and fishes such as tinca, pike and royal perch. You can visit wood paths and walkways between the blades; three main entrances, one at Corte Franca, each with an automatic ticket; open daily. No bikes inside.
According to the legend built at the end of the thirteenth century in the place indicated by a dove; it is depicted in the astronomical clock and visible by Piazza Duomo.
A panoramic road to take calmly.
It tells the history of the 350 stazzi recorded in the territory, the typical rural settlements of Gallura that in the seventeenth century brought the village back to life.
The village overlooking the sea.
A Roman bridge next to the abbey.

A small town on the Bergamo shore of Lake Iseo, where the lake becomes the Oglio river, with one of the longest lakes in Sebino, the medieval centre of the Contrada, the Liberty villas by Giuseppe Sommaruga and the Gianni Bellini art gallery in Palazzo Gervasoni.

At the foot of the village, near the river Bagno, there are bicarbonate waters hypothermal alkalines at about 30 degrees, already praised by Andrea Bacci in 1571 as "Argenteae Aquae Sub Parrano Castro"; in the area there is a thermal pond in which to swim.
A Roman cellar as it was in 79 A.D.

The Baroque church next to the cathedral where every 23 September remembers the death of Bellini with a concert and where since April there is a musical season dedicated to the Italian opera tradition.
Founded at the end of the 11th century by Bishop Gerlando, in the Norman-Gothic style, with an unfinished fifteenth-century bell tower and the Treasury of the Cathedral.

Opened in 2014 in the center of Capoliveri, it is dedicated to the treasure of the ship Polluce, departed from Naples to Marseille and sunk off Capoliveri on the night of June 17, 1841 with a large load of coins; the wreck was found, looted and then recovered by the State. Organizes workshops, guided tours, conferences and walks
Medieval alleys and the viewpoint on Enna.
A place of popular rites still alive.
Waldensian history in the temple survived persecution.

A coastal town of the Cilento National Park, Vallo di Diano and Alburni, on the promontory fortified by the Byzantines who called it "Akropolis": the ancient village is reached by the steps and the Gate of Earth, on top the Angevin-Aragonese castle with views of the Gulf of Salerno; along the coast the towers of San Marco and San Francesco and the church of Santa Maria di Costantinopoli overlooking the sea.
The small Calabrian Petra, an entire village dug into the rock.
The two-faced stone crucifix.
Toscanini Island.

On the Karst plateaus between Umbria and Marche, the marsh of about 100 hectares with dense aquatic vegetation is recognized of international interest by the Ramsar Convention for peat bog, flora and birds.
The most famous natural mummies in Umbria.
A romantic shot on the Liri.

Country that gives its name to one of the three valleys of Lanzo, in a basin crossed by the Stura di Viù, with the parish church of San Martino, the largest of the valleys, and the Celtic Stone of the Mothers. From here you can climb to the Colle del Lys, towards the Val di Susa, home to a natural park and the Ecomuseum of the Resistance Carlo Mastri.

The town of Valbelluna sul Piave at the foot of the Dolomites, with the capital Mel: Venetian square between palaces from the fourteenth to the eighteenth century, archaeological museum and necropolis of ancient Venetians, the castle of Zumelle and, in Lentiai, the church with the ceiling painted by Cesare Vecellio.

Trapanese seaside resort on a sheltered bay dominated by Monte Monaco, born around the sanctuary-fortress of San Vito; from the village you can reach the lighthouse of Capo San Vito, the Secco Tonnara and the Zingaro Reserve, and at the end of September the Cous Cous Fest is held.

In the historic center, towards the end of via Garibaldi, it collects hundreds of objects of historical value donated by enthusiasts and heirs of scissors and knives of the twentieth century, together with military blades delivered by various Superintendences, including those of Marche and Lazio. A part of the museum is an active workshop where you can see master craftsmen forging the blades; visits are on reservation, at least 24 hours in advance, through the association Molise to Discover.

Built in the second half of the 16th century at the behest of the feudal lord Andrea De Capua, it is considered one of the most important examples of the bell renaissance: square plan, large portal, courtyard and double staircase towards the noble floor, with stone decorations. It hosts exhibitions and events and offers a view of the country and the countryside; you visit it by reservation (tel. 0825 991009).

The oldest church of Morano, dating back to about 1000, with interior rebuilt in late Baroque style. It contains marble statues by Pietro Bernini, father of Gian Lorenzo (1592 and 1601), the choir and the lectern carved by the Fusco workshop (1792-1805) and a processional cross in silver from 1445.
Above Valperga at about 700 meters, the sanctuary and the chapels of the Passion on an isolated granite hill, in a reserve of 349 hectares rich in rare flora. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2003.
On the opposite side of the square the Correr Museum, connected to the National Archaeological Museum.
Ticket: see the International Museum and Music Library tab

In via Balbi, the sumptuous residence of Balbi and Durazzo then purchased by the Savoys, who made it the seat of the Genoese royal family; today part of the National Museums of Genoa.
In Piazza di Pellicceria, donated to the State by Spinola in 1958; it preserves among other things the Ecce Homo by Antonello da Messina, with marbles painted in trompe-l'œil on the first floor.
The cloister and the cathedral museum, with columns and capitals richly decorated.
Inside the park, one of the sabaude residences UNESCO heritage.
